title: Pretty good spa set, but a bit on the expensive side.
text:
Overall, I'm fairly satisfied with my order of this spa set. The first thing I noticed is that everything smells fantastic! A strong coffee fragrance wafts from everything in this kit, and all three body products contain real coffee. The scrub was my personal favorite scent-wise; I find it smells just like a caramel lattee.

The body bar is nourishing and non-drying, but it is exfoliating due to the coffee grounds, so I wouldn't recommend it for everyday use. I do personally wish it was a tad larger, as it melts down quickly during typical usage.

The scrub is quite dense, as it doesn't contain added liquid. However, this means you get a lot for your money, as you only need to use a little bit on damp skin to get good exfoliation. I like the addition of almond and coconut oil, as it keeps it from being overly harsh, and makes it quite hydrating.

A little goes a long way with the bath soak. I love using it in a foot bath; It leaves my feet feeling nice and soft, and the aroma is relaxing and pleasant. It does dye the water a light brown due to the coffee, however.

I like the candle, but I'd consider it my least favorite out of this set. It has a nice burn time for its size, and it's in a beautiful black candle tin with a lid. However, I found the amount of scent it provided while burning to be underwhelming.

Overall, I really like this spa kit, and I think it'd be fantastic for any coffee lover. It's a little expensive at the current price, but if the candle was a little stronger, and the bath bar was a little larger, then this would be a five-star product.

text:
I purchased this Wahl shaver to replace a seven year old Remington of similar design who's battery finally died. Recalling an incident several years earlier -- at the airport when my carry-on bag started to make a loud buzzing noise while I was in the security line -- I thought I would give the Wahl a try since it has a Travel Lock function on the on/off button not available from Remington.

This Wahl shaver gives me as good of a shave as the Remingtons I've had in the past, and the battery life is impressive. I usually charge it once every two weeks, compared to once a week with my last Remington.

After three months of use, I did have a problem with my new Wahl - the reason for a four star rather than five star review. title: BEST TANNING LOTION EVER! NO STREAKS! FOOLPROOF!
text:
This is the best tanning lotion I have found! I love the ease of application and the color once it darkens. There are no orangy/oompa loompa undertones. A word of caution--the lotion is GREEN! I was worried I had a bad batch or something when I first opened it but it is supposed to be this way. I apply it with a black velor/velvet type mitt and I have never once had a streak. Here is the step-by-step foolproof way to get a nice, even and natural looking tan:

1. Shower and exfoliate everywhere, especially elbows, ankles, knees. I use a facial exfoliator and then I just use those exfoliator gloves for my body because if you use something with oils in it like a body scrub the lotion won't penetrate as well.
2. Dry off completely. Pull hair up/away from face. Apply regular lotion generously to feet, knees and elbows. Then start applying the tanning lotion with the mitt. I start from the legs and work my way up. Calves-->thighs/butt-->stomach/sides/what you can reach of your back-->arms-->chest-->neck-->face.
3. Run the mitt with leftover lotion on it over the tops of your feet and backs of hands.
4. Use black latex-free gloves to rub in some regular lotion over your feet/ankles until absorbed. I also apply a little regular lotion to my wrists so there is not a line. You can use the black gloves to also apply sunscreen or other face lotion if you need to.
5. Let dry completely before dressing. This lotion is awesome because it hardly rubs off on your clothes, and any that does get on clothes will wash out in the wash. Just make sure you rinse your body off (after it's been on your body for several hours and tan is set) before exercising or you'll sweat it off onto your clothes!

I have never used a better tanning lotion, and the price point is amazing!

I think the issue is that they are too flimsy to hold a large amount of hair in place if it is not already braided. I do not braid my hair, I just use beads to secure it in bunches. I use anything from a 5 mm inner diameter bead to a 17 mm inner diameter bead depending on how much hair I am attempting to secure. The Good: the overnight product was absorbed by the lips, and seemed hydrating the next morning. Will update this review after a month or so for a longer lasting impression of effectiveness.

The Bad: Avacado, almonds, apricot seed oils seemed so... natural. Except the first 4 or more ingredients are chemicals. We are still looking them up to understand what we are putting - well, make that WERE putting - on our lips.

Product seems to do what, it claims - just the chemicals are not for us. Perhaps the description should be updated and include the chemical ingredients so we consumers know what we are getting into?

text:
These brushes are actually like eight combs strung together. I had to set the extra piece that comes with each brush to separate the tines. It was not easy to get the bar across the "combs" but eventually I managed. There are only two places the bar should be put and that is where the holes are on the back of the "brush." I assembled these brushes on the lower holes. My biggest issue with these brushes is that there are only two holes to lock the bar in place when I prefer four holes like my Heeta detangling brush (product number B0836XT7J8 since the Amazon embedded links are not working).

Once this is assembled, it glides through the hair and detangles. It works well on dry hair but even better on wet hair. I love the hard tines as it is like getting a massage on the scalp. The handle provides an okay grip but I would have preferred a silicone grip. Since the combs are separated, this brush can act as a vent brush for blow drying even though it is not of circular design. Hair can be removed easily since the tines are flat with no "ball" tip.

The only reason I rated this three stars is because of the hard time I had assembling the rod in place on each one, the lack of four holes for a secure fit, and the lack of silicone grip on the handle. Otherwise they work well. The current price of $8.99 is reasonable for two detanglers.

text: This is an excellent product. It can be very very messy though, so make sure when you do get it you get it in the tube with the needle nose applicator, and not the brush on type. I use this product in making seamless tape in hair extensions.  I apply it to the hair Wefting tape before I stick the hair weft to it, and then I put another line of it on of the other side and sandwich the hair in between the two strips of tape. Then just apply heat to the tape/glue using your flat iron. It only takes a few seconds. The heat activates this Glue to make an extremely strong seamless tape in extension that does not come apart. This product is absolutely ideal for that. You can use it to create taped in hair extensions that last for multiple installs. I have tried to use this product a few times to just Glue weft extensions directly to hair, but this does not work so well even though I believe that is specifically what this product is sold for. title: Broke on first use
text:
We have a Wahl Sterling 4 clipper. It's a good clipper, but the set of guards that comes with it doesn't include a 1/2 size. The plain plastic 1/2 guard is stupidly expense for a single cheapo item, so I opted for this once, which is supposed to be nicer and more durable.

Also, my clipper just seemed to have a harder time cutting with it. It took my wife over 30 minutes to shave my head, versus the usual 15 with the size 1 guard. Even going over it dozens of time, it still feels uneven. I wear the one-length-all-over-including-beard hairstyle you might associate with Jason Statham. So I usually trim my beard with the clippers, too, to get the same length all around. And this guard did an absolutely horrible job there. (Again, my size 1 guard does just fine.)

Pros: Feels solid and looks pro. The metal clip goes on easy and holds solidly in place.

Cons: Again, broke on first use. Produced a noticeably poorer cut.

Overall, very disappointed. Expected better quality from Wahl. (And I inspected it before use, I didn't see any damage from shipping, so I think the plastic is just weak.)

title: Magnets are too weak!!
text:
Update: The top pair in the 234 was my favorite because it's the most natural looking but after 2 uses, one of the magnets fell off! This brand has quality issues. I decided to order many other brands of magnetic lashes (Newcally, LAMIX, Coolours) and I found that the magnets for the Yiwamica's lashes are considerably weaker. The other brands lashes would pop on and when pulled off would pull my skin a little. This brand's magnets do not do that. I have to press the eyelashes on and then corners would dislodge. I thought it was due to the liner but no, it's the magnets! Between the magnets falling off completely and the weak magnets, I'm downgrading from 4 to 2 stars.

As for the styles, I bought 3 sets from this listing: 230, 231, and 234. See my photo.

The 234 is a set of 3 with a natural pair, a denser natural pair same length, and a longest natural pair. The length difference is probably 1mm, very hard to tell on the tray (I didn’t measure with ruler or anything) but you can tell in person when wearing them. I think only the first pair looks truly natural on me for everyday use because I have small Asian hooded eyes. The other two in the 234 tray are sort of natural but I would not use them for day time use.

The 231 has 2 pairs that looked the same as the longest pair in the 234 set...again not natural enough for small eyes for day time use.

The 230 has crisscrossed lashes where it is longer towards the outer corners and shorter towards the inner. These lashes are longer than those in the 231 and 234.

I ended up returning 231 because it was a repeat of my least favorite pair in the 234 set.

The 230 box had quality issues. One of the lash strands was super long on one of the lashes. The 230 set was also glued to the plastic holder instead of magnetized to strips on the tray like the other two sets. When I removed the lashes from the holder, the middle magnet fell off 2 of the lashes!

I also got a eyeliner and 2 lash pair set from the same company. You can see in my photo. That eye liner turned out to be really bad so I returned that.

Instead, I use the Aroama brand of magnetic liner also sold on Amazon (the one with over 1,000 reviews) with these lashes. The magnetics in these lashes are sorta big but since I have to draw the liner really thick for them to stay at all, it’s tough to even notice the magnets. The thick liner could also contribute to the lashes not looking as natural.

I want to mention the magnet spacing is inconsistent across this brand. There are always 5 magnets but some are gapped evenly while others you get 2 magnets on each end and one in the middle with a huge gap on each side. The ends of the lashes do tend to detach from the eye easily for me as compared to the middle so the configuration with 2 magnets on the ends helps me. The spacing is purely up to your preference though. Pay attention to the product photos to see which magnet spacing you would get.

title: Love this..not just for travel
text:
I have thick, coarse, curly, dry hair. I need moisture, frizz and curl control as well as a detangler. Normally I have lots of hair in my shower after washing not to mention the tangles. I read all the reviews before trying this. Was disappointed that some said it didn't last or lather.
I just wanted something to take on my vacation for two weeks. TSA has the liquid restrictions and I was going to have to check a bag just to take enough conditioner/hair products for two weeks.
My problem has been solved. I now have a shampoo and conditioner [ as well as a leave in bar). I tried this to be certain of the results before packing. This has been a blessing. No more tangles, my curls now behave, my hair is soft and smells great but not over powering. I even used the blow dryer to speed up the drying process. I never did this before unless I would flat iron just because I would look like einstein before the flat iron... even with product!
Now I have the hair I wanted. The shampoo lathers well. Just wet your hair and the bar and lather up!
The conditioner works great. I usually use alot of conditioner just to get through my tangles. With this conditioner I just rub this bar over the front and back of my wet hair after shampooing. When done I rub a little in my palms to get a very thin/light coating then finger comb it through my hair. I have a dry scalp so I make certain tu use some on my scalp, shower then rinse.
I use the leave in conditioner the same way, but do not rinse.
I use moisturizer shampoo and alternate the next shampoo session with a frizz control bar.
Just twice a week and my hIr already feels and looks great compared to what it was.
I bought some for my friends who needed the volume control instead of the moisture and frizz. Each one loves it and saw good results. One of them has difficulties holding bottles and washing her hair, but she said the bar was much easier for her hands to use.
This is my new product! No more expensive shampoos and no more recycling bottles. I feel I am using less product than the bottles, so this is a fraction of what I was paying!
The other savings is a plus as wel.. it goes right inside my personal item.. no more worrying about checking a bag just to get 2 weeks supply of hair product!!

title: It’s okay, but not the best
text:
For the price, you get a pretty good amount. The wax heats up quickly at a high temp and it looks very pretty in the pot (has glitter in it). Unfortunately, I have yet to figure out how to work with it properly. I have used half the bag so far. It did a fantastic job with underarm hair, since the hair was a lot thicker. Sadly, for both my legs and arms it didn’t do that great of a job. It left many areas patchy with hair, seemed like it didn’t grip the hair very well no matter which direction I tried. I didn’t want to keep going over the hairs and waste wax, so I have decided to let it grow out much longer for the next use (if I have the patience and can leave a razor alone).
Another problem I have with it is that I can’t seem to find a nice temperature for it to sit at. If I keep it on 180 (which is okay for my skin with other types of wax), it’s too hot and runny. If I turn it down to 160, it gets a little too thick for me to spread on my skin. It seems like the in between would work best but it’s still just as runny and makes it hard to work with overall.
So, I wouldn’t recommend this wax to beginners or to anyone who lacks patience because it does get pretty frustrating when you have to spend hours on end waxing yourself. I wouldn’t buy this again.

title: No more plastic bottles!
text:
The number one thing I like about this product is that it does not come in a plastic bottle. It’s packaged in a recyclable cardboard box.

Upon first opening the box the scent was a little overpowering for me, very natural woody smell. I was concerned it would leave my hair smelling too strongly. But to my surprise I really liked the scent while in the shower and it did not leave a strong scent in my hair once dried. I like that you can use the bar only where extra conditioning is needed, like on the ends of the hair, and skip the scalp. It didn’t seem to be as moisturizing as some traditional liquid conditioners I’ve used, but it gets the job done and doesn’t leave a grimy feel on the hair.

What I don’t like about this product is that the first two ingredients are alcohol. Alcohol is drying. So it just seems a little counterproductive to use alcohol as the first two ingredients in a moisturizing conditioner.

Overall I do enjoy this product and I would recommend for daily use!

title: Began to fail on first use
text: I bought this hair dryer because of the review Sweethome gave it. I did check the Fakespot scores for the quality of Amazon reviews on this product and it gave it an F, but for some reason I decided to trust Sweethome more. On the first use the Peony started to intermittently make harsh grinding noises. During a "grinding attack", the heat from the Peony would decrease, the air speed would decrease (make sense if the motor or fan is grinding), but more alarmingly little white specks would start being blown from the hair dryer and a smell of burning. I suspect the white specks are pieces of the white fan being grinded off. Quality control must be lacking because I've read additional reviews on Amazon of this same issue occurring. In addition to all that, I could feel air either being pulled into the body or blown out (it's hard to tell the direction) via the small gaps between the body and the handle buttons. The nozzle pieces also got incredibly hot, so hot that they adhered to the nozzle. I had to wait for it to cool down before attempting to remove them, after which a ring was left on the nozzle where the piece had either melted to it or melted the paint on the nozzle (I think it's the latter). In summary, all problems. Even if this is a lemon, there's enough reviews on here with the same issues that the defect rate is unacceptably high. I'll be returning this one and sticking with my $20 Conair from Costco that's three years old and has never had a problem.

title: Gorgeous, But Don't Stick Well
text:
I was so happy when these arrived. The stickers looks absolutely beautiful, a first glance I fell in love. The designs and the colors were great; the colors have an iridescent quality in addition to the wide range of colors, it really adds another layer.'

Now, what disappointed me. These don't stick, like at all. There is a small amount of stickiness that lasts for mere seconds before these things fall off their surface (I've tried plastic, acrylic, skin, hardwood, and even carpeting to see). Honestly I was pretty surprised that these didn't stick to my carpet fibers. You can see in my photo that I used these for nail art, and the lifting is visible. I held the stickers down when I noticed them lifting from the nail, but after a 30 seconds of holding the sticker down (onto a top coat, too) the gorgeous little butterflies lifted anyway.

title: Cheap, but Cheaply Made.
text:
I've had these for almost a year but I haven't used them that much--there are a select few designs that I use regularly, but the majority have remained untouched. Here's why:
-A lot of my plates came damaged; maybe I'm just the unlucky one in a thousand, but many had imperfections in the metal that ruined the images. Other than that, the undamaged plates worked decently. You might run the risk of having damaged plates like me, but I'm guessing this was just my bad luck. Can't really blame the company since I never made the effort to return them, and it's been waaay past 30 days (at the time I was just happy I got them).
-I liked that there were themed and matching stamps, but to be honest I just don't like a lot of the images enough to actually use them. There is an unnecessary amount of tribal/swirly images, and what were they thinking with the ambiguous pair of chili peppers? Take a good look at the individual images and take that into account more than the sheer number of plates. Will you actually use them?
-Unless you have child's hands, the full-nail plates are waay too small--it's most noticeable on the thumbs and middle fingers, but they can barely fit over any of my nails (in terms of width, not length--I don't have crazy-long nails). To avoid awkward-looking nails, I haven't used many of the full nail stamps. Images like the polka-dots are easy to align and restamp, but others not so much.
-They come off a little blurrier than Konads, but nothing too horrible
-Some of the images are nice in theory, but don't show up that well once stamped. For example, there's a cute lace french tip that I just couldn't get to work because it was impossible to pick up the full image.

On the plus side:
-they're cheap, and most of the images are pretty crisp
-A lot of the full-nail designs have matching french tips
-The french tips will definitely (probably) fit over all your nails, including thumbs.
-I like the themed plates--for example, there's a Christmas one and a Halloween one.
-I've heard complaints that these plates were too sharp, but I don't see how you could accidentally hurt yourself with them--maybe they've updated their plate design?

Although I haven't used many of the images, those I do use make the bundle worth it. The total price for all 21 image plates--damaged and unattractive though some may be--is the price of 3 Konad stamps. It's definitely worth the price, but I can't guarantee amazing quality.

title: Not a bad set but also not fantastic
text:
In this set you get a keratin shampoo and keratin conditioner. Both of them are sulfate free which is great, however when I read the ingredients it turns out that the shampoo actually has silicone in it, not a fan of that. Thankfully the conditioner does not seem to have any in it.

So the shampoo is not bad. The scent is decent, nothing spectacular though just ok in my eyes. It produces a nice lather that rinses out easily. What I do not like is the fact that it has silicone in it.

The conditioner in my eyes is much nicer. The big problem is, the pump dispenser does not work. The conditioner is just too thick and can not be pumped up for some reason. So the suggestion of another reviewer to switch the lids is not a bad one. The conditioner smells much nicer than the shampoo and produces a very nice soft feel on your hair while still wet. It also rinses out nicely.

When your hair is dry it does look and feel very nice. So in combination your hair does look nice when you use this combination, just not sure I am a huge fan of the shampoo in this set. All in all this gets a 3 star for me since the conditioner is pretty good, the shampoo is just below average in my eyes. As a set it may be just a tad overpriced though.

title: What contouring is and isn't, and why this is a great brush to use for it
text:
In my younger days, I used to model, so I became an old hand at contouring, which seems to have been revived a la Kim Kardashian. One of my favorite brushes from then was a flat contouring brush that was angled. I absolutely adored it for adding the right shadow under my cheekbones to make them stand out.

Since the contouring revival, I decided to give this a go again, but I couldn't find a reasonably priced brush that did what I wanted it to do (I refuse to spend a fortune on a brush for this, mostly because I do not see contouring lasting very long, but that's another review.) The HDSL brush came closest to what I was looking for: dense, flat and with a good handle.

It kind of looks like a paint brush, but the hair is VERY nice. Very soft and dense, and a miracle for something that's less than six bucks. My contouring skills are such that I know not to buy an entire palette of colors that are way too orangey or warm. I use Kevyn Aucoin's contour powder which is way pricey (you can find something similar in color in Makeup Forever's eyeshadow line), but the Aucoin contour powder color was absolutely perfect.

As I'm sure you know, contour is meant to mimic a shadow. It is NOT a bronzer (you cannot contour with anything with the slightest bit of shine); too orange and you look ridiculous. The color is a light matte taupe with zero hint of red in it. It should NOT be too dark, unless you are dark complected. Think of it as being two shades darker than your skin color, the way a shadow is cast on the hollows or low areas of your face.

This brush picked up the powder like a champ and deposited it nicely. Does a great job fading the contour color out so it looks like a shadow and not like I have a swath of dirt on my face. My only hesitation with this so far is that I wish it was angled, but no matter. It's not that hard to use in such a way (well, what do you want for less than six bucks?)

title: Get lash glue instead
text:
Well, I purchased these same lashes without the dandy little tool. I had such a bad experience, but I was determined to get those little ****s on my eyes. Well, the tool was of no help whatsoever. Those little lash pieces still fell and fluttered around. I could not even find one piece until I looked in the mirror and found it on my nose. I even watched YouTube to get tips. One model put hers on, claiming that it was easy after you get the hang of it... but even her lashes did not fit next to her eyelid. There was a space of about 1/16 of an inch. She said that they look really good "from a distance". Hey Hey Hey... from a distance??? You've got to be kidding. How many of us want to stay across the room to look good??

In addition, I really don't know whose eyes they are made for. These lashes do not follow the contour of anyone's eyes who I know. Who has straight eyelids??? These lashes look like wings on your eyes. They stick fly out at the edges and I could not find any way to get them to fit the lid, short of a lot of nail glue.... that sort of defeats the purpose of them.

Now I can look back at this experience and laugh. I'm quite certain that an observer would have found it to be hilarious to watch me. At the time, I saw no humor in it. This was funny enough to be on the "I love Lucy" show. I would have loved to see Lucy and Ethel trying these out.

The concept is great.... wow!! But, it makes me wonder if the developers did these to determine the lengths that we would go to for beauty.

In closing, I even tried to get ahold of the company.... and wouldn't you know, there was no contact number on their site. Amazon was gracious enough to receive them back from me. Thank goodness for Amazon's commitment to trying to ensure that we are satisfied.

Now do you see why I procrastinated in doing this review??? I have never submitted a review as negative as this. BTW, I finally admitted to some friends my experience with these.... and they confessed that they, too, returned their magnetic lashes.

title: Quick and easy paint masking
text:
I started using this product as soon as I found it. It goes on quickly and easily. You just paint it on the area you want to protect from being painted and paint over it. Once the paint is dry, just peel it off.

I have used a couple of other masking products and I cannot really tell a difference between them. They all seem to work about the same. Since I use other products (MicroSet and MicroSol) I guess there is a bit of brand loyalty going on for me. Having said that, though, I would still use this even if I did not use the other products. It works and that's all that really matters.

One bottle of this will cover about a square foot or about 144 square inches of surface if you put it on thick. If you "stretch" it out a bit it can cover twice that. A 1oz bottle lasts me for several months. I recently did a 1/35 Tiger 2 from WW2 in Tiger Stripe camo. This took about 1/4 of the bottle for all the masking including the paint chipping.

If used imaginatively, this product can help you produce some pretty nice looking paint effects. I have used it to even protect areas from chipping effects with hairspray. I removed the mask before painting over the hairspray. When I went back to do the chipping, the area I covered with the mask came out with no chipping. So you can use it to protect the finish in "low traffic" areas of your model. Just use your imagination and his product will come through for you.

title: Works well for my husband
text:
My husband has the worst acne on his back. We have tried body washes specifically for body acne and none has worked. I saw this 808Dude Facewash for acne and said why not try it. Summer is coming and his back is a mess. I bought him a puff on a stick and gave him this dude face wash and asked him to wash his back with it and see how it works.
Some of the ingredients are natural while some are not. The ingredients are- Aqua, Aloe Barbadensis (Aloe Vera) Extract Organic, Lauryl Glucoside, Decyl Glucoside, Cocamidopropyl Betaine, Sodium Cocoyl Glutamate, Certified Organic Glycerin and Aqua and Certified Organic Eleutherococcus Senticosus (Ginseng) and Parfum, Aqua and Glycerin and Paullinia Cupana Seed Extract (Guarana) and Citric Acid and Sodium Benzoate, Hamamelis Virginiana (Witch Hazel) Extract, Chamomilla Recutita (Chamomile) Extract, Citrus Aurantium Bergamia (Bergamot) Oil, Juniperus Virginiana (Cedarwood) Bark Oil, Pogostemon Cablin (Patchouli) Oil, Citrus Grandis (Grapefruit) Peel Oil, Lavandula Angustifolia (Lavender) Oil, Pelargonium Graveolens (Geranium) Oil, Melaleuca Alternifolia (Tea Tree) Leaf Oil, Helichrysum Italicum (Immortelle) Flower Oil, Coriandrum Sativum (Coriander) Oil, Glyceryl Caprylate, Potassium Sorbate, *Limonene, *Linalool, *Geraniol, *Citral, *Citronellol, *Benzyl Cinnamate *Component of Essential Oil.
The first day he came out of the shower complaining that it smelled like Patchouli (He despises the smell of Patchouli) I didn’t smell the patchouli but looked at the ingredients and wouldn’t you know it has Patchouli in it. He kept on using it anyway though thankfully. It has been 3 weeks now and there is a difference in the acne on his back. He is still getting some breakouts, but it is NOTHING like it was before. I think after continuing to use this for a few months most of the acne on his back will be gone in time for the summer. I did purchase this 808Dude Acne Wash at a promotional price to test and write and unbiased review and I do just that.

title: Ball applicator interesting, but ineffective - leaked a lot in shipping
text:
This is one of those things where I can't really tell if it's working for a long time, so I'm not even going to comment on the benefits of the serum itself since I didn't notice any de-puffing, or improved skin tone.

When I received this, the little storage pouch was damp, which I thought was odd. I opened it, and there was a little moisture around the cap which was also sealed in plastic. Now, I live in Denver, so I'm not really sure if the leakage was caused by the the item being moved to higher elevation - we're used to that kind of thing here - but I don't really know how much of the product I lost due to leakage. I can say for sure though, that at just 10 ml for the whole bottle, I lost at least 10% of the product, and I think it's a safe guess to put it between 20-30% or more.

As for the ball roller, I found it uncomfortable to use on my eyes, so I actually just rub it on my finger tips and apply it from there. I do feel like that prevents over-usage as I've had with other Hyaluronic Acid creams which tend to go a LONG way, and can be hard to use as sparingly as is appropriate.

Bottom line - the roller ball applicator is a novelty, but I wouldn't order this one again.

title: Sonicare is the best hands down!
text:
This review is for people who are trying to decide on the Sonicare or a Braun Oral B (or ANY spin brush for that matter). My previous toothbrush was an Braun Oral B, and in my experience, the Sonicare is way superior.

First of all, the Oral B has a rotating head. Well, after several uses, I've noticed that the head starts getting loose and my lips and cheeks sometimes get pinched in the gap between the head and the neck of the brush. This causes me to have to change the brush even before it's due. Also, it seems that the Oral B allows a lot of water to enter into the metal parts that make the head spin. Therefore, while brushing, the water along with toothpaste seem to clean those parts which results in dirty water in your mouth! It's not pretty sight rinsing out your mouth and toothbrush and seeing grey water in the sink!

So after dealing with spin brushes for several years, I decided to give the Sonicare a try. Besides all the hassles of the spin type brushes, most importantly, the Sonicare cleans better. I was surprised at how well it performed since I thought the Oral B was a huge step above a manual brush. But the Sonicare makes my teeth feel even *cleaner* and I love how it makes my gums feel as well! When the Sonicare first came out in the market, I knew that there was no way the head would even fit in my small mouth (with all my wisdom teeth in tact!) so that's why I never considered it before. However, the current design of the brushes is fantastic. They are compact and angled and I have no problems reaching all my teeth. I have a feeling once you try the Sonicare, you'll never go back to any other toothbrush. It's really *that* great!

So after my initial review on this cup expressing my extreme disappointment with the so-called spill proof lid, I was contacted buy a customer representative from Gus. He expressed his apologies and they ended up refunding my total purchase price even after I told them they didn't have to and sent me a replacement lid.

It is the slider that leaks because it does not seal. I informed them of my opinion on the design, which is I believe is a poor design for what is supposed to be a spill free top.

Having said that, the Cup itself is absolutely fantastic. It's well-made and does indeed keep my coffee hot for quite a while. I have not tested it with cold yet. The way Gus stands behind their product definitely tells me that there concern is for customer satisfaction.

They were very prompt and courteous. I really can't ask any more of them. I have put the rating up to 4. If nothing else it's because of the simple fact they reached out to me to try and make it right. That to me speaks volumes of this company's commitment to ensuring their customers are happy. That's not something you see a whole lot of these days.

If they can come up with a design that makes the lid truly spill free I would definitely buy this again.

It's best to exfoliate before you use them, and to line your lips since I noticed a bit of bleeding/feathering when I used the product. Then again, the applicator is a cotton swab (so no fine control) and you get a LOT of product with it.

title: The best thing about this is the jar it comes in
text:
If you look at the photo attached you’ll see that the package has a spot that reads “Don’t be put off by the pungent odour! It’s just the strength of the Valerian Root. (It disappears when in hot water).”

I believed that message. I should not have believed that message. It smelled like old gym socks left in a locker for a year and, while the taste was not as bad as the odor (or odour, if you’re Australian) it wasn’t very pleasant either.

As a food scientist/chef I always look back at my mentor telling me “It ain’t nutrition until it passes the lips”. It doesn’t matter how healthy something is, if someone won’t eat it or drink it, it can’t do them any good. Taste matters.

Taste is subjective and you may not be offended by the taste, I was.
As for its effectiveness, I can’t really say. There is literature that backs up to some extent, the claims made and it very well may help calm you or help you get to sleep. Then again, the same can be said for a cup of warm decaffeinated tea. Perhaps this is better than that but I’m not drinking it.

The packaging is very nice, it would make a nice gift for someone who is into this type of product. The painted glass jar is nice as well (the cap is plastic).

For what this costs, they should have at least used better tea bags; asking that the bags have strings w/ tabs on them, or that they are made of a higher-grade paper, shouldn’t be too much to ask when a teabag costs more than $1.00 per.

Again, the taste is subjective, you may like the flavor or, at least, not find it offensive as I did.

My daughter was looking for inexpensive brushes to replace her old ones. They arrived in a multi chrome (purple to blue shift) fake leather, which has 10 slots in a few sizes. The ‘gems’ are little plastic diamond shaped pieces in two colors (depending on the color you chose), and they are small enough so they aren’t uncomfortable when you are holding them and they provide a better grip for accurate use. The one problem she has with the diamonds is that they are held onto the brush with what my daughter could only describe as a piece of double sided tape. There hasn’t been an issue with the diamonds falling out, but I surprised if they eventually did. The rose gold metal on either end is a nice touch and it doesn’t clash. The brush ends are quite dense (depending on what brush you’re using) so it picks up product well and doesn’t suck up too much foundation and concealer. Overall, I’d say it’s a great product for the price.

title: First (almost) electric razor
text:
Just had my first shave with this. I've used two electric razors in my life. One was an already ancient one that my dad had, about 40 years ago. Ripped each of the few hairs in my face out one by one. Then an early Norelco 3-head circular job, about 30 years ago that either sucked or I didn't know how to use. Very even stubble was the result of that. Hence my refusal to try one until my memories have faded.

This review reflects one shave - not a long term review.

I'm impressed. It's slower than I expected, I half-thought I could activate an app on my phone or something and I would be shaved (I'm joking!). It's pretty darn close to a manual 5-blade fresh razor.

Here are the conditions under which I'm reporting:
- I'm 62, so my skin isn't exactly taut on my face.
- Not a heavy beard, I need to shave every day now, but not until I was about 35.
- This shave was with 2 days of stubble.
- I usually shave in the shower, using Braille to tell when a patch is smooth.

I used the razor dry. The manual said to charge the razor before first use, but it came out of the box showing 100% charge so I went for it. The manual also says not to apply too much pressure, so I was tentative at first. It helps to apply fair pressure while moving the razor SLOWLY through that fungus that seems to grow constantly on our faces.

Stretching my skin with other-handed fingers in most spots helped. I used a mirror just to watch the progress, but you can use your sonic sensors, AKA ears, to tell when the blades are and aren't removing stubble. I don't think a mirror is at all necessary, YMMV.

While I've been writing this, I've used Braille again to check on the usual trouble spots - I can just grab the mower and run it over the rough bits while I'm doing this. You could do this easily while driving somewhere - no risk of a small knick, and the aural attention that it takes doesn't really distract from driving.

I didn't notice when I ordered this razor that it came with an extra foil. Nice detail, since the foil is easy to damage being thin (as it should be). The kit comes with a carrying bag, which is nice to keep everything together while traveling. I would find a small rigid container for the extra foil if I were to travel with that - it could easily get bent in the carrying bag knocking around with all the bits. The foil is too long for the old canisters from film cameras, but a cut-off from a roll of Xmas paper would suffice.

The grip is comfortable and makes the shaving head easy to maneuver. The carrying bag contains everything in a small package - I'm a Cardinal (Archbishops and above don't shave) in the Church of Small Luggage and I will happily carry this instead of a couple of manual razors on any trip.

Finally (applause erupts from the crowd), very nearly close shave as a manual razor, a little slower than a manual razor, works very well dry (absolutely unlike a manual razor, though I've tried that also and it does sort of work).

Buy it. Try it.

I have used Norelco for 18 years now. I have purchased three other shavers thru the years. This time, I wanted to try the latest to see if the coverage and close shave is any better.

I noticed the head is lighter, probably because you can rinse the head in water; therefore, most parts are plastic. I did not expect the rinse indicator to light up each time I use it.

The closeness setting has three modes. My previous model had 9. It did not matter; I use the closes setting all the time.

The head has more coverage; however, I think the multi opening is too complex (holds and line opening to cut closer). I find that parts of my chin/throat area has a few strands that are difficult to cut. I tried different angles and push even harder to the face and it does not work well. I had to use the trimmer to trim down the few.

I was tempted to return it since it has a 60 days money back. My old one is "DEAD" does not charge nor does it work with outlet (7 yrs). So I decided to push forward with this model. Maybe this one will last me just as long as the previous model.

Tom (NYC)

title: READ THE REVIEWS FOR CLEAR INSTRUCTIONS!!!
text:
First, I suggest to do one eye at a time even though it takes longer. You’ll be doing yourself a favor.

1. I would cut the lift pad to your eye size, it makes working with it much easier. Visualize how and where you want your lashes to curl and place it accordingly. I wanted mine to flare out a bit so I put mine a little further away from my inner corner so that my lashes on the outer corner had space on the pad.

2. I used the Tarte Micellar Water to cleanse my eyelashes. The glue it comes with is awful and weak. You can actually use any eyelash glue to glue down your lashes. I used the House of Lashes glue. I used this glue to apply the pads onto my eyelid. You can use the glue however way you need to to keep your lashes down. I used a spoolie to push the lashes against the pad and held it there for a few seconds then I used the Y tool to separate them. BE GENTLE AND SWIFT. If you’re too rough you might rip your eyelashes off and the longer the glue sits the harder it will be to separate the lashes.

3. When I was satisfied with the eyelash separation I applied the perm lotion. ONLY PUT THE PERM LOTION ON THE BASE OF THE EYELASHES. From the very bottom to the middle where you want it to curl. If you apply it to the whole eyelash, your adhesive will loosen and your lashes will start coming off the pad. I used a Q-tip to apply this. Also I place a small piece of cling wrap on top of my eyelashes after applying the perm lotion to further secure my lashes from coming off.

4. After 20 minutes, I delicately removed the cling wrap, I used another Q-tip to apply the fixation lotion. This is thicker than the perm and should be applied to the whole lash. But still be very careful and gently apply it. I placed another small piece of cling wrap on top of my lashes to secure my eyelashes in place again.

5. After 20 minutes, I gently removed the cling wrap and used another Q-tip to apply the nutrition oil to my lashes. Then I used another Q-tip to apply the cleanser that comes with the box onto my lashes. Gently free your lashes from the pad. I used the Tarte Micellar Water to remove the rest of the glue. I dipped my spoolie into the Micellar water and combed my lashes through them to get any more remaining glue off.

These work very well for my application. My orthopedic surgeon recommended I buy shoes with heels to counter a problem I have flexing my foot upwards at the front. They don't exactly conform to the shape of my shoe heel, but they work fine. They are easily attached using the nails provided and Shoe Goo, or similar adhesive. I used two G-clamps to hold them while the glue set. Several pairs of these heels have now stayed firmly attached and outlasted the shoes.

title: Just OK
text:
I have used Norelco shavers for many years and prefer them to all other models I have tried. This review comes from much experience with the brand.

This Arcitec design looks fancy and works well, but gets three average stars because it really works no better than the previous non-space-age, less expensive designs. The 1050, 1060, and 1090 all operate the same, they just have a different display: none is better than the other, and don't waste money on the Cleaner accessory. It is fairly comfortable to hold (I prefer the feel of the original model because this is one is smaller), and looks fancy sitting on the counter, but it does not do a better job. It requires cleaning after each use as there is no space for the hairs. I have always cleaned my shavers after each use anyway. Unless you just want the apperance, it is not worth the extra money.

Technically: The triple-blade per round head (each cutter has three spinning blade areas) does not do any better than a double cutting blade. Kind of like a Saturday Night Live skit in the 70's, Jim Belushi said, "Buy a triple bladed razor. For those that will believe anything". Lift-and-cut is a ridiculous concept and a marketing ploy, but Norelco's do a nice job. Norelco went back to more diagonal openings with this model, which is good. Many other newer models have lots of little pin-holes which are worthless, as the hairs have no time to enter a small hole with shaving motion. You would have to set it directly on a hair to cut it. The less pin-holes the better.

Feel: The head design feels better on the neck, and has not caused razor-burn if I do not stretch the skin tight like I need to with the original model. It takes the same time to shave as my older unit, and I get no better results, no faster. It takes the same time to get a smooth shave, and the same persistance in some areas.

Function: It is a little bit easier to shave under the nose, above my mustache, but not a major difference. It is much harder to trim my sideburns with this unit as the heads almost cut my hair on my head above the ears the way it is shaped. Very poorly designed trimmer, so I use my older shaver for that.

Battery: Early, new battery life is good, as with most new battery devices. But, it states to not over-charge. Meaning, you need to be around when recharging to unplug it after it is charged; not good for those that shave and must go to work. The other units would shut off after charging.

Cleaner/Charger: Again, one needs to be around when it is finished to not over-charge. The cleaner is not necessary and a waste of time, money, and chemicals. I use a razor brush from an older unit, brush it out quickly over the wastebasket (one can't blow it out without getting hair dust all over the bathroom, and it can't be shaken into the wastebasket as easily as the older models), and I spray it quickly with Remington Silicone Lubricant (I can only find it at Wal-Mart, which is the only thing I ever go there for, by the way).

Overall: Buy it for looks and keep your old one in the drawer for sideburns. Nicer on the neck.

I would return it, BUT, it was a gift, AND I like the look of it. I know, I know!!

Update 12-29-07
I purchased a Braun 9595 through J&R on Amazon, and it has a 60 day trial return guarantee. This is the first micro-screen razor I have used and it is better in all respects to the Norelco Arcitec except for the fancy styling. It is fast and comfortable, and my face feels razor smooth. I was able to return the Arcitec and am really happy with this Braun 9595 model.

title: Fantastic first electric toothbrush for the money!
text:
After being scolded by the dentist one-too-many times that I wasn't brushing in circular motions and that I haven't been giving my wisdom teeth enough attention, I recently decided to jump onto the electric toothbrush bandwagon, but at the same time, I had no desire to spend half a truck payment on one with "sonic" cleaning or five-way floss/torture heads. Over the past month, I've found that this Oral-B Vitality, which is actually manufactured by Braun and bears a small Braun logo, cannot be beat for the money! It does just what I need it to, has a nifty compact recharging station with no exposed metal contacts, and my mouth hasn't ever felt cleaner.

The only two very minor cons that I think people should be aware of are related to battery life and the two-minute timer. It's probably true that the battery will last 20 minutes between charges, but I've found in daily use that if I don't hang it back on the recharging station after every other use, the bristles spin a bit slower than they do when the battery is fully charged. Not a huge deal, but my time is precious in the morning and I want maximum RPMs, so I prefer not to completely empty the battery beyond the manufacturer's recommendation to do so periodically. Also, I can see the two-minute timer being great for those who have a bad habit of not brushing long enough, but I find personally that I typically brush for about 2-1/2 minutes, even if I'm trying to rush, so it would be nice to have a way to turn the two-minute timer off. The timer isn't a light or a beep, but rather the toothbrush "revs" its engine down and back up a few times once two minutes have elapsed, which makes brushing ineffective over the course of those one to two seconds of revving and thus again wastes precious seconds. Again, not a huge deal, but a way to turn it off would be nice. Otherwise, this toothbrush can't be beat!

title: Removed red after dyeing my hair for 10+ years
text:
**Edit - Update - it's been a week, and the red that had previously lightened to strawberry blonde is now returning in full force. I'm so disappointed. While it wasn't too horrible on my hair, I hesitate to try it a third time and risk major damage for a product that clearly isn't all I thought it would be. I am sad to reduce this from 5 stars down to 2, since it did reduce the color slightly.

It's important to note that I didn't bleach my hair at any time, so my base is all grey. My intention was to remove the red, and eventually lighten my hair down to the grey and stop coloring for good. I used the product twice, one day leaving it in for the 20 minutes, then washing with a clarifying shampoo, followed by a 20 volume developer diluted 1:1 with water as this product recommended on the box. Honestly, my hair darkened after the developer, so when I used the product again the next morning, I repeated all the steps minus the developer, then followed the instructions for a purple shampoo. I also have a good quality hair mask, and Olaplex No. 6 & 7 products to help minimize the damage. My biggest fear was being left with a hideous orange color, or a bright sun yellow, which didn't happen. I'm pretty happy with the results, since I have heard how hard it is to get red out. The smell isn't nearly as bad as some of the reviews made it out to be, and the product was very easy to use. I did wrap my hair in plastic wrap, and tried to keep it warm with a towel to improve the results. I may give it another go just to get closer to the grey, but I'm going to give it some time so I don't damage my hair. Definitely glad I went this route instead of something that may have damaged my hair.

title: NOT A SKINCARE GIMMICK GIVES AMAZING RESULTS
text:
My first thought was that this was another gimmick but being a skincare junkie had to try it. I'm so glad that I did as it exceeded my expectations to the point that I've overlooked a few things I'd normally dock it on.

First use: My usual routine is to wash my makeup off and immediately apply HA [Hyaluronic acid] to relieve the resulting dry tight feeling. I filled this sprayer with HA serum and at first, didn't feel anything but cool air hitting my face and wondered if any serum was even coming out. Then suddenly the tightness was gone and my face felt like it was covered with a moisture mask. When applying HA with my fingers it always took a minute or two to soak in, not so with this sprayer the results were immediate! Although the Nano mist is so fine its impossible to see, the end results is an amazing feeling of soft fully moisturized skin.

With this sprayer you can chose to use serums, toners or water so your not limited to only water like other Nano sprayers. This sprayer is well made and the USB cord is included, the liquid chamber is small [perhaps two tablespoon capacity] easy to fill and it only used a tiny amount of serum to cover my face and neck.

The only Cons are the USB port's location on the bottom so it must be laid on its side to charge {that's weird} and the instruction booklet could use a little help. But, as stated at the beginning of this review I'm so impressed with how my skin feels I'm forgiving the aforementioned transgressions and giving this a 5 star rating.

Honestly, I don't normally get excited about skin care tools but this one is an exception and its made me a Nano spray believer. Highly recommend.

I hope you find this review helpful.

title: Excellent qualtiy aventurine/jade stones. Quality craftsmanship.
text:
The aventurine/jade in the massage roller and gua sha differ in terms of coloration. However, it does not detract from the overall quality and attractiveness of the set. The presentation further lifts the value as a gifting option.
The gua sha has a nice thickness, and has a good degree of polishing. This creates a shiny and very smooth surface. The contour has smooth rounding, with clean lines. Inspection of the heart shaped gua sha found no defects or flaws. Happily, there are not scratches or nicks to be found on the aventurine gua sha.
The massage roller has features associated with premium level products. It has the metal collar/ring on the metal axle/arm where it meets the stone roller. This is a nice aesthetic touch.
An important aspect, which isn't a cosmetic affect, is the plastic grommet that acts as a bearing between the metal arm/axle and the stone rollers. This plastic piece facilitates a quiet and smooth rolling action; without this grommet, there's a good possibility of noticeable squeaking and a 'rough' rolling motion. Of equal import, the grommet protects the aventurine and the metal arm from direct contact, and avoids erosion of both parts.
The set matches the description and images in the product details. I appreciate that the company is upfront about the stone being aventurine (it is often called Autralian or Indian Jade, due to the appearance, but is actually part of the quartz family). Many companies use the jade classification to enhance the credentials of the product. It's not deceptive or misleading. Anyway, glad to see the company provide an honest account of the materials.
Attached are photos to show real world images, with a ruler for size reference.
Based on the quality and initial impressions, this massage roller and gua sha set earns a 4.5 - 4.75 star rating, with a high level recommendation.

I've never owned an electric toothbrush before and was hesitant to spend so much money on a toothbrush. I've been having problems with my gums and I have very, very sensitive teeth and I knew I needed to do MORE to take better care of my teeth and gums. I bought this toothbrush a week ago and I can already feel the difference in how my gums feel and how clean my teeth feel.

My gums are bleeding, but my understanding is that this is normal in the first week or so of using this toothbrush (my gums were bleeding before).

I spend most of my time in undeveloped countries and do not have access to good dental care. I believe this is one of the better ways for me to take the best care of my teeth as is possible and I only wish I would have bought it many years ago.

The only negative I see is that I bought this one in the U.S. (where I'm staying for a few weeks) without paying attention to the voltage when I made the purchase. I don't think I can use this same one outside of 110v countries.

title: Temporary fix, best for women that wear make-up
text:
Listen up, especially my fellow dudes that want to roll back the clock a bit. This is an expensive parlor trick to hide wrinkles as well as bags under your eyes. The substance temporarily tightens your skin with a film that is lightly colored with a Caucasian base make up (at least mine is; maybe they have other shades -- I am in fact a Caucasian male). If you touch it after it dries it will break the seal and you will lose the effect. It only lasts until you wash again or rub the area. I doubt you'd get a full day out of an application.

I feel foolish for getting suckered into this expensive product as I was told it would be possible to drop back to weekly for 4 months then put the rest in a freezer for a few years - LOL!

If I were a woman that wore a good *spray-based* makeup product over top of it I might think it is worth the money. As a man that doesn't wear make-up, even though the skin tone is close to my own, I think you can easily see I am wearing some sort of cosmetic product.

I will probably only use this for web meetings and special occasions and then not buy again.

title: Good brush for a squeaky clean feel... but get a simpler one.
text:
This is my first electric powered toothbrush so I was not sure what to expect. It takes a lot longer than 2 minutes (around 5 minutes or more) for me to brush properly with this brush and cover all tooth surfaces. When I am done, my teeth do feel "squeaky clean", a feeling that would require a ton more brushing with regular non-electric brushes. I don't like the automatic indicator feature on this brush that indicates when to stop brushing a particular side and switch to the other side. The brush actually stops spinning for a second and it feels like an interruption to me. I am almost NEVER done when the indicator comes on to give the signal for a switch.

Brushing with the electric brush is MESSY - way more messy than brushing with a regular brush. A number of other reviewers have complained about the difficult cleaning of this brush. I have no such issues. I simply take the whole brush head part off the brush base and rinse both the brush head and the metal base that holds the brush head in the water before leaving them on my bathroom counter to dry. Recharging takes an entire day but when fully charged, I can use the brush for nearly a week (once a day) before the red-light-indicator for recharging comes on.

title: ouch! I felt like the bride of frankenstein
text:
I bought this direct from an advertisement on amazon. Everything about this package was stylish, beautifully presented and arrived quickly in perfect order. The DVD was excellent and there were clear simple instructions on a sturdy pamphlet. The included conductive gel and Serum with peptides were pleasant to use and fragrance free.

On page 12 of the manual "precautions" "headache and other painful sensations have been reported during or following electrical stimulation" was omitted from the website.

It was very unpleasant during use; causes visible twitching and muscle contraction. Even on the lowest setting I found this frankly painful especially in the jaw. My muscles felt tightened alright afterwards but to the point of face ache and a headache. My eyebrows were so lifted on one side it was a bride of frankenstein look. I think this unit needs a redesign to lower the current again by half rather than chasing quick results. Decreasing the time of application by half didn't help much - the overall sensation was still of having been kicked in the head rather than of having had a facial. I didn't want to use it more than twice before asking for the company to honour its 100% satisfaction guarantee and issue a refund number which they did.

If the website upfront about the level discomfort I might have left another star on this for other users who are probably not as sensitive. My advice is don't buy it unless you can try it first. Very disappointed as I wanted this unit to work in tandem with my [[ASIN:B000JIN0OG NuFace Microcurrent Toner for Lifting and Toning the Face]] - which leaves me feeling relaxed and fabulous but can't be used around the mouth or eye area.

here is the response:
"Your FaceMaster passes less power to your skin than a good static discharge might on a dry day after walking on some carpet (less than 20 microamps at intensity level = 1, less than 200microamps at intensity level = 10). There is no possibility of nerve damage.

We recommend that you try a couple of techniques:

1. Use a bit less conductive serum (a perfectly dry foam cap will not conduct any electricity, while a completely soaked foam cap allows almost 100% of the current to pass). Using less conductive serum should be similar to having intensity settings below level 1.

2. Use less pressure on your wands. No current will pass to your skin if the wands are not touching it; likewise the most current would pass if you press hard enough such that 100% of the foam caps were surrounded by skin. Using less pressure to reduce the surface area of contact is also like having intensity settings below level 1.

The sensation caused by the e-stim is something that you will become accustomed to. In fact, it is possible with prolonged use that the sensation will be eliminated completely (we receive comments from people saying their FaceMaster is no longer working because they no longer feel it - it is just that they have become use to it).

Feathering mode has a significantly different output characteristic than Eye or Face mode. The treatment is meant to stimulate collagen and elastin within the skin and will not provide any muscle stimulation."

I don't feel like toughing it out as a professional session is completely painless there is an easy alternative.

title: Super hydrating
text:
I bought this mainly because it contains peptides and those are something I dont have in the rest of my skincare routine. The eye area is very delicate to begin with and as we age, the skin thins out along with the fat. This has been by far my biggest aging issue. :( I dont know why Ive been having such a hard time but around 21 the skin started thinning out rapidly. It may have been from being on doxycycline. Anyways, peptides help thicken the skin over time. It wont restore the fat loss but it can combat the thinning skin issue.

Nupeptin Restoring Eye Zone cream is PACKED with beneficial, anti-aging ingredients. I see various proteins, extracts, antioxidants, ceramides, and other natural sourced ingredients. This is a very thick eye cream and suuuuper hydrating. I like how plump and supple my undereye area looks while wearing this. You can tell by the ingredient list that it is very nourishing. Upon application, you can even tell by the consistency.

It takes a while for peptides to give full results. But the results are long term. Since peptides work similar to chemical exfoliators i would advise to wear a sunscreen while using this product. Also for best results, dont combine it with other actives (IE alpha hydroxy acids). The supple and plump effect should be immediate though! I am so pleased with this product. Its better than a lot of $$$$$$ ones ive bought.

title: Not an Effective Hair Management Product
text:
In my opinion - a good hair management product would remove hair for about 1 month before it would begin to grow back, it would be reasonably priced, relatively easy to use, would work on all hair types without irritation(or cuts), and would require less than 20 minutes of your time.

This product did not meet any of the above criteria(unfortunately) - for me.

Some history - for about the past 5 years I have searched for the ideal solution to my hair problem. I tried "Nair for Men" - disappointed and irritated. I tried regular "Nair" - result was only slightly better. Later I tried "Veet" for women(which I am not), and left it on for about 10 minutes, the results were passable but not perfect. And the results did not last, 1 week later and the hair was growing back. I also tried using an old electric shaver which I no longer used on my face, I had to use the trimmer on it to cut down the hair to shaving size, not an easy task with my long thick dark brown hair. I was not satisfied with the result using the electric shaver. It should be noted that I was using these products for the "lower" region where they should not be used, but I have no need for hairless legs or chest, hair here (mostly) does not bother me(although I believe hair below the neck no longer serves a purpose, other than to become sweaty, smelly, and itchy).

So I decided to try "ballsBALM". The 1st thing I noticed - the small size of the tubes. If I wanted to remove all the hair on my body I would need more than 1 of these(more like 5 or 6). Although all I wanted/needed was to remove the hair around the "groin" and lower back.

After applying a thick layer and waiting more than 10 minutes I tried wiping it off with a towel or "washcloth" or whatever you want to call it. Very little hair actually came off. In the back of my mind I kind of knew this was not going to work, with "Veet" I had to use a special "scraper" to remove the hair(I tried it on my 2nd try). Using a wet sponge more hair came off than with the towel. I re-applied another layer of "Bare Balm" cream and then after waiting for more than 15 minutes and using the "scraper" I had used with "Veet" a significant amount of hair actually came off, although not entirely(the roots of the hair were still left in the skin - like with other similar products). It was not a perfect result, and I did not even bother trying it on my back(I did not want to spend another half hour in the bathroom). To get to this point I believe I used about 40-50% of the tube. In 2 weeks I was back to square 1.

The smell of the product did not bother me(no lasting cucumber smell), but I did not find it to be better when compared to similar store bought products(which are not perfect either).

title: Nice Facial Cleaning Brush Offers Four Diverse Brush Heads but Only One Speed Option
text:
I'm very interested in trying new beauty products to pamper myself, and I have some dry skin on my face that I'm always struggling to keep in check, so it sounded appealing to give this waterproof facial brush cleaning system a try to compare and contrast to other similar products I own.

This skin cleansing kit comes with one waterproof and cordless rotating machine, one facial brush, one large body brush, one serum and moisturizer applicator sponge, and one pumice stone. This machine requires four AA batteries to run, which aren't included.

The brushes feel pleasant to the touch, and I liked that four different attachment heads were included. They are soft, but have just enough pressure to them to feel like they will exfoliate dirt, oil, and dead skin well. The set-up for this cleaning system is simple and straightforward, but I found it quite difficult to open the battery compartment on the end of the handle.

Once the batteries were inserted successfully and the battery compartment was snapped back into place, all that I needed to do was to pick a brush head and push it in to the attachment point. Then you can turn the unit on or off by pressing one of two buttons on the blue section of the brush. In my experience with the brushes, they didn't rotate evenly, and the brushes wobbled as they rotated. I'm not sure if this is an intended feature or not, but I'm suspecting it simply means the platforms for the brushes aren't quite even.

I'm glad that this cleaning system is waterproof, but I'll admit I was a bit underwhelmed that it only has one speed, and that that speed is rather slow. I still feel like I will get some good use out of it, but I would have liked if there were more speed options, because for attachments like the pumice stone, you really need a slightly faster speed for it to perform really well.

That said, I was generally pleased with the accessories offered in the kit, but would have liked if they included a small storage or travel bag of some kind.

Overall, I like this waterproof electric facial brush, and would recommend it if you're considering adding one to your own health and beauty routine. Just keep in mind it has only one slow speed, and that you will need to provide your own storage bag and batteries.

I am a longtime Amazon Prime customer who writes reviews in my free time. I was appreciative to be given an opportunity to test and review this waterproof facial brush cleaning brush complimentary for my honest and unbiased review. If you have any questions or comments about this product or my review, feel free to message me and I'll be glad to help!

title: Proceed With Extreme Caution
text:
I'm really torn on this review. If I could give it 2.5 stars, I would. It does have a considerable pro or two, but it also is laden with a lot of items in the "cons" column. So first, the good stuff: SugarBaby delivers on its promise to provide a dark bronze tan. The color is deep and natural looking and develops quickly. Another unexpected pro with this product is that I found the "guide" to be a pretty color once it dried and settled, so if it was necessary to go out after tanning you wouldn't have the odd color found in some products' guides. Of course, the guide in itself is a pro also, as it always helps to be able to tell if you've missed a spot, gotten it streaky, where you left off, etc. The color also lasted a fair amount of time (6 days or so.)

Now to the cons. I had to apply the mousse with latex gloves (the result of a defective tanning mitt) and eventually the help of my husband. I was absolutely exhausted once I finished tanning the parts I could reach, and he finished my back and arms. Although it was a tremendous pain, it looked good and looked even. After 30 minutes, I still couldn't get dressed in even a loose robe because a few areas felt tacky to the touch. It was almost an hour before I felt sort of dry. I eventually put on very loose pajamas pants and a long sleeve t-shirt; 5 hours later I went to bed. In the morning, there was tanner on my duvet cover, sheets, and inside my clothes.

So, Pros: Good color, lasts fairly well
Cons: Backbreaking to apply, long drying time, color transfer onto fabrics

Reserve this one for when you don't mind the extra trouble to get really dark.
Tip: Apply it 1st thing a day around the house, wear baggy clothes, and as late at night as you can, shower off the guide. You'll have given yourself the 8-10 hours your tan needs to develop (and then some), plus you'll save your sheets AND wake up smelling DHA free. :)

[[VIDEOID:e6424147f4b4136bd53f39eb82f6fc17]] Pros:
Decent construction.
Cleans itself of fur pretty darn fast/easy.
Cover for the bristles is nice.
Removes some shed and combs hair.

Cons:
Packaging is cheap, half clamshell stapled to a cardboard backing. This isn't a big deal but it did result in the packaging being fairly mangled (like it had been tossed around at a pet store for way too long) and would look embarrassing if you purchased it as a gift. (This did not affect my score though, as it's just packaging)
So much retail space, probably 1/3 of which has no brush.
Bristles looked bent/misaligned right out of the package. Again kind of feels like maybe it was used (it looks super clean, but between the bent bristles and the mangled/stapled packaging I gotta wonder)
Doesn't feel like it's REALLY effective at thinning out the shedding fur. (it took quite a bit of brushing to get that wad in the video, and he's a 13-15lbs ginger-chonk.) With how hot it's been I was expecting a lot more shed out of him. Maybe he cleans himself really well and I don't realize it.

Verdict:
It's an adequate brush. The solid brush cover is great and the ease at which it cleans itself with the pull of the trigger is amazing. I do wish the brush head were a little smaller or there were more bristles covering all that brush head. Just feels like a waste. I'd also invest in better packaging and quality control (if that's really how the bristles come from the factory).

If you need a brush this will suffice (at least for short haired cats, I cannot attest for dogs or long haired cats.) Probably wouldn't be my first choice though.

title: Very finely milled! Doesn’t look like have powder on!
text:
Overall, I think this is a great powder! I love how finely milled it is! It’s so soft and velvety on the skin! It doesn’t look like I have powder on, but sets my makeup in place. It looks and feels nice on the skin. You get a good amount of product. I’m really happy with it! The only thing I don’t like is how hard the lid is to twist initially. I also don’t like the product page talking about natural ingredients - baichi flower seed oil and jojoba seed oil - being in the powder and that not being on the ingredient list. So, I took a star off for that. But, other than that, I recommend this powder. If like me, you don’t usually like powders and the only ones you do like are finely milled, you’ll love this powder! If you’ve had trouble finding powders that work for you. If they tend to make your skin look dry, powdery, or cakey. I recommend trying this one out!

This comes in an outer product box. It is made in China. It has a cruelty free logo (PETA). The ingredients are listed on the back. It includes mica and parabens.

It’s odd because the product page states that it’s made of “natural safe ingredients” and has “baichi flower seed oil water-oil balance, long-lasting makeup” and “jojoba seed oil moisturize the skin,” but neither of those ingredients are found in the ingredient list on the back of the product box. So, I don’t understand where that comes from? I hate when there’s what seems like blatantly false claims on a product page. It makes me not trust anything from the brand.

The jar of powder is square. It’s a good size. It is plastic. The bottom is clear but frosted and matte. The top has the same design as the front of the box. It has a nice look to it.

I hate to say it, but how to get the top off had me a little confused at first 🙈 I initially thought it would twist off, but when I went to twist it, it didn’t seem to want to move. Then, I thought, well since it’s square, maybe it will pull off. So, I carefully tried to pull the top off, but it didn’t want to budge. Then, I tried twisting it again, this time really putting effort into it and it finally moved and I got it off. At first it seemed like it only went halfway, but wouldn’t twist any more (again, I was being careful because I didn’t want powder getting everywhere). Then, I just lifted it up and it came off. I thought after the first time it would be easier to get the top off, but it wasn’t. You still really need to put some elbow grease into it every single time, which is annoying. If you have trouble with things like that, this might not be the powder for you. There was a clear sticker covering the holes, which I always appreciate! So, had I yanked the top off, Powder wouldn’t have gotten everywhere! But, you never know since some brands don’t do that! But, I’m glad this one did!

Another thing, I kind of wish the part with the holes, where the powder is, I wish it was square like the jar. I always dump powder into the lid and dip my brush into that. Then, whatever powder I have left, I dump back into the jar. Usually, I can just take the cap with the leftover powder and carefully put it on and the powder will fall into the main part. With this, if I do that the powder gets down on the edges of the jar (see photos), so I always have to make sure to carefully dump the powder back in before putting the lid on.

I had a hard time deciding which shade I wanted to get. Usually, I go with translucent. But, sometimes I like a little extra coverage from a skin toned powder. But, this powder had an option for a pink powder, and I always heard pink was good for brightening, so then I thought about that one! The descriptions on the middle of the product page didn’t really help. For #1, “Ivory White,” it said, “Suitable for fair skin. Create white makeup.” I was initially thinking this one was translucent, until I read the description. I’m fair skinned, but I don’t know what they mean by white makeup. But, it seemed like it was going to have a white tint to it, which I didn’t want. For #2, “Natural Color” they had, “Suitable for any race. Create light makeup.” If it’s “suitable for any race” that would imply it’s translucent, but it didn’t look translucent. It looked like a fair skin toned color. For #3, “Soft Pink,” it had, “Suitable for pink skin. Create a glossy, ruddy makeup.” I have fair skin and I’m cool toned, so pink skin makes sense. Glossy doesn’t seem too bad, but I’m not sure what they meant by that. Do they mean it’s going to give a glow? And who wants ruddy makeup? See how confused I was! 🤦‍♀️

I thought I ended up going with #2 “Natural Color,” and the box mine came in had “#2” on the top flap, but when I looked at the color of the powder through the frosted clear bottom it looked soft pink. When I first dumped some out into the lid it looked soft pink. But, when I swatched it, it seemed more of a fair skin toned color. So, I THINK I got the right shade (#2 Natural Color). It definitely works for my fair skin. But, I don’t see how this would be “suitable for any race.” To me, it seems like it blends out MOSTLY transparent. But, it does seem like there might be a HINT of fair shade/white to it, so I’m not sure if it will work for medium to darker skin tones.

The powder is very finely milled. It has almost a velvety feel when you touch it. I am 35, have normal to dry skin with some extremely dry areas, and suffer from hormonal acne. In my experience, most powders make my skin look dry or powdery or cakey, so I only like using powder in specific places where I absolutely need it. Even then, there’s only a handful of powders I like for that purpose that look good on my skin. This has become one of those! Out of the handful of powders I like on my skin, the one thing they all have in common is that they are all VERY finely milled. I find that the more fine the powder is, the less it looks like you have powder on your face. It just sets my makeup in place in my oily areas without making it look dry/powdery/cakey.

title: I liked the idea better than the product
text:
With four cats and a large dog, I am always looking for good grooming tools. I liked the idea of this brush, but the actual product really wasn't all that. First of all, this thing is much larger than any other slicker style brush I have. This is a great feature for my large dog, but it was just ridiculous trying to groom my cats with this large, unyielding wire brush. So, not a good choice for the cats.

Unfortunately, not a good choice for my dog either, as she has a short coat with little to no undercoat and she was really uncomfortable with wires dragging on her skin. She's more of a rubber curry comb type gal, I guess. Besides the size and wire bristle problems, the plastic itself felt a little brittle and cheap and when you add in the mechanics of retractable bristles... I think higher quality material would have been a better choice because that slider for the bristles is very basic. Finally, while I loved the idea of the easy-to-clean retractable bristles, they really aren't necessary and if those wires become crooked or bent it will cause all kinds of problems with the retraction. I've made it decades by just pulling the fur out of my slicker brushes-- it literally takes 2-3 seconds-- and while the thought of retractable bristles is nice, it totally isn't necessary. It's not a practical tool for me and doesn't work for any of my animals due to its size and the wire bristles. It also doesn't seem terribly well-made nor is it made of high-quality materials, and for the price it should be.
