title: 2 of 3 have micro glitter (mica). Sticky but not too bad. Moisturizing
text:
These come in a nice little box. They are vegan and cruelty free. They are made in the USA. I included the ingredients at the end of my review.

You get 3 glosses - a peachy pink toned one that has a strawberry scent/flavor, a more reddish toned one that has a grape scent/flavor, and a clear one that has a bubble gum scent/flavor. As for the scents, I can notice them when applying, not so much after the fact. I don’t really notice a taste really with any of them, but the ingredients do list “flavor” not fragrance/parfum, so it made me think they’d have more taste to them. Not a big deal to me though.

While 2 of them are tinted in color, the color doesn’t really translate onto the lips. They just look clear on the lips. They don’t change any color of lip liner, lipstick, matte lip, etc. that I put them over top of. So, I liked that.

The formula is nice. It feels nice and moisturizing on the lips, which I expected given they have nice moisturizing ingredients like Shea butter, coconut oil, and squalane. They do feel SLIGHTLY sticky on the lips. I hate sticky glosses, but these aren’t overly sticky. They don’t feel thick or heavy on the lips. They feel nice and thin. They are glosses so they do need re-applied often throughout the day. But, I’m used to that with glosses so it’s not a big deal to me.

The strawberry and grape both have micro glitter in them (mica). I didn’t know that when I got these. None of the product photos showed they had glitter and the description didn’t say it either. I’m not a fan of micro glitter in my lip glosses. I feel once the gloss wears off, it usually leaves behind glitter particles on my lips. Also, they can sometimes feel gritty. So, I was surprised when I saw 2 of the 3 had glitter. Luckily, these didn’t feel gritty. I do notice that there are some glitter particles on my lips after they wear off, but it’s not too bad. The glitter particles are really small, so it’s not really noticeable. So, I don’t mind that.

Overall, these are nice glosses with a nice formula. They might seem pricey when seeing the $30 price tag, but you’re getting 3 tubes of glosses, so that’s only $10 a piece, which isn’t bad. Of course, it isn’t great. You can get a tube of gloss that looks great and works just as well from the drugstore for slightly less. But, the ingredients might make it worth it to spend the little more. I give them 4 stars.

title: light, floral lavender
text:
Lavender is my #1 go-to essential oil. I think I use it in 90% of my blends, whether in the diffuser or in topical blends (or sprays, etc). The only thing I definitely don’t use it for is my home-made cleaning products where citrus oils are the only essential oils.

This particular oil is a very delicate scent – some lavender oils can pack quite a punch in terms of the scent. This is certainly floral and has a ‘high note’ to it. You can easily pick it out of a blend. It’s my first oil from New York Biology and I’m very pleased.

I love blending lavender in particular with chamomile, as it has an almost instantaneous calming effect. Also love to blend it with bergamot, ylang ylang, mandarin, and a drop of lime.

The bottle is very large, a dark brown color to protect the oil from UV rays which can damage the oils and decrease the shelf life. My favorite way to dispense oils is with the eye dropper (the euro droppers found in smaller bottles tend to gush several drops at once, so that’s definitely not my preference) – you can really control how many drops you dispense with these eye droppers.

Arrived well protected in bubble wrap and there was no leaks.

* I received the oil for evaluation and review

title: Unique. . .Maybe Too Unique
text:
This is a really neat razor that has one possible issue, which I'll get to later.

The handle is big and heavy, and its unusual shape is very stylish. It gives a nice shave, too. If you have a small face or tight features, the large head might be a bit tricky to use in some areas, but that hasn't been a major issue. I usually use an old-school double-edge razor, not a flexing cartridge razor, so the fixed head angle isn't an issue for me. If you're used to a razor with a movable head, this one might take some getting used to.

The included shaving foam smells good and works well. You don't get a lot, but you don't have to use a large amount of it.

The "stand" is just a heavy metal cylinder with a round hole in the top and a pad on the bottom. The hole is wider than the razor handle, and just deep enough that the razor doesn't topple out. It's kind of weird, like the stand was designed for something else, but I guess it works.

I'm not sure why they call this package a "travelling razor kit." It comes in a large gift box, and doesn't include any sort of travel case or bag. Plus, it's the biggest, heaviest razor I've ever seen (aside from folding straight razors). I wouldn't even think of taking this thing on a trip.

Despite all the good things about this razor, there's one major red flag: At the moment, replacement blades aren't listed on Amazon or on the Suprent website. The package includes two cartridges and a card to get a third for free, but there's no guarantee that more will be available when you need 'em. While the included cartridges are definitely good for several shaves apiece, if that's all you get, you'll soon be left with a very expensive paperweight. I rated the product based on my use of it, but recommend that you verify the availability of replacement cartridges before buying.

title: Disasterous experience
text:
Where do I begin with this one... The ponytail arrived in good condition but with a strong smell to it. I needed to dye it dark brown before wearing so I stored it in the bag it came in for a month or two. When I took it out I noticed it was quite (really) tangled, but I was able to wash it and detangle it just fine, and it was shiny and bouncy after the first wash. After this is when things went downhill. I lifted the color so it could take the brown dye, but to my horror it was badly tangled again almost instantly. I went ahead and put the brown dye on so that I could do all of the serious detangling when it was done. However, it wasn't quite that simple.

I have pretty thick, long, curly, color treated hair myself but never have I had such a hard time detangling hair. I had soaked it overnight in conditioner, and when that didn't work, used almost an entire bottle of detangler but it didnt seem to do much, I couldn't pass a wide tooth comb through it at all. After HOURS of brushing it out from tip to roots, soaked in conditioner and detangler it finally got to a manageable place, and I had a whole handful of hair that had been shed in the process. I have heard that some hair suppliers clean and treat low quality hair from multiple donors with harsh chemicals that dissolve the cuticle, then re-coat it with silicon before selling it so it looks smooth... I am certain that is what happened. The worst part is there is no way to really tell until you wash it a couple of times, at which point it can't be returned. How convenient. Seriously, these people should go to jail for fraud, and amazon should be investigated for selling items from any random vendor in unregulated countries. What if an adult gets a life threatening allergic reaction, or a child is poisoned because a toy has lead on it, for example. Who is responsible then? This is not okay and I will be looking into my options to get my money back, although I will never get back the lost time. DONT BUY HAIR ON AMAZON!

title: It's not what I thought it would be
text:
I gave this 3 stars for "Softness" because the brush is average to a bit firmer than what would be ideal and comfortable to use on your back, while the loofah strap is average. The brush bristles are kind of scratchy and not the "good exfoliating" kind of scratchy. They're more like the "ouch, that's scratching me" kind of scratchy. Overall, though, it's acceptable and average.

Next, I gave this 2 stars for "Easy to use" because I don't find this easy to use. The brush is separate from the stick that extends it to reach your back; you slide the oval-shaped brush onto the stick by inserting the stick into a cut out section on the back side brush. The problem here is that it doesn't stay on firmly at all. I ended up with 2 options: either not on firmly enough, so it kept popping off, or pushed on so much that it's very difficult to get off of the stick to use separately. The loofah strap is really easy to use, though. It's nice and long so there's plenty of length to comfortably hold each end and move it back and forth at most angles, no matter how thin or thick your arms or body may be. That's a real plus! But I still couldn't give more stars if only half of the set is easily usable.

Finally, I gave this 4 stars for sturdiness because there's no doubt, it seems pretty sturdy. The bristles on the brush have stayed intact. The loofah strap is firm and sewn solidly -- but it may be too firm. It's hard to get flexibility out of it. The elastic strap handle on the brush is flimsy, but overall, it's a solid set. The wood is a good, solid, well-finished wood without splits or cracks. It doesn't seem like a cheap product that's going to warp and break easily if you keep it away from hanging to be soaked when it's not needed for use. Putting it somewhere nearby where it stays dry is best.

title: Better then most at this price point, depends on which one you get
text: So it's honestly not bad at this price point. It sheds a bit but all units have some shedding. For the mix brown I give 4 stars.The face front is about 2 inches and is meant to be cut and plucked for a natural look. I did neither in the photo. I just folded it under the the front as I'm afraid that cutting will make it look lifted in the front and obviously show it's a wig without some glue to put it down. The color is not exactly what I wanted. I was hoping it would be a darker brown. It's kinda a mousey brown and alittle strange in my opinion. It will need to be restyle in the front as some waves/curls flattened out by how it was packed in transport. The part is both a plastic fake skin and a mesh on top. You can see the mesh upon close examination. Makeup might help to conceal this.... Or make it worse. What I did like was the fullness and length. The weft was not too easy to be seen even when pulling hair apart. This is good compared to other brands where the wefts are often very visible, especially in the back and crown of a unit. Because the simulated scalp is narrow, you won't be able to change the part. It's also a bit flat near the part so it's gonna take some work to give a bit of volume. I would have enjoyed this much more had the color been a rich brown and if the scalp was a bit more realistic. Would I wear in public? Probably not. Would this be good for photo shoots or costumes ? yes. Would I buy other colors from this brand? Yes and I haven't done that with other brands on Amazon. For the purple ombre: I give 3 stars. It doesn't have the lace in front. This is more pure costume. The black is very shiney and the front of wig where the part is shows a bit of the black backing for construction. If it laid more flat and had the lace I would have given the purple ombre 4 stars. Dull the shiney with some powder like dry shampoo or maybe even dark eyeshadow. The fake scalp is actually better on the purple ombre compared to the brown mix. The ombre for the blonde is also a 4 star. Hair at the crown is a bit flat but the rest of the style is beautiful. The brown to blonde has the 2 inch lace like the long brown one. It's not as full on the head but you don't see the wefts unless you pull it apart a bit.  I feel the color is much more realistic. Hair feels pretty good for a synthetic. Note if you play too much , it will get a knotty feel. Again, good for photos. Some people might actually wear it daily but I don't know if it took take daily abuse. Length is great.

I always like to apply the mask right after my shower before bed. After I've washed my face in the shower, I will apply the mask before any of the rest of my nighttime skin care routine. When I would use the mask, I would skip the serum part of my nighttime routine. I found that applying serum after the mask is simply redundant an unnecessary. After removing the mask there was always plenty of extra serum that would sit atop my skin, so I would rub the rest of it in gently with my hands until it's saturated which didn't take very long as the serum I found saturated very nicely. The mask did provide a very nice amount of moisture to my otherwise dry skin. I tend to get a dry spot or two on my face from time to time, particularly around the chin area, and I found that after wearing the mask I would not suffer from that issue. It left my skin smooth and with a nice afterglow as well. All in all I was very satisfied with my experience, so I would recommend giving them a try. text:
This is a good product. I haven't used any other to compare it with and
only used it once so far. There is an amazing assortment of attachments.

than a few millimeters, its best to use the clipper attachment first to
trim it down and then use the rotors. The biggest let down is the clean
up process. Hair is tightly compacted into the rotary blade housing.
I used tweezers, a dental pick, and compressed air and still couldn't
get all of the hair out. The mechanism is small and delicate so you have
to be careful. The instructions indicate that water can be used but I haven't
tried that yet. The instructions are brief and awkwardly worded. There are
helpful demonstrations on the internet.

title: Good...IF
text:
This is a potentially excellent product--IF you don't need it to be completely stable. It wiggles some, though if you put your weight directly over the leg and push straight up, it's fine. Just don't expect it to be rock solid. I have a regular grab bar on the right side and use the left support rail only--and that's fine because the two rails are not directly connected so you can use one rail or both. But as a big guy (230 lbs), I'd be nervous if I didn't have the grab bar even though it's rated for 300 lbs. it would be perfect for a smaller person who just needs a boost, but it could be potentially dangerous if a larger person with serious balance problems fell sideways.

Note, too, that this will NOT work with a 1-piece toilet that curves upward from seat to tank. The connector piece needs about 2 inches of flat space behind the seat.

Pros: Sturdy aluminum tube construction; designed to bear weight directly over the support; easy to put together with a screwdriver and maybe a pliers (depending on your toilet seat hardware); adjustable for height and width.

Cons: Works only with a traditional toilet; "wiggles" to the left and right; adjusting width and height might be difficult or impossible for a person with poor hand strength (the spring loaded buttons are stiff); made in China (but what isn't these days).

title: Overpriced and of diminished manufacturing quality than before.
text: A bit overpriced for the fact that I'm actually using 2 razors to shave ALL of the hair off my face and head.  That's not really the point of buying a razor, and unfortunately the varying quality of electric shavers ensures that you'll be experimenting forever.  That really sucks, I say.  Here, I'm cutting hair with the new razor, it is not cutting short enough, so I'm cleaning it all up with the previous razor I had.  It does cut hair, but the additional pieces are useless in this case as I'm referring to cutting hair without any pieces attached.  So, what do we have here?  A 10 piece haircut set by Wahl, a company that is generally reputed for its haircutting kits.  The set is only partially effective, and requires additional shaves to complete.  So, A) you wouldn't see it used in a barber shop, B) effectiveness is cut in half by quality.  I hate doing this, because I have bought Wahl in the past, but this particular razor is of diminished quality than what had been manufactured before.  I bought this razor because the original razor I had was not cutting short enough anymore, but now that razor is effectively being used to do the job of the new razor, which does not cut hair short enough.  Pretty par for the course regarding products I've bought in this decade.  Not sure what the hell is going on out there, but this decade has seen a stark downturn in the amount of flawed products on the general market.  I pine for the 90s and 00s, when I had no problem buying something that worked well (the 80s were defined by places like Radio Shack and therefore on par with what is occurring today.)  Back in the early 90s, I had a razor that lasted several years; All cuts were low enough, and all use was consistent.  Can't say it's like that today, anywhere you turn, regarding ANY products (the last CD I bought was a manufacturing horror story that I never could have ever foreseen in, say, 1991, and the CD I bought before that exploded in my player and broke into over 500 pieces.)  However, I still have CDs that I bought from the grunge/Pearl Jam/Nirvana era that are still in perfect condition and still going strong.  What gives?

title: Close, comfortable, and convenient
text:
Other reviewers have covered just about everything that I would have to say, so let me just add a "me, too" to what I consider to be the most important points.

1) Very, very comfortable shave, the most comfortable I've ever had. (I will qualify that by saying that this is the first electric shaver I've used in the shower, so as far as that type of shaving goes, my experience is limited.) It's not as close as a blade -- almost, but not quite.

2) It's very easy to clean, charges fast, and holds a charge for a pretty good length of time (probably about 45 minutes or so of shaving time).

3) The gel and lotion packs are a neat idea and are very convenient, but they are exceptionally pricey. They're about $1.25 each, and they last only about a week. I do use them when I travel for the convenience, but at home, I use regular shaving gel, and I encourage you to try the same. It saves a lot of money.

4) As with any new shaving technique, you will need to experiment a bit to find out what works at what doesn't as far as direction of motion, amount of pressure, and the like. They do say in the manual that you should give it three weeks, so if you don't like it at first, give it some time and try different shaving methods.

5) I've never actually dropped mine, so I can't confirm or deny whether it breaks as easily as others have said it does, but the shaver does look a little delicate, so being careful is probably prudent.

6) I don't use the trimmer, either, but I can see how having to change the attachment would be annoying, as others have reported.

All in all, I'm very pleased with the shaver. It makes shaving easy, convenient, and even fun -- so much so that, for the first time since I started shaving over twenty years ago, I'm actually shaving every day. For me, that says more about the shaver than anything else could.

1. I don't understand these reviews that complain about getting water into the battery compartment and corroding the batteries. I've never had this problem. It would seem that one would have to be really careless for this to happen. Don't submerge it or pour water over it, and you should be fine.
2. Don't worry about battery life. Get some Eneloop rechargeables, and swap them out anywhere from a couple weeks to a couple months and you'll be fine.
3. This does such a good job, my dentist assumes I'm flossing like I'm supposed to be. I'm not. I do use a waterpic, but only a couple times a week these days. My dentist gave me an A+ on my last visit (part of this is because of the fluoride rinse that's been helping strengthen my teeth, but that's another review).

So now to the reason I only gave it three stars.

I had one of these that we bought years ago. I don't remember how long, but it's been probably 5 years. I'm not exactly sure, but it's been awhile. It's always worked great and still does. We finally got tired of sharing, and when we saw they were only $20 on Amazon we got another one.

This second one has had to be replaced under warranty twice in about a year and a half. It just stopped working, both times. No corrosion in the battery compartment or anything. The unit looks pristine, it just stopped working.

The first one lasted about 8 months. The second one only about 6 months.

So while this is a great product (functionally) and I would still likely buy it again if my current one died out of warranty (can't beat $20) I'm getting concerned about the quality. Here's hoping third time's a charm.

title: The Bag Works, But Will It Last?
text:
The Gonex hanging toiletry bag works for short weekend trips, though I doubt it would persist through the rigors of camping or a multi-week, international journey. The bag is very lightweight, which is good for a backpack or small suitcase, but the thin materials of the bag appear as though they will wear out pretty quickly, especially when frequently loaded with heavy bottles of body wash, shampoo, and the like. I like that I can hang this bag on the back of a bathroom door (see photo), but the hanger on the bag is plastic, which limits the amount of weight you can hang in this bag.

I seldom fly or make long trips, so the Gonex bag meets my needs on short, overnight trips. If you are a person who camps or takes long journeys, you may want to try something a bit more sturdy and durable.

I hoped the kinky texture would be similar to my own hair but it was not. In my opinion, this feels like Indian hair that has been crimped. Very silky, very soft, & affordable so I'm not mad. I haven't noticed any shedding and I only needed to use 3 pieces since I was only trying to add a little length. The clips are very secure feeling in my hair & it was super easy to install myself. I am definitely a newbie to hair extensions so if you're nervous about being able to do this yourself, don't be!! I will say the hair did smell like burnt hair. Ya know the salon smell with all the hot tools on? Yeah that's the smell lol. Also I will note that it is very difficult to straighten the hair from the weft to about 5 inches down. If I would've known the hair wasn't a truly kinky texture, I would have gone with the regular straight. Overall I'm very happy with the product! I recommend highly.

Oh and sidenote: just for those who may be wondering. You can totally put your hair up with these clip ins. I do suggest getting a longer length though for a ponytail or high bun. No less than 14 inches in my opinion. Also if you're looking to add fullness to your hair, I'd recommend buying 2 sets. As stated earlier, I just wanted a little length in the back b/c my hair is already super thick so one set worked perfect for me.

title: BEWARE: Soft ... NOT Extra Soft
text: First and foremost, the brushes I received are marked "SOFT" not "Extra Soft" as product title says.  I received eight (8) brushes in two sealed packaged of four (4) each. I just think the individual packaging lends itself to the brushes remaining sterile until they are ready to be used.  I did notice some difference in the overall quality of the brush heads in comparison to the OEM heads.  The description refers to flossing action bristles; but the OEM Oral-B actually have several rubber flossing bristles amongst the other bristles.  These replacement brushes do not have the specialized flossing bristles.  But, all in all, these brushes seem to do a good job of cleaning my teeth at a FRACTION of the OEM cost.  They fit my Oral-B toothbrush body well, they stay in place, and they agitate properly.  Although the quality is not identical, these brush heads are a VERY GOOD option for a budget-conscious household.

title: good budget value tooth care kit for single people, but absolutely no fancy features or extras
text:
For the price, this is an excellent basic electric toothbrush and flosser. The two pieces lack the fancy features of more expensive pieces, but my dentist says all those extra features are not worth the money. The toothbrush works great and the only feature my dentist recommends is the 2 minute timer to make sure you give yourself enough time to brush all your teeth. I've always used string floss in the past, but this water flosser seems to work just as well most of the time. Sometimes there is some food stuck in my teeth that I still have to use the string for.

As I said, features are minimal. There is 1 charger for both devices, so you can't use the charger as a stand for both items. Instead of all the cardboard in the box, why not include a cheap plastic tray or stand? There also is no travel case, just a little cover for the toothbrush head. I would really prefer a full length hard case to be included instead of having to buy an aftermarket case that doesn't fit well. Also, you only get one tip each for both the flosser and the toothbrush and there is nowhere to easily store extras. This kit is probably designed for single people only, not couples or families.

title: Like a Less Forgiving Old-Style Pencil
text:
I'm an eyebrow fanatic, and I've used eyebrow wax, powder, pencils and stencils. I'm a huge fan of shaping and powder - that seems to work best for me - but I've never seen applicators like these so I thought I would give them a try.

Mine didn't arrive overly wet like those of other reviewers; they just seemed to be like normal pens. But the application was uneven and I did have to press hard to get any color other than simply a dark shading (like the side of a lead pencil).

Once I did use firm pressure, it was a little like using an old eyebrow pencil - but less forgiving with the multi-levels. Be sure to shape your eyebrow first, then apply the pen; don't expect the pen to comb as well as draw. The pen can provide the dramatically even look, or, with a lot of manipulation, a more natural look (which I prefer).

I didn't find the pen to be as long-lasting as expected. I try to be really careful in application, as I don't like to abuse my eyebrows or skin, and remove product only using makeup remover. However, I do perspire on my t-zones and that perspiration completely defeated the eyebrow pencil.

This is an interesting innovation with the four-tier brush - and it may work well for others, just not for me. Ingredients, which I so appreciate being noted on the box: water, acrylic ester copolymer, propylene glycol, hydroxyethyl cellulose, c177491, c177492.

title: Interesting Gritty Texture And Strong Clove Scent
text:
This Spa-Da Immunity Support Soap is one of the more interesting soaps I have tried. You get a pack of 6 small shield shaped soaps in a resealable plastic bag. The soaps are about 2.75 inches in length.

The scent is strong when you open the bag and especially in the shower. Some of the oils and ingredients included are cloves, cinnamon, oregano, peppermint, parsley, eucalyptus, and rosemary. If you don’t like the smell of cloves, then do not order this because that is the most predominant smell in my opinion. I like it though- it has a nice spicy kick.

The soap definitely feels different than I expected. It doesn’t feel really smooth like many soaps. When dry, they were slightly powdery when I ran my finger across. They are slightly gritty feeling which I noticed more once the soap became wet in the shower. This could be nice if you like a slight scrubby feeling. I typically rub it onto my mesh bath sponge or silicone sponge so I don’t really care about the grittiness either way. I found that it lathers and suds up very well with both my mesh and silicone sponges.

I just started using, so I’m not sure how many showers I’ll be able to get out of each bar. Honestly, I thought they might disintegrate and get used up fast simply based on how powdery they felt when dry. I don’t think it will last as long as some other soaps, but I was still surprised that I could somewhat see the outline of where the shallow cross was imprinted on the soap even after my first shower-and I did intentionally scrub my sponges all over that side pretty vigorously. I took a picture of what the soap looked like after one shower compared to unused bars.

Anyway, my skin feels very clean, perhaps even a little moisturized after using and I haven’t experienced any irritation to my sensitive skin (I have eczema).

I like that this soap is natural and free from harmful chemicals. I also love that it is made in the USA-Ohio specifically, which is where I am from.

I’ll be sure to update my review if any issues arise like if I find that the bars do in fact get used far too quickly. I hope my review was helpful in some way, and if so, I would love to know- thanks!!!

title: Good shaver for the price but a design flaw that can be fixed.
text: Okay, this shaver, which is sold under a varIety of name brands but is the FK-605 IPX7, almost certainly made in China (maybe by Genpai ?), has a design flaw, at least in this iteration, which causes it to suddenly not turn on (and maybe other fault modes as well). It's a good shaver, especially for the price, but mine recently would just not turn on, even though when I plugged it into its charger it showed fully charged. I like to fiddle with broken things and try to fix them, and I found that the little circuit board inside the shaver was out of place. The circuit board is held by one small screw and two plastic clips, but a good jar can knock it out of the clips so that it doesn't make correct contact with the on/off switch slider. Warning: If the battery has a charge on it, use only non-conductive tools once you get the case open. The board was fairly easily snapped back into place, and full functionality was restored. I used some wooden toothpick pieces to wedge the plastic clips securely in place, so hopefully this won't happen again. To expose the six little screws that hold the case together, the silver piece that holds the on/off switch can be pretty easily popped off, and then the black piece below the silver piece will come right off.

title: Not for the modestly inclined!
text:
Assalamu Alaikum. If you are a Muslim or another religion that wears a hijab (headscarf) let me start off by saying that this scarf is NOT for you unless you are purchasing for a child that is 6 or under to wear as hijab.

The length is ok, decent at best but not great. The width is the real issue. It will barely cover a medium to large size cranium such as mine. And forget about the nape of your neck because this will NOT reach that far to offer some covering. You better have a super high tide turtle neck on before trying to sport this as a hijab and leave the house!

As far as colors, they were fairly vibrant and really that was the most positive part of my experience with this scarf (not shawl). The Chiffon material is decent but a little cheaply made compared to other Chiffon hijab scarves I have had. And before someone gets all gins shooting about price and you get what you pay for, well that isn't always true. I get way better quality at heart hijab website and they are based in the UK and they ship all the way to the US where I am temporarily. And that isomething total shipping, not shipping per item so if you do a breakdown of scarves versus shipping and cost per item I found much better quality and price elsewhere.

If you are just wearing this for fashion to tie round your neck or use as an accent in your hair up-dos than this is the perfect size and you will have plenty to work with. But if you are in the same boat as me, a Muslim or someone who dresses and covers for modesty than you will be passing this off to your six year old for dress up.

Sage was meh (still smelled like I was walking into a place with incense but no real distinguishing scent above just being incense). I’m burning Myrrh now and it doesn’t have that acrid stronger scent that I am used to and smells much like the sage.

They last decent and light easier than the larger sticks that one would get elsewhere (e.g. Flora Classique Inc).

However - for the price - I think I’ll just go back to the cheaper stuff elsewhere.

title: The facial cleanser is great! Body wash was meh...
text:
When I bought this product, I received both the cell stimulating body wash and the facial cleansing creme and I feel differently about each product so I will write my review accordingly.

Body Wash (2/5 Stars):

I actually bought this because I needed a new body wash. I was hoping that the mint and argan oil would make my skin feel refreshed and very clean, but it really didn't. The body wash leaves a filmy sensation after I use it, and the mint scent/sensation does not pack the amount of power I was hoping for when I initially bought this item. I used the body wash for exactly one week before I put it in my cabinet to gather dust, as my back-up "I forgot to buy extra body wash" bottle. I really didn't like it much.

Facial Cleanse (4/5 Stars)

The facial cleanse was just the freebie that came with the body wash I wanted, so I wasn't really expecting to replace my usual face soap. I was so disappointed with the body wash, I almost didn't try it at all but I am glad I did. The facial cleanser delivered the minty sensation that I wish the body wash had. It was reinvigorating and made my skin feel both clean and fresh, without leaving any residue. I definitely have kept this product in my shower and would definitely consider buying it on its own because I enjoy how gently it cleans and how well it removes my make-up at the end of the day.

Overall, I rated it 3/5 Stars because of the average review of both products, but I will never buy the body wash again; the facial cleanser definitely made up for the purchase for me.

title: Dangerous Ingredients - Several Potential Carcinogens
text:
Not only did I not see any significant results with this bust cream (that is actually more of a balm than a cream) but it also contains several potentially harmful ingredients. As stupid as this may sound, I went ahead and tried the product anyway. Judge me as you wish, but please read this review and its entirety so that you may make a careful and truly informed decision on whether or not to purchase this cream.

Before I discuss the ingredients, I'd like to discuss the product itself. The "cream" is very thick—like a lip balm. It smells sweet and soft, but it has petroleum undertones which concerned me a little. That's why I decided to research the ingredients. As for the effectiveness of the product, it does not deliver. I followed the instructions (that were clearly not written by a Native English speaker and are somewhat difficult to understand) and applied this cream twice a day for a week. After those 7 days, there were no significant results—no changes in breast size or firmness.

Please, please, please do your research prior to buying cosmetics so that you know what you're putting on your body. Your skin is your body's largest organ and it absorbs these chemicals, which can lead to several health issues over long periods of use. The ingredients in this bust cream are highly questionable, ones that I would advise you stay away from.

Around 33% of the ingredients in this bust cream are potentially harmful, especially for use on the skin. I've outlined the harmful ingredients below, so that you can make an informed decision.

- Petroleum Distillates
Gasoline is a petroleum distillate, along with several other fuels including kerosene. The Center for Disease Control (CDC) states that petroleum distillates are exposed to the body via "inhalation, ingestion, skin and/or eye contact and feature symptoms such as irritation of the eyes, nose, and/or throat; dizziness, drowsiness, headache, nausea; dry cracked skin." Petroleum distillates are a "possible human carcinogen." They are actually prohibited or restricted for use in cosmetics in Europe.

- Ceteareth-20
According to the Environmental Working Group (EWG), Ceteareth-20 "may contain potential toxic impurities such as 1,4-dioxane." The EWG also recommends that consumers stay away from products containing these ingredients, stating that it may have the potential to contaminate certain products with carcinogens. Any moisturizers that contain this ingredient should include a warning that it is not safe to use on injured or damaged skin. Unfortunately, this Jaowying Bust Cream does not contain any such warning.

- DMDM Hydantoin
This ingredient was the most concerning for me. According to the Environmental Working Group (EWG), DMDM Hydantoin has been "proven to be a human skin toxicant and allergen with strong evidence to approve such." Why a company would want to include this ingredient in a skin product is beyond me. It is a formaldehyde donor, which means it is a derivative of formaldehyde (embalming fluid). The chemical has been linked to allergies, chest pain, fatigue, depression, headaches, and may even cause cancer.

Again, I cannot stress enough how important it is that you make informed decisions, especially when it comes to your body and health.

title: Okay, has some flaws
text:
The razor has a nice look and feel. Big display, good on/off switch, etc. It came with a paper from the manufacturer wanting to help before giving a bad review. That's admirable, but the problems I had with it are inherent in the manufacture, I think. The razor has a middle section between the two blades, meant for cutting longer hairs. A lot of razors have that feature, but this razor either didn't have blades or they didn't work. I could see the mechanism moving, but it didn't cut the hair. Consequently, the hairs got trapped in the slots without getting cut. It just pulled them, painfully. Shaving everyday didn't help, either.
The other blades were sharp and cut just fine. I stuck with it for a couple of weeks, but just threw it away.
I've been having trouble finding a razor that the blades don't get dull after a month. I couldn't even use this one long enough to find out if they would last that long.
This isn't me bashing the company or product, just my experience. I wish I could find something NOT made in China. No one has a standard of manufacture on products coming out of China, it seems. So far, anything made in China lasts about 2 months, then falls apart, no matter the brand. I've had several "high end" razors from brand names that I would not purchase again, because they don't last any longer than a cheap one, because they all come from the same place. China.
This is also not me railing against China. I just think a company that is going to outsource their manufacturing should require the same standard of product that they would require somewhere else.

title: FINALLY the search for the perfect water line eyeliner is over!!!
text:
I have searched high and low and tried handfuls of eye liners from expensive ones found in Sephora to grocery store cosmetic aisle brands.
Here's what I wanted out of an eye liner:

1. Most importantly I wanted one that would stay on my lower lid "water line" without pooling in the corners of my eyes within 4 hours.
2. An eye liner that goes on smoothly and easily
3. An eye liner that is black but that doesn't have any sparkles in it
4. One that stays all day but doesn't require a nuclear reaction and scrubbing to remove

I finally got all those things in this gel eye pencil!! It is the PERFECT eye liner for water lining. The very first day it arrived, I decided to test it out hard core. I put it on that morning at 7:30am and left on a hike in the mountains ascending 3,000ft in elevation over the course of 3 miles and back. I sweat like a pig, had sunglasses on half the time and off half the time, was wiping my face, you name it! I was absolutely in shock when I got home at 3:30pm that afternoon to look in the mirror and find that my waterline look nearly PERFECT! Unheard of. I'm so mad at myself for not taking an after picture, but I was just so tired and dirty that I forgot about it. Take my word for it though, this stuff went the distance BIG TIME!! It also came off very easily. I just put a little of my Neutrogena oil free eye makeup remover on a q tip and rubbed very gently and it came right off. WOW!

I really am blown away by this product, especially after trying so many and being disappointed. I was beginning to think there wasn't an eye liner out there that would really stay on my water line all day but I found it and I hope you found it too! I wish there was somewhere I could find this locally, but I've looked and haven't seen it anywhere yet. Thank goodness there is Amazon! And thank goodness for the people at Essence who have perfected eye liner! I can't recommend this enough. I did NOT receive this item free or at a discount

title: Used to love it, but.....
text:
I honestly hate having to leave a bad review. I used this product for a year and loved it. My skin looked better than it ever had, but then my fourth bottle really failed me.
My first three bottles each lasted me four months. Each seemed a little different in formulation. In the first bottle, the cleanser came out almost like water. Since it was my first bottle, I figured was just how it was (and some of the previous reviews would have me believe so). The second bottle was very foamy, but the smell was different, in a bad way. I kept using it, and kept having great results. The third bottle smelled better, but foamed less.
Then I got the fourth bottle. Smell was normal, foam wasn't great. Then my face began breaking out terribly, and the bottle ran out in 4 weeks!! I reached out to the company, telling them that I was breaking out and that the bottle was gone in four weeks instead of four months. They emailed me back, telling me that their formula hadn't changed, and that maybe I was using more without realizing it. I would assume that a company selling a 4oz bottle of facial cleanser for $30 would be a little concerned instead of accusatory. I assumed that maybe I got the last bottle on a run, so maybe the formula was unbalanced and the bottle wasn't filled properly. I know, for sure, that I did not use quadruple the amount of cleanser each day, and the company assuming that I did is crazy.
To make a long story short, I used to love this stuff, but since the company only offered to send me a 20% off coupon code for my next bottle, instead of a full replacement for a bad bottle, I will not be buying from them again. I really and truly wish it had worked out though.

title: AMAZING COLOUR!!!! Truly an "electric" blue! Also really easy and reasonably mess-free.
text:
Wow. Super-easy to use...I just combed it into a tween's blonde hair (no bleaching). Gave the colour great dimension with the various shades of natural blonde. Would be hard to use on dark hair without bleaching.
I left it on for about an hour, unwrapped. I cannot figure out how you'd blow-dry hair that's IN a shower cap as you do it (part of the instructions), so I just removed the cap and did the blowdry while gently combing through the hair with a comb (until dry). Then a rinse - this is where all the blue looks like it's coming out. Use cooler water.

We re-dyed every 7 days, and the colour stayed vibrant.

Since then, it's been about two months and the electric blue went to pale cotton-candy blue, then to teal, now it's the colour that blonde hair goes with too much pool chlorine in the summer (sort of a washed-out green). I've heard that you can get more colour out by using a "clarifying" shampoo, but the tween seems happy with the transformation.

No real mess, but the bath does have a faint blue tinge to the bottom from the rinsing. It seems to scrub out a little more with each regular cleaning.

WARNING: If you leave strands of blue hair on the counter and they get wet, they will leave thin blue lines on the Corian. This is true even days after you dye the hair.

title: OTC Progesterone Doesn't Do It For Me
text:
For the past 10 years I have tried one over-the-counter progesterone cream after another, including ALL of the brands recommended in Dr. Lee's book. Unfortunately, none of them worked very well for me. After 10 years of going from one brand to the next, I finally gave up, got my hormones tested, and had my doctor prescribe a compounded bioidentical formula for me.

The problem with over-the-counter progesterone is that you really don't have any precise way of knowing how much progesterone you're really getting, regardless of what the label says.

I thought I was taking 40 mg. of Natra-Gest a day. And yet, when my progesterone levels were actually checked, the pharmacist said the amount of progesterone floating around in me was almost non-existent. Go figure. This makes me wonder if there really is as much progesterone in over the counter creams as specified on the label.

Now I'm taking 40 mgs. of compounded bioidentical progesterone cream. At least I know how much progesterone I am really taking in.

ZRT Laboratories has simple saliva testing which you can order online. You spit into a tube, send the saliva back to them, and within 2 weeks, they send back your results with suggestions. They even give you an easy-to-understand summary about what they found. You can then take those results to your doctor and arrange to get a compounded progesterone made specifically for you.

Because of the many problems I experienced with over-the-counter progesterone creams over the past 10 years, I'll never buy them again. They just don't work for me.

I guess each woman's body is different. My doctor did tell me, however, that compounded progesterone cream and over-the-counter progesterone cream cannot even be compared. According to her, they are like "night and day." Those were her exact words.

If you find that you are not receiving satisfactory benefits from any over-the-counter progesterone cream, it may be time to think about trying a compounded progesterone, made specifically for you. These one-size-fits-all over-the-counter progesterone creams are not able to help all women, especially women who are in their late forties and are in the perimenopause stage of life.

title: MIxed feelings
text:
After reading on many shaving blogs about how much closer a straight-edge razor will shave, I decided to try it out. I got tired of using disposables and having difficulty cleaning them and dealing with the cost. Having never tried straight edge shaving before, I debated whether to buy a high end blade, a cheap one, or something in the middle. I decided to go for the higher end of the lower cost models and bought one of these.

My first impression on removing it from the box was that the gold embossing on the handle really detracted from the looks of an otherwise attractive blade. But it doesn't really matter what it looks like if it works well. Out of the box, it is not shave ready. I did everything I'd read about to prep properly (except hone the blade) and it just didn't produce a close shave and pulled quite a bit. By way of comparison, I went back over and got a much improved result from a three week old disposable afterwards.

I have no doubt that this will take an edge and function just fine, and I suspect there is some truth to the "snob" argument that a better blade will hold an edge longer, as is true of knives, but almost any blade can be honed to sharpness. In fact, I subsequently purchased a different brand of carbon steel blade that was pre-honed from the seller and it performed quite nicely. To be fair, I don't know that a more expensive blade won't have the same issues if not honed by the seller prior to shipment.

As stated by another reviewer, any blade will require maintenance and the skills to sharpen it if you plan to use it regularly. I will give a try at sharpening this one eventually since I will need to learn this skill. Just be aware that you may need to develop the skill or find someone to do it for you before you will get a good result.

text:
This is the worst eyebrow pencil I’ve tried at this price, and it’s even worse than the e.l.f. version that’s similar. I know that’s dramatic but the reason why I wanted to write this review is because I’m just so frustrated with the quality compared to the price. It’s just not okay!

I’ve been using the nyx precision brow pencil, but this was a few dollars cheaper at ulta at the time and so I got it because the nyx one is like 10 bucks. My brows are the makeup I wear most consistently, so I’m always trying different brow pencils to try to cut down on the cost. But I go back to nyx every time. Maybe the morphe one is okay but it’s pretty hard and waxy so not really. Now I know the importance of the extra two dollars for the nyx.

This pencil is so soft, it wears down so quickly and also because of how soft it is, it’s not precise at all. And it’s not pigmented either, so I end up using a larger amount of product because of that. To do both my brows, and I fill them in pretty lightly, I use about 1/8” of product each time. The nyx one I use less than 1/16” and it’s more pigmented.

I would compare this to the elf one in terms of pigmentation and texture. Except the elf one is like $3. So at this price point I expected it to be way better than something that’s less than half its price.

And after using it a few times, the spoolie end came off when I was trying to take the cap off to use it. The main body of the pencil cracked on that end. So now I have to use a spoolie from another brow pencil, good thing I have one. And this has just been on my desk, not banging around in a makeup bag or anything like that. So definitely don’t get this if you need to take it places it can’t handle it.

This is one of the few times I would return a makeup product, it’s just so egregiously bad.

title: Great scent, good hold and volume, rinses poorly
text:
After having had a 1/4-inch buzzcut for about 15 years, about 18 months ago, I started growing out my hair, which is now quite long and sits around the bottom of my ear. As a result, I've been using different types of hair products to style it in different ways and keep it under control. Given a chance to try this pomade, I decided to give it a shot.

Packaging-wise, this is really simple: a glass jar with a metal lid. It has that old-timey barbershop feel, and would look nice on your counter or shelf, if you're into displaying your grooming products. Just remember it's glass, and an accidental drop on your counter or tiled floor is going to result in a disaster. The lid is a good quality and the seal seems to keep the product fresh.

As soon as you open this jar, you'll recognize that "barbershop scent". It has that minty-eucalyptus odor that's refreshing and eye-opening. There are days when I use this, when I'm sitting at my desk I wonder "what smells so good"...and I realize it's my hair. So if you're into good scents and smelling-good for yourself or others, you'll definitely like this.

The consistency of this product is quite interesting. It looks like vanilla pudding. However, it's definitely much thicker than vanilla pudding. It's not sticky. It feels and looks like a compound that would end up very oily in your hair, but that's not the result. Even given my hair's length, I don't have to use a lot of this, and typically on damp hair I only have to use about two fingertips' worth of this product in my hair.

While your mileage may vary, when I put this in my hair, it has an immediate effect. It provides immediate styling strength. It also helps to add a bit of volume, so that as I comb it through, I can easily prop-up the parts of my hair to give it a little volume and height. It dries well and doesn't get too stiff, leaving my hair with some movement, where I'm not afraid to run my fingers through it or adjust it. I'd say it's really good for my more "casual day" styles.

My only complaint, and for me this is really important, is that it doesn't rinse well in the shower. I only wash my hair every third day to maintain its health, and while nearly every other product I use rinses almost cleanly without leaving much of a residue, this particular product won't rinse cleanly. This becomes a problem if I use this on day two, but want to use a different product on day 3, for example. It definitely adds to residual build-up. I realize not every product rinses cleanly with just water, but this one is particularly problematic, forcing me to either wash my hair earlier or plan the days on which I use this so the build-up doesn't become an issue on consecutive days. So, if like me, you don't like washing your hair often, this may be a deal-breaker.

Overall, though, I'm quite impressed. The small jar is actually going to last me quite some time. It has a great scent and styling power. I'd probably use it every day if it weren't for the rinsing issue.

My hematite magnetic bracelet arrived today, one day sooner than expected which is a good thing. The early arrival is the only reason this product got an extra star, I would have only given it 2 stars, not 3, but the early arrival helped saved its rating. I know the old adage "you get what you pay for" and I guess I will have to learn to deal with that in regards to this bracelet. Don't get me wrong, it's attractive, very masculine and has an awesome color. But the quality of it all, it would have been nice for them to put a couple more hematite pieces onto the bracelet. I'm not a very big guy, my family jokes about my girl looking wrists all the time. But even with my petite wrists the black stretchy bands that make up the bracelet are showing. I have like a half inch gap of missing material, meaning a half an inch of my skin and those two black cords are showing! It would have been great for them to put at least two more of those block shaped pieces and maybe 4 more pearls into the bracelet, then I wouldn't have this embarrassing gap on the back side of the bracelet. Oh well, I will wear it from time to time, but not as many times as I was was planning to before making this purchase.

I have used this product since it was first introduced and have ordered from various sellers on Amazon. This order does not work like the Dove antiperspirant I can purchase at a local store. To make sure there wasn't something else going on, I bought the same product at the store and applied it like I used to and went through the day without a single issue.

The product, when purchased from the store works great and lasts a full month for a can. This product that I bought on Amazon requires multiple heavy applications a day - I've gone through 6 of the 9 cans in 2 months. I've given up and am throwing the remaining cans out since it's like spraying aerosol into the air with for no apparent reason since the product from this purchase doesn't work.

While I don't love spending $5-6 per can at the store per month, spending $3 per can for 3 cans a month from this purchase is no bargain for a product that pretends to be the same as what I can buy locally. That's sad since I've purchased this several times on Amazon from other sellers without an issue but now I'm skeptical and probably should stick to buying it from the local store.

text:
I received this product for free through the Vine program.

I requested this for my wife who was looking forward to trying it. She was less impressed after actually using the product and below are her impressions:

Now, to be honest, I have not used eyebrow powder before. I typically use a pencil. I do so because my brows are nonexistent by the time they reach my arch. The included photo shows what I typically get from my pencil on one eye and the new stamp on the other. I found that applying the powder is faster than my usual pencil routine. However, I still had to spend time cleaning up all the excess powder from above and below my brow after application and I had tried to get any excess off the stamp prior to use. This ESpace eyebrow stencil kit is labeled light brown. My hair is medium ash blond, and this eyebrow powder is WAY TOO DARK for my coloring. The stamp has two colors, and I picked the one that looked least dark. I know my head is small and although the kit includes twenty-four eyebrow stencils, they all seem too big for my face. Assuming you have an average head size these stencils might work for you. The kit’s brow razor works fine. If you like dramatic large brows this system might work better for you than it did for me.

title: A Great Mascara AND A Great Lash Curler!
text:
I have pretty small, hooded eyes, so it’s hard to find a lash curler that works for my eyes. The biggest issue I have is them pinching my eye when I’m clamping down to curl them. I always have to lightly clamp down to see if I’ll pinch myself and, if I will, then adjust. Then, I end up having some parts not curled. I’d been looking for a new curler for a while, when I saw this I figured it was worth a try since I also got mascara.

Someone in the reviews had said the package came damaged. Mine also did. It wasn’t too bad, just seemed a little beat up. But, the products inside were completely fine and didn’t seem damaged at all, so I was okay with that.

I am very picky about my mascara. Well, not so much the mascara as I am the mascara wand. With my small, hooded eyes, it makes it so I end up with a lot of mistakes of the wand hitting below my lower lash line or onto my hood. So, I prefer thinner wands. I wasn’t sure what to expect with this mascara, but I was also getting a lash curler so I figured I’d hopefully like at least 1 of them. I’m happy to say that the mascara wand isn’t too thick. It’s not extremely thin, but still thin enough so it works for me. It also has a little bend to it, which helps with application. The mascara goes on very easily and doesn’t clump up after a few coats, which is great! It stays on all day without smearing. But, it also washes off easily at the end of the day, which I always love. It’s hard to find a mascara that stays all day without smearing or smudging, but is easy to wash off. So, it’s nice this does both!

The lash curler is amazing! It’s lightweight. It feels so nice. I love the red, black, and gold. It looks so fancy! It fits my eyes really well and curls my lashes AMAZINGLY without pinching my eyes at all! I’m really happy with it! It also comes with replacements for the rubber part on the curler, so that was great!

For $11.99 (at the time of writing this), it’s an amazing deal! You’re getting an amazing lash curler and an amazing mascara. You can’t beat that! If you’re looking for a great mascara, a great lash curler, or both, you should definitely give this a try!

title: Why can't America make them like this? Talent. That's why.
text:
What an incredible display of motion on screen. That Iron Monkey has amazing fight choreography is a given but what amazes me many times in these movies is how even with all the non-stop action they still seem to get in some descent character development. Let's face it. You can have the best fights ever but if you don't care at all about the people it's only good for one viewing and we're here looking for multiple viewing, right kids!
The chinese actors are incredibly adept at using few words and clever use of body language to convey as much in one scene that Stallone or Willis can't produce in an entire movie. The problem in the U.S. is that acting is not really infused with any real physical ability like in Asia. Often from a young age martial arts are a part of a performer or actors life. Some more than others. Someone in the US who has studied for the physical abilities probably can't act their way out of a paper bag because it hasn't been a part of growing up for them. The prime example being good ol' Chuck Norris.
Just say thanks that we in the U.S. can finally get good access to these action masterpieces. This movie is Fist of Legend's equal in fight scenes but surpasses it in natural humour.
If you want to experience another great HK movie that's in a modern setting and not a period piece try Tsui Hark's Time and Tide. Not as action orientated but with great characters and slightly more realistic sequences.

title: Perfect for my needs
text:
These spray bottles are just what we needed. We use spray bottles for a variety of purposes, and after putting these to the test we were happy with the results.

First was for spray cleaner. We sometimes mix our own natural cleaners, and they worked great for that purpose. No muss, no fuss, just good even sprays. They are ideal for this.

Next, I use a soapy mixture to control pests in my garden. Same results here. The bottle sprayed nicely and evenly, with no leaks or clogs. (I'm sure if there was just water in the bottle, it'd be perfect.)

The last use was the trickiest: a water and white glue mixture used in crafting. Things were a little more fussy here, but still usable. The spray worked, but the nozzle would get minor clog after a few sprays, sending the spray in uneven, odd directions. A bit of warm water would clear it up, then it would clog again. Still, this was water and GLUE, so it's not uncommon for some bottles to be fussy with such a mix.

The squeeze action works pretty well, simple and smooth. The plastic is a slightly harder plastic, more prone to breaks if squeezed than softer bottles. The manufacturing quality is on the cheaper side. They work well, but are not made for wear and tear.

Overall, getting six of these for a ten spot is a pretty good deal, so they get a thumbs up from me, with the caveat that they won't take a lot of punishment.

title: Quality Brushes, case turns into 2 cups for storage and easy access!
text:
This is a really great quality set of brushes. I am a mineral makeup user, and struggle to find brushes that pick up the right amount of product without being wasteful. I have several brands of brushes, some purchased from amazon and some purchased piece by piece in Ulta or Sephora and these brushes are the same type of quality you would expect to find in a beauty store. You get 12 brushes and a very nicely made carrying case, I actually split the brushes into face and eye and keep the case open as holders placing eye brushes in one and face brushes in the other. I like that the seller addresses the smell issue head on, they include it in the instructions, you need to air out the brushes for 2 days and then gently wash the bristles, I find that philosophy brand face wash is what I prefer to use as a weekly washing for the bristles it really restores and removed the makeup that accumulated thru out the week. I will breakdown the brushes and how I feel they perform.
1. Large Powder – perfect for my setting powder to complete the look.
2. Large Angled Contour - great for both blush and bronzer
3. Duo Fiber – use for stippling on my powder foundation
4. Foundation – applying foundation to my hairline and around my nose
5. Large Shader – works very well, picks up product without being wasteful
6. Concealer – smallish but so are the spots it needs to hit!
7. Medium Angled Shading – use for my eyebrow powder
8. Angled Shadow – great for my crease
9. Tapered Blending – awesome at working out the edges of the lid
10. Small Angle – use for my top lid eyeliner
11. Eye Liner – use for my bottom liner, fits well under the lash line
12. Pencil Brush – use it wet when I want to darken my mineral liner
I have had these for several weeks and I am impressed. I received these brushes at a discount in exchange for a honest review to test them and I am glad that I did.

title: Impressive ship speed, simple & easy product assembly, sturdy seat, comfort & cushion level of seat is ok -below average
text:
Impressive shipping speed- Product was delivered promptly and I received it today (within 3 days of order)- shipped out of a local warehouse near King County, WA. (Thank you shipper). I ordered this for my small office that did not have space for a full chair and I needed to adjust seating based on varying table height so I wouldn't have to adjust my patient treatment table every day after my office partner uses it. This chair hopefully was also intended to slide out of the way under the table. (This is yet to be seen).
Packaging was simple and in a nice sturdy cardboard box with built in sturdy handles- a plus. Unpacking was easy and there were 4 pieces included in the box all of which were bubble wrapped except for the base and seat pieces. The easiest assembly I have gone through and took me all of 5-7 minutes. There was no shipping record or paperwork and the assembly instructions were almost non-existent except for a single sheet of paper with a picture of all the components shipped.
The first thing that struck me was how wide and large the saddle seat was so this is a great purchase for those who are wider in the seat. Roughly measures about 17" wide and 16" long from rear of seat to the saddle tip. the leather on the stool looks great and is nailed with a few staples on the underside. The construction on this is average and attention to detail was missed. Again a small move that would have raised this rating to much higher.
The picture enclosed wasn't very clear with the plastic piece in the round foot rest component. I had to figure this piece out. Everything else just snaps in as displayed in the order shown. Tighten the foot rest plate so that it is stable. I sat on the seat for about 10 minutes and it was not a comfortable experience for my tail bone. I will have to pad this seat even further with a towel or a blanket perhaps. They indicate a 3" cushion which I do not think is hardly sufficient. I am not used to a saddle seat and it feels like you are straddling a seat between your legs with a small hump in front of you. I opted this for the footprint of the stool, cushion, comfort, swivel and the ability to support lower-back issues.
If the seat comfort was slightly more comfortable and cushioned by at least another 2-3" I would have given this product 4 or 5 stars. Will update after 1-2 months of use.

title: Excellent for price, but somewhat misleading advertisement
text:
I just received this dermatoscope yesterday. For the price, it is excellent. It is a simple to use, contact dermatoscope that gives the user a bright, clear image of skin lesions. I like that it is LED since those seem to last forever, and it even has a lifetime guarantee on the light source. It is comfortable to hold and the carrying case fits well in my white coat.

My reason for not giving 5 stars is that the product description claims that it can be used with or without oil. I suppose this is technically true, as I use alcohol as my immersion fluid of choice. However, if this scope is used without any immersion fluid (as implied by "oil-free epiluminescence microscopy"), it is basically just a 10x magnifying glass. The purpose of dermoscopy is to help visualize structures below the stratum corneum. If the light is not polarized (which it is not in this dermatoscope), then an immersion fluid is necessary to reduce light reflection/refraction/scatter by tiny irregularities at the skin surface in order to see the deeper structures. If you want a true oil-free dermatoscope, you will need one with polarized light (note that these are generally much more expensive and do not necessarily produce a better image). I truthfully did not expect the claim "oil-free" to hold true, but purchased it anyway since I don't mind using immersion fluid and the price cannot be beat. Therefore, I'm not disappointed, but if you are considering purchasing this mostly due to the "oil-free" claim, I'd advise against it.

Basically, if you want a dermatoscope that will give you a great image at a great price, this is your product. If you do not want to use oil or another immersion fluid, make sure you purchase a dermatoscope that is polarized.

Update: October 2013 - After using my dermatoscope for three and a half years in residency and private practice dermatology, the contact plate (where the glass contacts the skin) broke. When I contacted the manufacturer they responded quickly and even offered to send me a free replacement. I continue to be pleased with this dermatoscope and the customer service that stands behind it.

title: Just what a natural loofah is supposed to be!
text:
I’ve been using natural fiber loofahs (not the plastic kind) off and on since 2010. By nature there is some variation, depending on the size of the underlying plant, the way it’s made/grown, any bleaching, softening or other treatments applied that may change the texture. This is GREAT value for three medium-to-small sized natural loofahs.

The first time you use it you gotta soak it in warm water to puff up (it will turn into an oval cylinder, rather than staying like a flat pad) and release its seeds. I didn’t find the seed quantity to be gross or unreasonable, though it’s definitely different than most natural loofahs you’ll buy in a drugstore or Whole Foods, say—those tend to be treated and at least prewashed, to remove the seeds etc.

The smell: I have a super sensitive nose. Just speaking for the item I received, this is 100% “normal loofah smell” —a little grassy, kind of like dried clean straw that’s been dampened again—with a bit of a smoky smell. It’s not offensively smoky. Like a lot less than most whiskey. No “funk,” though the natural loofah herbaceous-ness does get stronger when it’s wet.

I didn’t find this too scratchy at all—in fact, by the time I’d finished soaking out the seeds I found it a little soft for my liking. To be fair I do drybrush about once a week, so I’m used to a good scrub. But if you know what a “normal store-bought loofah” feels like, this is no scratchier than that. If you have super sensitive skin, try using this after it’s soaked in a bowl or tub of hot(!) water for 10 min or so, with some emollient body wash like Aveenk.

title: I found this hair to be quite good for the price
text:
I found this hair to be quite good for the price. The texture is smooth and straight, silky but not fragile. The texture and shine is pretty realistic--maybe a bit on the shiny side--but since the hair is of a uniform colour, you'd have buy multiple colours and mix them in order to avoid the flat "bad dye job" look. The feel is a bit plasticy, but wigs aren't for touching anyway. The hair is resilient, and doesn't tangle easily or pick up static. The colour (dark auburn) was a fair bit darker than shown on the photo. I have a professionally-calibrated monitor for graphic design, so if the photo colours are off, it's not on my end. That said, I can understand if they did that on purpose: The hair itself is so dark that it would show up black on a lot of people's monitors if it they didn't lighten up the photo a bit. The quantity of hair is pretty good for the price, but I find I'd rather pay a little more for the bundle to include just a bit more hair--the amount per bundle is juuuuust a tad too thin to make a satisfying extension or ponytail, so you'd end up having to buy two and having a bunch leftover. Lame.

I received my order within four days. The hair had been folded up a little too tight in the packaging, so when I first unboxed it, it had a couple of kinks that fell out on their own during the wigmaking process.

The reason I'm giving it a four is because of the lies and deceit about this hair being suitable for curling. Granted, you should never take a styling iron to synthetic hair no matter how heat-resistant it claims to be, but I had that previously-mentioned "bunch leftover" so I gave it a shot on a low temperature. The hair came out melted and frizzy-but still straight. Why god why would you tell people that their hair can be heat-styled if heat styling will ruin their hair? For the wig itself, I used the standard steam-styling method, which worked just fine and didn't damage the hair.

I'll try the product again in a few days now that I'm done with the medicine, but I had the opposite result I wanted from using this product.

The smell is initially strong, but not once applied to the face. It takes several seconds for the heat of my fingers to pick up enough of the salve to apply. The liner was still awful but the lash was a little better except for in one spot where there was extra glue on the lash itself which again made the lash very uncomfortable to wear. Also, the lash kept wanting to lift away from my natural lash line. In the pic you can kind of see this in the corners of my eye. Better fit though although not super comfortable. I still didn’t think I’d be able to wear all day or even for an hour without wanting to rip it off. Anyway, I removed that lash and a magnet came off with it. title: HORRIBLE! Tracks showing, HUUUUGE knots, hair fried!
text:
I got the 22” Body Wave 13x4 T Part Lace.

I do NOT recommend this wig! I recommend you quickly exit out from looking at this one and find ANYTHING else! The hair is so fried! It looks and feels unhealthy! The knots are HUUUUGE! They look sooo unnatural! The top is thin so you can see the tracks. Since you only have 1” parting space, which is already the middle part, there’s no room to change it so you can’t even try to cover the tracks. There are stains inside the cap, which look to be from the combs. There are tons of dark hairs mixed throughout the hair (even though the product page said it was virgin hair, unprocessed hair. But this definitely did not come from a natural blonde. It was bleached and it wasn’t done well so it’s totally fried!). I would honestly give it zero stars if I could, but I have to give at least 1 star. I go into more detail below if you’re interested…

The product page states this is 150% density. I’m never good at determining if it’s accurate density. It honestly looks about 150% density. HOWEVER, there are areas on the top that are thin and you clearly see the tracks. Unfortunately, this is a T part Lace, so you don’t have room to change the part to cover the thin area. To me, that makes it unbearable.

The knots on this thing are INSANE! I have no clue what on earth is going on with them but they are HUGE!! They look so unnatural and ridiculous!

The product page says it is “premium hair material” and “we guarantee that T part Blonde 613 Lace Front Wig Human Hair Is 100% Real Blonde Human Hair Wigs, Soft & Healthy, No Tangle, No Shedding, Can Be Dyed, Bleached, Curled Etc.; You Can Buy without Worries.” Honestly, that is a joke! It is blonde, but it has been processed to be blonde. There are a ton of dark hairs mixed in throughout the hair. The hair has been badly bleached so it’s fried. I would never want to dye/bleach this again because I honestly don’t think the hair could take it since it’s in such bad condition! It definitely isn’t “healthy.” It’s not even really all that soft because you can feel how the hair is fried.

The hair they show on the mannequins in the product photos on the product page are definitely NOTHING like the hair I received! That hair looks soft, healthy, plucked well, and without humongous knots and tracks showing on top.

When you scroll down to the middle of the product page where they have more info. It says on the side in the grey box, “Wig Type: T Part Blonde Body Wave Virgin Human Hair Wigs.” It also says, “ Human Hair Quality: Unprocessed Brazilian Human Hair, Minimum Shedding.” “Just Like Your Own Human Hair, No Chemical.” Just full of LIES! This is NOT virgin hair. Virgin hair is also known as unprocessed hair (they mean the same thing). Unprocessed hair is human hair that has NEVER been chemically processed, this means over the life of the hair it’s never been dyed, coloured, or bleached. As a result, unprocessed hair is incredibly healthy. This has DEFINITELY been bleached so it is NOT Virgin/unprocessed. It is definitely NOT “no chemical.”

It has 13x6x1 T part lace. That means the lace goes 13” in the front ear to ear, it goes 6 inches back, and the parting space is 1”. The product page said, “T- part 13x6x1 Lace, Giving You the Ability to Have a Longer or Multi-direction Partings and Makes You More Natural.” If you know what 13x6x1 lace means, then you already knew when you purchased it that the parting space is only 1” wide. But, some people might not know what that 1 means at the end. They might see it, but then see the product page says “ability to have a longer or multi-direction partings” and think they can change the part if they want. Like I said earlier, you can NOT change this part! It is only 1” wide and that whole 1” is plucked out making the middle part. There’s no room to change it. It’s unfortunate because, like I said earlier, you can see the tracks next to the part and if you could change the part you’d have the possibility of covering them up. But, you can’t with this.

Oh, and there’s weird stains inside the cap. They look to be from the combs.

I thought it was really funny in the middle of the product page they had a little thing that said, “Are you satisfied with the 613 blonde lace front wig human hair you bought before? If not satisfied, you can try ours. Maybe we will become the terminator of your choice of blonde lace front wig human hair, and we hope to have the opportunity to become your superstar.” Become the terminator of your choice? What the heck does that mean?! 😂 They definitely are NOT going to become my superstar, or anyone else’s if they keep putting out wigs like this! Especially given the fact they’re charging $102.39 for the 18” body wave (at the time of writing this review) is crazy! It is nowhere near worth that! I definitely do NOT recommend!

text:
I really learned to shave properly about a year and a half ago and bought a Merkur and an Edwin Jagger double edge along with a couple of straight razors. I also started to collect shaving soaps and creams one of which was this one. I realize that almost everything to do with likes and dislikes when it comes to do with shaving is very individual so my opinions may not resonate with yours!

I find Mitchell's Wool Fat to be a nice soap. It took a little practice to learn to make a good lather with it but it was well worth the time! The lather holds up through a three pass shave and works well when using a straight razor or a double-edge. I am also impressed with the way this stuff lasts! The puck I am using seems to keep on going so I would say the slight extra cost is offset.

Pros

Makes a good long lasting lather

Lubricates the face well

Not expensive when you factor in the longevity of the puck

Cons

None that I can think of.

Jimbo's rating system:

Ease of making a lather ****

Fragrance ****

Lubricating quality ****

Does the lather hold up ****

Soap to lather ratio *****

Bang for the buck *****

Would I buy this again? Yup!

I give this a solid 4 star ratting because this is, in my opinion, a really nice shaving soap and I would not hesitate to buy it again.

Jim
