title: Meh, I'm torn on this one. I really want to like it... (UPDATED)
text:
Let me start out by saying I'm really starting to love Philips Norelco products. I was always a Braun guy but I'm starting to convert, based on amazon reviews and my own recent purchases. As an example, I'm a recent owner and very happy owner of the [[ASIN:B0037HP9OA Philips Norelco BG2040/34 Philips Norelco Bodygroom Pro Grooming System, Black / Silver]].

What I like:
With that said, I want to love this product, I really do. It's (for the most part) high quality, its rechargeable, you can clean it under tap water (a must for me), its light-weight, it's a brand I trust. I love that there are no blades to replace (self sharpening), I love that the clipper attachments are built-in/adjustable (no swapping required for me) and I love that it comes apart easily.

My first haircut - too short!
You could call this my fault, or you could call it bad design. Or both. I'm a guy that pretty much shaves his whole head; to keep it simple, and to last longer. I do it myself, because I can and because my wife has better things to do. But I don't like it too short. Which is why I tried to start long and work my way down until I got a feel for these clippers. I started at level 3, grabbed the clippers in the most comfortable position I could manage, and started my haircut. I noticed immediately you can't go too fast with these. They don't have the power of my cheap plug-in clippers, but cost almost twice the price. Which means I had to go a lot slower with these. Perhaps that's just a drawback of cordless? Anyways, my hair was already short, and I was only taking off a little hair; but these things start jamming and pulling my hair as if I was taking kindergarten scissors to a tree branch. So I backed off and took it a lot slower and didn't snag my hair any more. First strike. And then it happened. I felt my head and realized my hair was a lot shorter then normal. And it was. The clippers somehow slipped from position #3 to #1 while I was cutting. And here's why. To adjust the clippers, you push on a small tab on the back and slide the attachment up and down. Its very easy to do. This tab, however, sits exactly where I grip the clippers when I cut my hair. And that's how it happened; I grabbed the clippers, mistakenly pushed the tab, and slid the attachment while cutting my hair. My vote, poor design. The attachments should lock in place and require a twist or something more difficult.

My second haircut - bald spot down the side of my head!
You could also call this my fault, or you could call it bad design. Or both. So I cut my hair a second time today - this time making sure I took it slow enough as to not bog the clippers and snap my hair. And I was careful not adjust the attachment position mid-haircut. But upon approval of my wife of my second haircut, and her laughter, I realized I screwed up. Yep, looked in the mirror, and I have a huge bald spot in the side of my head. BALD. So what happened this time? When I cleaned the attachments after the first haircut, and put them back on the clippers, one side of the attachment didn't fully seat in its guide rail. The attachment was cock-eyed on the clippers, and the flimsiness of the attachments allowed the clipped blades just enough clearance to shave my head clean. Lesson learned - make sure your attachments are seated perfectly on both sides before cutting hair.

What I don't like:
-Not enough power if you like a fast haircut - a little too weak for my taste, much weaker then my cheap plug-in clippers (take it very slow and it works)
-Flimsy attachments (seriously Philips, WHAT WERE YOU THINKING, YOU'RE BETTER THEN THIS) - but so far they haven't broke
-Attachments can mistakenly be seated improperly on clippers (I have a new bald spot to prove it)
-Attachments adjust too easily (which means you'll go too short if not careful)

After writing this review, I think I've convinced myself to return these and obtain something better. I hope Amazon will take them back, or I'm stuck with these poor performers. Philips Norelco IS better then this. I imagine these were on the way to a great design but shoved into production prematurely. They really need to go back to the drawing board and perfect the design - they are SO CLOSE! But not close enough for this Amazon shopper.

Take my advice on this one, and look past this product. I'll definitely try another product on Amazon, and I wouldn't hesitate to try another Philips Norelco product.

***************************
UPDATE: SEPTEMBER 2012
***************************
I wrote my original review on this product in August 2011. I've now owned this product for a total of 1 year, 8 months.

Another Amazon shopper asked me for an alternative cordless hair clipper that I could recommend to them.

Based on my experience with this product, I replied with the following:
"I don't think I will be purchasing another cordless hair clipper. The batteries don't last long enough, and they just don't have the quality/power of the plug-in variety. Maybe in the future they will be better when lithium batteries become more common and cheaper. For now I'm going to save up for a professional Oster plug-in clipper (probably the OSTER Classic 76) as I'm tired of using cheap clippers, and I've saved so much money by cutting my own hair. Buying a higher end clipper will probably be the last time I have to buy clippers! Thanks for reading and replying to my review! "

Out of respect to Philips Norelco, I do have to admit that (almost 2 years later) I STILL use these clippers (albiet plugged in constantly); and they are still running and cutting my hair. So they haven't failed yet, and they are still saving me money.

With that said, I could definately be MORE satisfied with this product; but overall I'm still using them and have saved more money then these cost me in the first place. So thank you for that Philips Norelco.

I cannot, however, recommend this product to my fellow consumer. It's not even worth having this model on the market. Others will likely be disappointed in this product, and this could ruin Philips reputation.

title: Product works but could use improvement in the way it smells.
text:
I decided to try Lume because I hate the way my old deodorant cakes under my arms and embeds into my clothing. White clothing turns yellow and is quickly ruined. Darker clothes show the white residue as it has worked completely into the fabric. By the end of the day, a weird funk develops that's like a mixture of sweat and deodorant that's rather off-putting.

Lume does last the full day, but I wouldn't say it lasts 72 hours as advertised. The performance is satisfactory and it seems to solve the caking issue. The end of the day funk is less noticeable. So far it's a win.

My only complaint is the smell. There's a weird undertone that is a bit repulsive. The first time I tried it, I had to wash it off as the smell wouldn't go away. The second time I tried it, I used very little product. Drawing up maybe one millimeter of product. No more. The strange smell was much less noticeable and even went away fairly quickly. It still prevented body odor for a full day. So I think the trick to avoiding the underlying odor of, I am assuming, the active ingredient is to use very little product.

Ideally, we wouldn't have to deal with that smell at all. The product could use some improvement as a result.

title: Great...BUT Beware of Size Issues
text:
EDIT - I wrote the review below and then I realized that each page has it's specific style AND varied SIZES. I didn't realize this at first. This fact alone will lead me to not buy them again. It's common to mess up on ONE brow in a pair. Its nice to be able to go to your page and just cut off a new one and not worry if it's the same size as the others. I only like the bigger (longer) brows, so I won't even want to use half the brows on each page. Major issue for me. I'll leave the tips below, because if you don't care about size differences, maybe this info will help you.

1- They are overall amazing!
2- They take some practice, but it's worth it.
3- When I mess up, I remove them with alcohol and toilet tissue. I wet it with alcohol and rub with dry toilet tissue. The dry helps rub the transfer off. It's not super pleasant, but it works.
5- They last for me for two full days.
6- As crazy as it sounds, I followed the advice of someone here and shaved my (small) brows after trying to apply over my natural brows. I was very freaked out about shaving my brows, but my brows sucked anyhow and it improved the look of these by far!
7- My advice is to try all or almost all of the varieties sent in the package. It can't hurt to try, right?! Remember you can always remove them if you really can't stand them. Some of the ones that looked very odd on paper, looked not bad on me! Some look better on "natural" days and some look better with make-up. title: Easy Adjustment from Nonelectric
text:
Unlike others, my motivation for going with electric shaving was based on medicine. That is, I am so many different blood thinners that, no matter what shaving system I use, I managed to get at least a small cut or two and these would bleed and bleed, etc. So, it occurred to me to try an electric razor. I read the generally excellent reviews posted at this site--thanks to all of you guys for your input! I decided on this middle of the line Norelco. It's a couple of models from the bottom; the bottom one is cord only, the next one is cordless only, and then comes this model. I spent some time at the store looking over the different blade systems; even Norelco alone has several going. I knew I didn't want that squishy mess like the most expensive, and I was reluctant to sink a small fortune into something I might not like. What decided most of all for me to get this 'Reflex Plus' system was that it has a whisker collection chamber so they don't go all over the place. I think the model(s) above this have lithium ion batteries, whereas this model still has NiCads--which I hate. If I traveled more than I do, I'd spring for the model above for about $10 more. NiCads are slow to charge and are generally crummy; I've been using them in photo equipment for 30 years. This particular razor can be used just as easily plugged into the wall, which I like. I also like the fact that it doesn't require a separate charging stand, you just plug the cord into the bottom.

How did it shave? Great for me. I'm blond with a fairly soft beard and it plowed through about 3 days' worth of beard, making a chopping sound the whole time. I felt an occasional 'pull' but then this was fairly long beard. Once the long hair was gone I found it quite smooth to shave with. I bought some 'Lectric Shave' at the store at the same time I bought the razor but I didn't use it. Having fairly light-colored hair on my face, I never have the Fred Flintstone look regardless. I found, though, that the razor certainly got my beard acceptably close. I can still feel hair on my face, but not to an unacceptable degree. I have usually used a German Mercury double-edge razor with Wilkinson Sword blades and this doesn't shave that close. It might do better or different with another's beard. As for me, I'm delighted, and it didn't cut me at all. I'm in my forties, so don't have any deep wrinkles, etc., to cut through. That might be different.

Unlike some of the other razors I looked at, this model is light to hold and not bulky. Some of the other, more expensive models seemed both huge and heavy. I wasn't willing to mess with that. Having only used this a couple of weeks, I can't speak to the long-term durability. Seems appropriate to the price, though. I don't think it'll cost me particularly more than blades and shave gel in the long run. It is very quiet. I am looking forward to many more pleasant shaves!

title: Reliable product from a great company!
text:
I came to Amazon looking for a replacement comb for this trimmer. No fault of Remington, my trimmer is 3+ years old and has suffered more than one drop to the floor. The adjustable comb isn't made of titanium and you can expect to eventually break anything that is small and made of plastic.

A Remington rep saw my inquiry and asked me to contact them at the customer support email. I sent them an email and they called me the next day. After providing basic information, my rep said he would send me a replacement for free. The replacement arrived today ( 06/02/22 ) and not only did he send me the comb, he sent 2 other models just to make sure that I would have the right one for my trimmer. I don't know about you, but where I come from that's called "excellent customer service".

The CEO of Remington used to do a lot of commercials for the company and his famous tag line was, "I liked it so much, I bought the company"( ! ) He was an old school American entrepreneur who understood how valuable happy customers and word of mouth were to attaining and keeping success. It's good to see that his way of doing business lives on at Remington.

My trimmer is 3 years old. Remington was under ZERO obligation to do what they did for me. And yet, they did. If you have an issue with the product or ANY product, take the time to reach out to the company. Put the ball in THEIR court and give them a chance to make things right.

Thanks,

-J.

title: Fun to Use!
text:
My daughter and I discovered facial sheet masks over the summer and have become fans of them. They are easy and fun to use. This box of Anti-Aging sheet masks comes with 5 masks. Each mask is individually wrapped. When you open up a mask and remove it from the packing, you see that there are 2 layers. One is the sheet mask which is thin and papery like. The other is a plastic type material. The two layers are together, so I put both of them on my face. The other masks that I have used didn't have this plastic layer. I couldn't get it to lay flat on my skin very well, so I peeled the plastic layer off leaving just the paper one. This was what I was more familiar with. That layer was easy to mold to my face. The mask was very cold which felt refreshing. It's very wet - not to the point of dripping off my face, but enough that you want to spread it around more on the mask as it is on your face. It says to leave it on for 15-20 minutes. I opted for the lesser time because my coffee was ready & I didn't want to wait any longer for it! Then you are supposed to rub any left over "goo" (for a lack of a better word) into you skin. I accidently got a little into my eye, but it didn't burn or sting at all, which surprised me. I have very sensitive eyes and was expecting to feel some pain. I regularly use anti-aging products, plus I have only used one of these sheet masks so far, so I don't notice any difference to my skin, but I would definitely add this to my beauty routine.

*I purchased these masks at a reduced price for the purpose of trying out & reviewing. My thoughts & opinions are my own.

title: It's not 100% human hair
text: So when you first receive this hair, it's super soft and smooth, but after about a week you can tell it's not real human hair.  I think this hair would work really well if you were maybe getting married or something and you put it in the day before the wedding. The hair would still feel nice maybe through a week long honeymoon. After that the hair starts to get really frizzy and has major breakage.  The hair becomes really dry and because it isn't real human hair, no amount of moisturizer will help because the synthetic hair doesn't absorb it at all. I'd like to point out that I've used extensions for years. I have a pair of clip in Remy extensions that are over 8 years old and still in amazing condition. I was able to get about a month of wear out of these before I had to take them out because they were driving me crazy. The tape they use is amazing.  It's almost over the top as the tape outlasts the hair. If you are looking for something long term, I wouldn't recommend this hair.  If you want something that is going to last you for 6 months to a year- you have to get 100% real Remy human hair.  I got a month out of these using every trick I know and they were still a mess by the time I took them out.  But if ur looking to use these for an event or short term, it will save u some $$ to use these. Just be prepared to fight to get the tape out! Oh and try to not wash your hair...like at all....if you can.  Once whatever they put on the hair to make them so soft washes off the hair, it's all bad from there!  Good luck!

So these are good in that they hold fine hair very well, but with that grip, as others have stated, comes the unenviable task of getting it out of the hair. You can roll it out, however that will wind any wayward hairs around it and result in a yank.

If anyone should use this, I would recommend it for someone with very fine, straight hair, not prone to any type of flyaways. Also, you'll want to make sure that you flatten down any frizz or flyaways before rolling it out over the pony. It can be done, but I'm not sure it's worth all the effort and toil.

I put it into my daughter's hair wet, with a silicone serum in it overnight. Even though her hair was sleek and still in the pony completely, the removal was problematic. I am sticking with the grippy Goody pony holders, although I am curious if they'll make design improvements, because there is potential. Her pony held well and it was super easy to put it in.

title: Water seal and battery experience
text:
I have been using this brush now since Approximately November 1, 2010. I use it every night but not in the mornings and am totally pleased with it. Two thoughts might be helpful for those reading about problems with the water seal on the bottom of the handle and battery usage.

1)I was flabbergasted once I started using the brush by the comments of those who had trouble with the water seal. I suspect there are two types of brush users. Those like myself who keep their lips closed while brushing and therefore have no water drip down the brush whatsoever. And then I suppose there must be people who brush their teeth with their moth open and the brush handle pointed down and let water and saliva and paste drool down the handle. I suppose it would be possible to get moisture to the bottom cap of the battery compartment is you did this regularly and perhaps some moisture could get in. Or perhaps if you rinsed the brush but also rinsed the whole handle you could get moisture in.

So if when you brush your entire handle does not regularly get wet, then this complaint about the water seal will have no effect on you.

2) My experience with battery usage has been that the two AA batteries supplied with the unit lasted from 11/2/2010 until 1/16/2011 being used once a night for two minutes. Two rechargeable NiMH batteries are still going strong as of today 3/6/2011 with the same usage rate.

The brush head is still in fine condition and not splayed out.

I hope this helps folks trying to decide on this unit. Seems ridiculous to pay for a more expensive model that is virtually the same but with unneeded "features"

ADDED COMMENTS AS OF 6/5/2012: My and my wife's brushes are still going strong with no signs of fatigue, breakdown, or water seal problems. We continue to use NiMH rechargeable batteries and get months of use out of a charge. I just came back from my dentist today and they have noticed an obvious improvement in my gum health. I will be ordering another one to use in another bathroom which will be more convenient for morning brushing before leaving for work. Great product and great price savings over the unnecessary added "features" of th higher priced models!

title: Confusing marketing.....
text:
The seller really should change their description of this hair dryer.

First, the pictures make it look as if you can use the concentrators in either the vertical or horizontal position and this isn't true at all. In the horizontal position, the concentrator will fall off because it will not lock.....see promotion picture and my uploaded photo.

****This may not seem like a big deal until you start using it and have to adjust the direction with your wrist.****

Second, the description states the wattage is between 1800 to 2000 but the label says 1800 watts only....see description paragraph and my uploaded photo.

While the blow dryer is cute and an obvious design copy from the Dyson blow dryer (seems China has been copying Dyson these days but can't match the superior quality of Dyson), it's kinda heavy and gets too hot, even on the medium heat setting. I had to turn on the cool shot to offset the heat.

If you have hand arthritis, carpal tunnel, shoulder arthritis, etc, this will give you some trouble due to the heaviness, along with the inability to switch the concentrator into the horizontal position.

2 star deduction for the deceptive advertising, lack of concentrator versatility and heaviness.

title: Palm oil - pore clogging - failed applicator
text:
Not so good: Tube design failed, pore clogging, not 2-in-1
Good: color
Unknown: lasting?

I was glad I read a few reviews before I opened it, then I opened it carefully, pushed gently, and it burst out the sides all the same. I wasn't sure if it was because the on/off was marked on the lid but not the tube, maybe I just turned it the wrong amount? ½ turn seemed reasonable, so I turned it tighter and more came out the sides. For what it's worth, the instructions just have us dabbing a couple dots on with the sponge and blending with the fingers or brush. The sponge is an entirely unnecessary addition.

As you can see from the photo, this did allow me to put a nice and thick layer on my arm just in case anyone is looking to see how dramatic it can be. I do like the color, it's a good match, but I wouldn't use it on my eyes or my lips because the product says 'liquid blush.' There is a graphic on this page that says 2-in-1, despite showing eyes/blush/lips on the very same graphic, which I am pretty sure would be 3-in-1.

The last issue is the ingredients. The top ingredient is Ethylhexyl Palmitate, which is a pretty well known comedogenic (pore clogging) problem, so it's not great if you have breakouts. That's why I don't know how long it lasts or well it holds up over time, it's not worth the high risk of breakouts so I didn't wear it long. You might have guessed that 'palmitate' is also a derivative of Palm Oil, which is an industry that is destroying many biodiverse forests.

Two stars for color, texture feels nice, but I would only recommend this to people with clear skin that don't really have any desire to use the applicator sponge.

title: My Mustache speaks for itself.
text:
This wax is my go to wax for my mustache. I have a thinner mustache with thin tips and this holds beautiful curls all day long as long as you don't get it wet. It will hold up to my dog's occasional kiss, but anything more, like rain, and they will fall apart immediately. With this said it makes it really easy to clean up at the end of the day. It does tend to leave droplets on the sink, but they wipe off with a damp rag.

This wax does have a dye in it, and it does cover the few greys i have in my mustache. The brown was too dark, this seems to blend a bit better and look more natural with my brown facial hair.

I have attached 2 photos so you can see the length of the mustache and the normal size of my everyday curls. If I am dressing up I will take the time to make larger curls, but they are more delicate and don't hold as long.

I find this to be super easy to keep with me, as you may find throughout the day that you may have to touch up your mustache for various reasons. The tube makes it extremely simple to do so.

With that said you do need to have water with you when you do the mustache as if you use your finger, which you will have to do to get curls, you will have to apply it with your fingers and they will be covered in the dye.

The dye is not permanent and has never stained any of my clothing.

There is a slight odor to the wax, but it's no stronger than some of the high end waxes I have tried. I continue to came back to this wax for it's simplicity and ease of use.

I'm not sure if this just wasn't product tested with the shower actually on or if my product is defective. "suction cup bottom grips to any floor." The suction cups are a great idea for a shower product, but do they work on this one? ABSOLUTELY NOT. I don't know whose idea it was, but I would like to see someone actually cup this thing in the shower, put some soap in there, turn the water on and use it without having to superglue it to the floor.

It absolutely does not stay in one place no matter how light you try to get your foot in there. And I don't know why the pumice stone is there at the heel because you're lucky if you even get your arch in before it starts sliding away. I literally almost fell and broke my ankle the first time I tried to use this because I went into it thinking the suction cups would work. So just be warned, you need something sturdy to hold on to while using this product.

Another problem is the over-the-foot plastic. Why plastic?? If i'm not water skating through the shower on this thing and actually get my foot in all the way, that plastic hits the top of your foot and it's painful. I get the whole car wash appeal it looks like they're going for but that plastic needs to be made out of a softer material.

Since i'm assuming the paying customers are the only product testers in this case, I found it easiest to use one foot to hold the product down by stepping on the pumice stone and one foot doing a combined up/down left/right motion inside the "foot wash" while holding onto the shower rod with both hands. This did crack my pumice stone after 2 uses but at least it wasn't my back.

So as far as likelihood I would recommend this to a friend to use for its intended purpose, I would have to take a hard pass.

title: It only made my hair a little softer....
text:
I bought this at Sally Beauty. I am caucasion, in my 50's with blonde/gray fine hair that is straight with some body & has never been colored or bleached; length is 2" below my shoulders.
My hair has been very dry for a long time despite lots of moisturizing, a salon keratin treatment (cha-ching!), argon oil, deep conditioning, etc... This Aphogee two-step protein treatment was recommended to me at the Sally Beauty store, and I figured it was worth a try. I followed the instructions to a T & also watched lots of youtube videos. I used this today exactly as directed & with high hopes. I shampooed & towel-dried my hair, then applied protein treatment, blow dried my hair for 12 minutes w/ the protein treatment in it, then rinsed in shower with warm water followed by the balancing moisturizer for at least 2 minutes, rinsed & used a moisturizing hair mask ("Mystic Divine" Coconut Complex Hydrating Masque), then rinsed again. My hair felt softer, at first, but my frizzies & curly gray hairs are still sticking out all over. I didn't get any more body in my hair either (my keratin treatment was last year 2017). So, all in all it is okay as a moisturizer, but no better than a regular deep moisture conditioner or mask. I'm not sure if I would use it again, maybe. I'm glad I just got the sampler size.
Here are my tips:
1) Use a spray mister bottle for the protein liquid & make sure you get out every last drop from the packet because most of it came out as beer colored water, then at the bottom of the packet was more of a thick cream, so I shook them together in the spray bottle & I'm so glad I used that! Don't just pour it on your head, at the very least pour a little into your hands at a time (after massaging the packet to mix contents) and smooth through your hair that way. There was just enough for my hair length.
2) Don't put a towel or anything around your shoulders, no clothing either because the protein treatment will dry your hair to it. Don't pull your stuck hairs off your skin, they'll come unattached in the shower, no worries. I kept my hair behind me to apply treatment & blow dry.
3) After drying the protein into your hair, don't touch your hair or bend it, (you can very gently touch lightly with your finger, if you hair wasn't already super brittle; it will feel like plastic sort of. 4) Be very careful blow-drying; I pointed the dryer downward alternating between medium & high heat & kept it farther from my hair so it wasn't blowing it around as it hardened. When hair is totally hard & dried through then gently let the shower water fall over all of your hair until you feel no more stiffness, then you can condition.
It's worth a try! The packets were just under $4 at Sally Beauty if you want to try it, or order here on Amazon.

title: DO NOT BUY!!!!
text:
Like others have mentioned, I’ve used this body spray for about 23 years, so an extremely long time. I know exactly what it is supposed to smell like..VANILLA.
I purchased 2 bottles, sprayed some on me, and was immediately wondering what the hell was this scent?!
I actually thought it was me!

It’s not that the company added more alcohol, they actually changed the entire formula.
There’s not even a hint of vanilla; it’s a mix of old, expired, rancid perfume blended with fermented flowers.. Absolutely horrible!!
So if you think you’re going to be the special one that doesn’t get a bad bath like the rest of us, I’ll tell you now that it’s not going to happen.
The company reformulated it completely and trashed a product that made them money for years.
So, like the rest of us, I’m sadly searching for a comparative replacement. Not holding my breath, though.
Such a shame when companies decide to do this, which is usually a way to market their other, new products.
Well, lo and behold, I just walked into the big chain store and there sits about 10 new fragrances from Body Fantasies..
This company thinks they can take away one and we will automatically just settle for another of theirs.
Nice move, but the people that want vanilla aren’t going to waste money on “Lilac” or “Pomegranate”

title: good for the length, bad for the quality
text:
The good:

These fit my Wahl clippers just right.

The lengths are perfect for what I am personally looking for, with leaving the top of my hair longer than the sides. Obviously check the lengths of these for what you'd want your hair to be at. I cut my own hair so these work perfect for what I want.

The comb is fine to be added in, but I feel like if you already have Wahl clippers, you probably should already have a comb. But it's a neat addition.

The bad:

The shorter guide is white, so the picture is misleading. Yes it is just a color, but some people don't like being misled. The comb is also a weird ugly orange color, yet again, different from the picture.

The worst thing about these clippers is that the guides are long, yes, and VERY FLIMSY. This is where the product can be iffy because I feel like they'll break, or the comb part on the guides will bend and cut my hair wrong or have it cut a big chunk out.

You have to cut your hair very lightly with these combs or else if you push to hard, they will bend and cut at an uneven length. I don't get why they couldn't somehow make the product where it's either more supportive for the comb parts on the guide, or just use a more sturdy material so it doesn't bend putting little pressure on it.

Overall, if you really need these lengths, try to look elsewhere first, if there aren't many others, then these would be fine to get. Just be very careful using these, or find some way to support the guide combs so they don't bend.

They do seem a bit on the pricey side for a poorly made cheap piece of plastic, but I needed to get them for my hair lengths.

title: I wish I owned the factory that makes these things...
text:
This is a factory replacement part for several models of Braun shavers, so it fits perfectly, and it works just like the original part.

The bad news is the price. You'll hold it in your hand and say, "How could this thing cost $30!?" Well, it just does; if you want the factory part, you have to pay the factory price. There is no after-market replacement.

Do you even need to replace the cutter assembly? Probably so. Obviously, if you dent the original by fumbling your shaver, you'll need a replacement. However, even with perfect care, the original cutter wears out in about 18 months. If you pop the foil cover off of your shaver, you can see why: The blades run back and forth against the foil cover, shearing off the whiskers that have protruded into the tiny holes and slots. Eighteen months of friction does the damage.

So, if you want the Braun shaver-- which, by the way is excellent-- then you just have to buy the parts needed to do the periodic maintenance. Life is like that sometimes...

title: Side by side comparison of three sleep masks-Earth Theraputics is no longer my favorite
text:
This is a side-by-side comparison of three masks:
[[ASIN:B001ET7HJI Earth Therapeutics Mind/Body Therapy Sleep Mask, Cotton, Silk]]
[[ASIN:B00FJQFJX8 Bedtime Bliss® Contoured & Comfortable Sleep Mask & Moldex® Ear Plugs]]
[[ASIN:B00M9BC1M8 Premium Quality Eye Mask with Contoured Shape By Nidra]]

I've used the Earth Therapeutics soft mask for five years, and the the Nidra and Bedtime Bliss masks for the last several months. All have their advantages and disadvantages. My favorite is now the Nidra mask, but it has an important flaw.

I sleep from after midnight until 8am, and my bedroom is bright. Therefore, I need a mask that will stay on for seven or eight hours. If it shifts when I move during the night, it will not be covering my eyes when the sun comes up.

Although I used it for several years, the Earth Therapeutics mask does the worst job of staying in place all night. I think this is because it does not have as much shape or structure as the other two masks. Also, it presses on your eyes, making it a bit less comfortable than the other two masks. I no longer use this mask.

The Nidra mask does the best job of staying in place. It is also slightly larger than the Bedtime Bliss mask, and feels a bit more comfortable. However, the Nidra has a flaw: Although they all have the same length band, the elastic on the Nidra band has a bit more tension than the Bedtime Bliss or the Earth Therapeutics masks, which means that it is too tight on my fat head. I have actually had to extend the strap with a piece of dual-sided velcro strap in order to make it comfortable. Now it fits the best and stays in place better than the other two masks.

The Nidra mask is about 3/4 inch or 2cm wider across the eyes than the Bedtime Bliss mask. If you have a small or narrow face, you may want to try the Bedtime Bliss mask first

As far as light blocking and comfort go, both the Nidra and the Bedtime Bliss do a good job. Therefore, my choice is the Nidra because it stays on better after I make the strap longer.

Summary: I have stopped using the Earth Therapeutics mask. The Bedtime Bliss and Nidra are very similar, but the Nidra fits me better and stays in place longer. If you have a large head like me, the Nidra mask will be tight. If you have a small or narrow face, try Bedtime Bliss.

title: Slow process, but good results
text:
I was nervous about getting this. There are SO MANY models and brands and reviews out there that I finally decided on one that was within my price range to try, but also had decent reviews. I've had this now for about 4 months and have not had any re-growth of the hairs I've taken out. That's what I was looking for - lasting results. That being said, it is tricky to get used to doing this. It's best if you have someone doing it for you. There are a couple of things to keep in mind: 1. You go one hair at a time, and each one took me about 3-4 minutes, and the instructions say not to do more than a square inch of skin at a time. So depending on how much of an area you want to do, and how dense the hair is it may take months and months to clear a significant area, and that's if you do it every other day. 2.) You will have unsightly sores. You are penetrating your epidermis and electrocuting the hair follicle, so you will get a scab on each pore you zap. I used the Tea Tree lotion they recommend on Amazon and it seemed to work fine. I don't know if it would have been the same without the oil. My scabs were there the same amount of time any other scab I've had has been on me - about a week.

So it's slow going and leaves scabs, but once the scabs went away my hair has not come back at all. It's been great that way! I'm really glad I bought it. The reasons I didn't give five stars is because it said, "Clean and Easy". It's not easy, and when something leaves you scabbed over, that doesn't scream "clean" to me. The other reason is because I had to zap each follicle twice on the highest setting before it worked. But I gave it four stars because it did work! So for the price, and once you get used to it, and if you have a way to hide the scabs for a week, then it's great. I'm happy with the results, which for me is the bottom line.

text: This is my first time using moringa oil. I find it to be a bit heavy (so will probably use it more in the Winter for an all over moisturizer). As another reviewer mentioned, it does smell like "pizza spices" - oregano specifically, which is a bit off-putting at first but does go away in a few minutes after application. I had bought it to help with my Summertime acne-prone skin, so I then tried to use it as a spot treatment. It didn't seem to help. It seemed to make my face oily. I did test it to see if it was real by placing it in the fridge and it did solidify, which is a good sign of it's authenticity. It states that it is organic in the title, but does not state it on the bottle or box packaging anywhere. This seems to be a growing trend on Amazon lately...products will state they are organic (specifically facial oils) and when you receive them, there is no certification on the product. Pretty misleading. I have used this on burns and a couple rashes and it worked quickly and effectively. I will try mixing this oil with jojoba this Winter for extra moisturizing, but really don't expect it to work to on my acne-prone skin. Meh!

text:
This is a very thin, clear oil. It isn’t as thick as baby oil and runs almost like water. I would never put oil or an oil-based product on my skin because it clogs the pores. Some people might be able to get away with it, but even though I have dry skin, my skin will break out if I put oil on it, so I have skipped that test. I did rub it into my hands and it dries fast without leaving an oily slick.

title: Leaked Out
text:
I was excited to get my package today...but was quickly disappointed when I discovered that the toner had leaked all over the box and half of it was already missing.

NOTE: nothing in this box was sealed! The box itself wasn’t even sealed. The opening you see in the photo is literally a hole in the box (no plastic film) and none of the bottles had any kind of sealant or plastic wrap to prevent the lids from coming loose or the products from being tampered with. I suspect this is why the toner leaked out everywhere.

That being said, I tried out the products tonight and was highly impressed with the emulsion and the face cream. Both are heavy and rich and super moisturizing. A little goes a long way with the face cream as well so I think that tiny container will actually last for quite a while. The toner and essence were okay, but didn’t leave enough of an impact to really form any kind of first impression about them. I could honestly see myself buying larger versions of the emulsion and face cream though!

Despite my love for the emulsion, I had some difficulty getting it out of the container. It didn’t have a pump on it like the essence did and is of such a thick consistency that I was literally banging the bottle on the palm of my hand trying to use gravity to force it out.

All in all, the products are okay but the packaging and bottle style aren’t exactly top notch. I’m not fond of receiving unsealed products.

title: A good toothbrush and a good price
text:
I bought this toothbrush because of all the statistics singing the praises of electric toothbrushes. I thought that this head looked particularly effective, so I placed my order.
This is a great toothbrush. Some people have complained about the head size, but that's practically an Oral B trademark, and after a week or so you don't even notice. The toothbrush itself is pretty intense. It might hurt your gums the first time you use it. It is fast and powerful and it really gets the job done. The battery will last almost a week without charging, but after a few days you start to steadily lose power. I recommend keeping it charged most of the time. It's not particularly loud for a brush of its kind, but it does make some noise.
My only complaint: the vibrations sometimes bother my lips and/or nose. It's not as noticeable after awhile, but it's a bit annoying at first. Still, that's not really the toothbrush's fault. It can't help being that intense.
A final comment: Don't listen to some of the negative comments. A lot of them happened because the person didn't read the instructions before use. If used properly, the brush is a huge improvement over a manual. I think my dentist will appreciate it. Five stars.

title: caution
text:
T970 is miles away from its predecessor(s) (I also own a T7500 Deluxe) as far as the feature set goes. It boasts a charge level indicator, incorporated vacuum, and fast 15-minute charging time. However, I don't know what was in the mind of the industrial designers who came up with this latest installment from Norelco/Philips other than capitalize on the truck craze that's taken such a powerful hold on us. Indeed, I wish all those miles were for the right reason. Let me explain:

I view the newly added vacuum function adding only marginal benefit to this unit, at the expense of draining battery power fast, noise making, and increased diameter size. With T7500, all one had to do was to charge the trimmer every other 15th use or so, and undo a couple of things to clean it after each use. Also, T7500 was smaller, it fit well in your hand and/or travel pouch, and could be charged at 110V-240V. Now, T970 requires a recharge every 3rd use or so, and it's so much harder to fit in you hand and/or in your travel bag since it has a larger diameter and comes with a power adaptor that works only at 110V. Cleaning T970 is akin to undoing a Matrioshka, the Russian nesting doll.

Thinking more about it, I came to the conclusion that T970 wasn't put together by industrial designers but some marketing types... For these guys I would venture to suggest that they should keep T7500 on the market; it would serve very well the traveller types, whereas its successor would be for stay-at-home folks.

Considering it sells at a discount and it comes with a 60-day return period, I am able to rate it cautiously at 3 stars.

I think my natural hair is too long for it to work like I wanted it too. I have armpit length hair and it is difficult to get my hair to stand on end. title: From mortified to 'hip'
text:
I have been using Odaban for at least 5 years for excessive underarm perspiration. For most of my life, I had to wear carefully selected shirts and blouses to disguise perspiration stains that reached down to my waist. On excessively hot days, I held my arms out slightly so that the dampness did not touch my clothing, leading to muscular aches and pains. I actually turned down a job offer because it required wearing a blouse that would show dark stains. Teaching middle school students was quite a trial, since they noticed and commenedt on my excessive sweating.
The first four days, I applied Odaban every night. Then it began to work. I reduced the amount I used it to once a week without issue. At this point, I often go 2-3 weeks before I need re-application. It may feel at times like you are perspiring because it feels cooler on the affected area, but a touch test confirms that there is absolutely no moisture.
Perhaps the most wonderful effect is that I can wear whatever I want. Tight long-sleeved T-shirts were always a distant dream for me. Now I wear them in every color of the rainbow. Nobody knows my secret (but you).
Of late, I'm applying it around my hairline with similar success. In the California summers I often work outside in extreme heat and drip sweat in rivers under my hairline. The sweat gets into my hair and is hard to brush out when it dries. No more.
Had it not been for Odaban, it's likely I would have quit teaching. I wanted to hide myself away. Now I have the distinction of being considered a cool dresser by 8th grade students who regularly compliment this 64 year old lady about her hip clothing choices. And the little wardrobe I once had is now busting at the seams.
Odaban is a lifesaver.
Maritza

Braun's competitively priced electric powered toothbrushes are very good values and reliable performers. Most models use the same rotating type replacement toothbrush heads.

Both Braun models will do a good job, however the faster more powerful Vitality, will probably get more done in the same amount of time. title: Dentist recommended, patient approved
text:
Very pleased with this water flosser. My dentist has recommended a water flosser to me for quite some time, but I had been delaying purchasing one due to the cost. I opted for this H2ofloss water flosser for the ease of use (portability, with the small water repository) and better cost compared to other models.

PROS:
- Shipped quickly
- Multiple flosser heads for different needs
- Easy to use (charging, filling water repository, attaching different heads)
- I feel a difference, especially on my gums. Using the water flosser feels like a gum massage, which makes me feel like I'm combating gingivitis by using this.

CONS:
- Water sprays a lot, which I knew beforehand. I stick my head into the shower to use this so I don't get water everywhere.
- Water repository needs to be refilled a couple of times per flossing session (one fill lasts ~30 seconds)
- Staccato irrigation rather than steady stream. Unsure if all water flossers are like this, but it wasn't exactly what I was expecting.

Overall, really glad I finally got a water flosser, and am looking forward to feedback from my dentist.

Unfortunately, the product makes me break out. I am not a huge fan of lavender oil for the face given possible sun sensitivity (I have pigmentation) hormone disruption and general irritation from essential oils. I personally like the scent, but like some, I found it strong at first.

I'm using it as an eye make up remover now, since it irritates the skin on my face within a few days of each use. NOTE, I have sensitive skin, so not everyone will have the reaction I did. With that said, not every product I use causes break-outs.

Seems like a great Micellar water for those who like the ingredients and the scent of lavender, because it does clean the skin well.

title: A Good One-off Cosplay or Party Wig
text:
This wig has a beautiful ombre--one colour blends into the next very nicely without a harsh line. There is a lot of and it's thick, though not overly so. It came packaged with a cute flower garland headband and a lace stocking cap.

The wig cap itself is adjustable in the back, however, it doesn't have any hooks/combs in the top or sides to secure it--not a problem, since it's easy enough to use a few strategically placed bobby pins. Also, if you have a large head or a lot of hair, getting this wig to fit might be too much of a struggle. (I had to braid my hair and wrap it a certain way around my scalp to get it flat enough to fit in this wig.) Finally, it's shiny to the point of looking synthetic--dry shampoo helped a great deal toward correcting that--and the part in the center is crazy wide.

Considering the price point, I would have awarded this wig the full five stars if those had been the only quibbles. However, it sheds like a Pomeranian and tangles like a kudzu. The shedding goes far beyond your typical wig shed--and you know it's a problem when you get up from a seat and see strands of hair clinging to the seat--and then there's the tangling which can't be undone with a quick pull-through with your fingers--I'm talking fairy knots galore.

Now, this isn't a bad wig, which is why I didn't go lower on the stars. In fact, it would be a great one-off or once-in-a-blue-moon cosplay or party wig. But if you're looking for something more substantial, for daily wear, or a serious event, then another wig might be in order.

title: Not suitable for thick and wavy hair
text:
I really loved the idea of this hair straightener brush, so I decided to give it a try. I straighten my hair just about every day and I have long, thick and naturally wavy hair. I am always on the hunt for easier and quicker way to do my hair. Ultimately, I am hoping to save some time off my busy morning routine because every minute counts. This brush heats up quickly and it is safer than flat irons simply because there is a lower chance of burning myself. However, I find this tool a little too heavy for me to handle and it is quite impossible for me not to touch those three buttons on the side of the device switching the temperature up and down while working on my hair. It leaves my hair fluffy and does not do a great job straightening the roots because there is only so close I can get to my head. I have to section my hair piece by piece just like I do with a flat iron and it does not get all the frizz out as well as a flat iron. It turns out that I spend more time than my regular straightener trying to get the job done. Sadly, this brush works fine but not as well as my flat iron and not like I have imagined.

I admit that this device is not only well made and very sturdy, it is also of high quality and attention to details. I really want to love this product, but I don't think it lives up to the claim that it straightens my hair fully. I will say that it does straighten to certain degree and does a decent job of taming some frizz, but nowhere near in comparison to what I would get from a straightening iron. On top of that, it does not do a good job at straightening my bangs. In fact, it is too large to reach the roots. Every time I stroke my hair to straighten I hit the button and it turns it off. It will take some serious practices to get used to. Regardless, this is a good product for second day straight hair where I just need a touch up or if my hair is already partially straight. I think this straightener would be great for someone who does not have very thick hair like I do. My hair certainly looks less wavy and perhaps slightly less frizzy, but this tool does not straighten hair for the silky effect that I hope it will achieve. Since everyone has different texture of hair, I strongly believe this will work great for those who have thinner, tamer hair or simply using this brush as a touch-up tool.

title: Orly Color Amp'd is IT!
text: Color me PLEASED!! After having my nails done with gel at the salon, damage to my nails not to mention damage to my pocketbook as well, I have been on the hunt for the perfect polish for an at home manicure. The polish needed to be lush, vibrant, easy to apply, fast drying and resilient. I know, I know, asking too much??  Orly Color Amp'd fit the bill perfectly.  A nice palette of colors ranging from pastels to dark and rich. The polish feels somewhat silky, very easy to apply. The brush is amazing! It is contoured to the shape of a nature nail with a nice curve at the tip so you can get in close to the cuticle without a lot of maneuvering. It is a thicker brush which fans out nicely and allows the brush to hold enough polish to paint a nail without having to go back to the bottle. The directions suggest waiting 8 minutes to allow the polish to dry which I do between each coat. Once the clear coat (make sure you buy the Orly Color Amp'd topcoat!) dries, I am off and running. No nicks, smudges...nothing. Every couple of days I swipe a coat of the topcoat on and my manicure can last 10 days. And, I am not a princess; I am cooking, cleaning, gardening and this polish holds up. One IMPORTANT note: the first time I used it, no basecoat ( basecoat is in the polish itself), two coat of color and the topcoat. Next day....chips!! ARGH. I went to Orly's website and found the answer. Alcohol. Yep, swipe your nails with alcohol before you polish, even if you just used remover and washed your hands. USE ALCOHOL. Works like a charm! Now what are you going to do with the extra time you have from not going to the salon??

title: Changes in their ingredients list, added other junk
text:
Using my husbands account.

I've purchased this product around spring '18 used it and it was amazing, talk about hair feeling soft as butter. I mean your fingers, comb, brush or whatever you use will go straight through your hair with ease. I left it in for about a couple hours since I've haven't had a protein treatment in years. But THAT'S how soft, silky smooth it was from root to tip after my first use.

From protein treatments I reviewed and talking to hairstylist I understood that I should use it 1x every 6 weeks but it's truly based off your hair needs. So I decided 1x a month was ok for mine at this point. I purchased and used again in July '18 with similar results but not as silky because I cut the time it set in my hair to a little over 30 mins. Mainly because I didnt want it that soft because my hair is fine but curly, coily and straighten it was like baby hair all over my head although my hair is bra strap length.

I purchased 2 more packs in Aug '18 and noticed the packaging was slightly different. Instead of saying "made with natural coconut oil and monoi" it now reads "made with FAIR TRADE coconut oil and monoi". I then compared them together and noticed it no longer says "Made with natural Vitamin E (Tocopherol)" above the ingredients list either. I continued to read the ingredients list and a couple things have been removed which are: Helianthus Annuus (Sunflower) seed oil and whats been added in its place is Tocopheryl Acetate, down the list these other ingredients have been simply added not replacing anything Leuconostoc/Raddish Root Ferment Filtrate, Dimethyl Stearamine.

I said that to say this, my hair personally loved the last ingredient list as it was, but this new list my hair is not okay with because it seems like it's more drying when applying on wet hair. Versus the last packages I used, they glided on and conditioned my hair along with giving it protein. So if I cant find the original ingredients and packaging I'm gonna have to discontinue supporting this product and brand. It was the only thing from palmers that I've used in years. And I told the world (everyone I know) how great it was, bought and gave some out but no more after this.

I don’t feel like I was sweating any less than would be normal and I was having to pat myself down with a towel constantly when I wasn’t onstage.  Also of note, the setting spray is meant to be cooling, which all setting sprays are, but is also meant to almost eliminate sweating.  I reapplied the setting spray several times just to cool off.  Still. HOWEVER… at the end of the night, despite sweating and blotting with a towel constantly, I was the only cast member who didn’t look a mess.  It definitely worked far beyond what I think setting spray alone would have done.  I’ve never used the mehron setting spray that but I’ve never had a setting spray of any brand work to THAT degree.  Stage make up is heavy and it still looked pretty great.  After removing my make up, my skin wasn’t at all dry either.  I don’t know how moisturizing it was but for a product that’s meant to be an antiperspirant, it was definitely not drying in the least.  So I don’t feel like it actually inhibits sweating. It has a cool floral print with a lot of neem bark bits (I think so anyway?) that really help with exfoliation. The smell is a bit funky but it also is clear to me that it's only using neem and those essential oils listed, neem is a funky smell. I do feel like the feel was nice and it lathered and cleaned well.

However I think for the price the ingredients are kind of junky. You can see that they make a big deal about it having shea butter, etc, but that's way down on the list of ingredients. This is mainly a glycerin based soap with a harsh surfactant/foaming agent in it, Sodium Stearate, as well as a lot of other ingredients that I haven't seen in a long time in a natural soap bar. I didn't have a bad reaction to it and it doesn't have sulfates but I try to stay away from foaming agents and given the price I don't understand why they are trying to play both sides by acting like this is an "all natural" soap when it's a more traditional soap with shea butter, neem, and other stuff added. It's true though that glycerin based soaps can be less harsh on the skin but even the glycerin based soaps I've used don't have all these extra ingredients in them.

I don't think I'd buy this again, although my husband had no problem with it - check out Neem Tree Farms for legit neem soap.

text:
This is really a very unique travel/gift set. The items included truly make it handy when traveling and the items are not typically found bundled together. There are a few items that I really wanted. A) It has a glass nail file with a carrying case. This glass file is very nice and they last for such a long time that this item alone was worth the set. What I really like about a crystal/glass nail file is that you can clean and sanitize it. Besides maintaining its use for much longer periods than regular nail files, the fact that I can clean this is a huge bonus for me. B) The travel perfume atomizer. This is just fantastic for travel/storing in a small bag, etc... it is super simple to fill (fill from the bottom if you've never used one before and can be confusing at first) and there is no need to carry around a full bottle of my favorite perfume. There is a small window so that you can easily identify when it is time to refill. The tweezers set with a built in light is actually very nice. It is comfortable to hold/use and the light is useful. Now these may not end up being your "go-to" tweezers for eyebrow maintenance but they are a fairly good set. The make up brush is a good quality as well and stores away without leaving/getting make up in your purse. As someone that is not typically a fan of 'gift sets', I will say that this is a very nice set.The fact that the items are not typically seen bundled together, makes it one I would enjoy giving as a gift

I received this item at not cost for testing. All opinions are my own.

title: Weak power, weak massaging brush, doesn't pluck hairs from the root
text:
This is my first experience using an epilator, and I used this for my underarms.

Pros
-guidelight
-cordless
-can use under water
-easy to disassemble and clean
-nice cleaning tools and storage bag

Cons
-charge lasts 20-25 min at most, definitely NOT 40 min as advertised
-the power level starts off at a certain level (only requiring you to epilate over a given area once), then after 1-2 min it drops and you must epilate over the same areas over and over to remove hairs because the power level is so weak
-this only plucks about half of hairs from the root; it cuts the other half of hairs close to the surface
-this does NOT pluck hairs that are 0.5 mm in length; in fact it will cut many longer hairs and leave them at 0.5-1 mm, unable to remove them no matter how many times you run the epilator over them
-the massaging brush is too soft to exfoliate anything at all, better to use a loofah/manual brush

Overall:
This is an average epilator, definitely not worth $100. I might return this and get an Emjoi.

title: Great mirror. One small design flaw.
text: I love this mirror. I have used it for nearly three years and have been happy with it. When I first purchased it, i was planning to use the battery feature as i didn’t want another appliance that needed to be plugged in on my bathroom counter. But that battery feature is weak, the batteries run low quickly and the light is not as bright on battery power. Totally worth plugging it in for the brightness. The design flaw is in the rotation from magnified to unmagnified. You can rotate the mirror any direction and number of times you want. So, unless you are disciplined enough to only rotate the mirror 90 degrees one way and then back the opposite direction, you are effectively twisting the wires. We all know that if you twist wires enough they become faulty. Had the design included a stop on the rotation so that you could only rotate it one way and then back the other, it would reduce the chances of the wires twisting too much. Over the years I am sure I have twisted them a few too many times now so the light will sometimes flicker or become dim because those wires are weak and losing connection. One simple mechanism could have improved the longevity of this mirror.

title: Quit working after 12 days
text:
Worked for 12 days, but on the 12th day, when it ran out of water and I pushed to button to turn it off, it would not turn off. The Mode button also had ceased to work. After about a minute of me pushing buttons and shaking it, if quit and indicated the battery was exhausted. So much for going 30 days as advertised. I recharged it for about 6 hours until it glowed green indicating a full charge, and I disconnected the cord for charging and pressed the on button but nothing and it immediately indicated it needed to be recharged.

When it worked, I was not thrilled with it. It has three buttons in a row at the top, the top one being the one to release the little nozzle wand for want of a better term, the second one the on/off button and the third being the mode button. When you go to use it, and you decide to stop while it still has water in it, you need to turn it off while keeping the nozzle wand in your mouth so you don't shoot water everywhere but you cannot see the buttons so you just start pushing and maybe you will get lucky and hit the power button, but just as often, you will hit the mode button and it just starts working at a different pressure as you grope around. My solution was to not stop when I wanted to but keep going until it ran out, then pull it away from my face far enough to find the buttons and turn it off.

It is not practical to try to rotate the nozzle wand so is easier to use by just rotating the whole unit which means you lose track of where the buttons even are.

title: Fair for the money
text:
I got this on sale for a pretty good price back in 2007.

Part of the appeal was that it was, loosely, 'Air Force blue'. I'm a blade guy, when I can help it, but sometimes that isn't an option. Like those times when you're truly pinched for time in the morning or your schedule is so hectic you just can't fit a good blade shave in. There are definitely times during Wing Training Assemblies, given the duties I'm usually assigned, that that's the case.

Is this a substitute for a blade? No, not really. It's a substitute for not having shaved at all. That's considered unacceptable in uniform. This won't give you a really clean shave, but with it at least you did shave, whereas if all you had was a blade you'd sometimes have to skip it and hope no one important notices!

I've never replaced the cutter heads. Part of it is that I just never used this enough to worry about the prescribed interval. Thus, four years later, they're not worn out yet. However, Norelco HQ55+ replacements have disappeared from local retailers shelves where I live, so I'd have to order a set from a national retailer if I wanted to do so. In any case, the new heads cost as much or more than I paid for this thing in the first place, which was just shy of $30.

The trimmer works well enough. The cord stays put. The batteries haven't died yet - no batteries, no problem! This is a concern if you're getting it as a backup instead of regular use. It could sit most of the time for three or four years, you use it a handful of times, then the Ni-Cad or whatever rechargeable batteries your shaver uses die and you get to trashcan it just as if you'd used it daily. Not much value there, is there? This isn't exactly silent, but the noise level is tolerable.

You get what you pay for, friends!

title: Looks great, mediocre shave
text:
This was kind of a last ditch effort to find a more comfortable shaving experience. I've tried several electrics with the hope of finding a more comfortable shave since I have sensative skin and am prone to razor burn. At the end of the day, I've found frequently replacing the Mach3 blades is the best I can do. It gauls me to keep spending on money on something I have to toss, but it's better than the alternatives to date.

The Norelco Architec 1090 looks great and shaves better on the neck than the foil shavers I've tried including the Panasonic Nano and Braun Activator. However, it still misses a critical area in the middle cheek just along where a goatee would start to back about 1.5 inches from there. The hair in that part of my face tends to lay down. The Braun seemed to get that area OK, but did not do well in the neck area.

When I push harder to get those hard to get whiskers, I end up with road rash and sporadic ingrown whiskers. This and other electric razors may work with people who have different types of beards or face shapes, but I've yet to find an electric that works for my whole beard.

In my opinion, a $250 razor ought to do the job quite comfortably. I think there are better ways to use the funds, like on three years worth of blades and shaving cream.

The quality of this wig is decent and the texture is between soft and slightly course so if you have sensitive skin than beware. I know that some people can easily get a skin rash just off the texture of hair alone so I had to mention it. The length of the faux locs on the wig is a good length and you can easily do a high ponytail or a sloppy bun. The nape of this wig is a slight disappointment because they left out a big part of the net to the wig which is unusual but I would suggest you wear a head wrap if you wanna wear it up or leave some hair down so it won't show. The cap on this wig is very adjustable and very comfortable. Overall I'm pleased with what I paid and I will most definitely get my use out of it. The one thing I will say is be prepared to do some small tweeks to your likeness , I didn't like how there was a light brown lining around the edge of the lace so I used makeup to cover it as good as it could get and my baby hairs were too curly and long for me personally but it can be fixed. text:
When I first opened the jar, I groaned a little. Judging by the consistency of the product, I thought it was going to be more of a styling cream, than a conventional pomade. It felt too loose and watery.

I'm not really sure how, but this stuff changes dramatically when you apply it your hair. It firms right up and makes it very easy to put your hair in place and hold it there.

When it drys, it holds well. It's not as stiff as hair gel and has a little bit of flex, but it should hold up well, unless it's very, very windy outside.

A little bit goes a long way. I don't doubt that this jar will last a few months. Then again, I don't have a lot of hair.

There is not much of a scent and once it's applied, you won't notice it at all.

I'd say this is the best pomade I've found and even beats out American Crew in terms of quality and value.

title: Excellent product!
text:
When I first used this shaver there were a few things I had to learn. It's quiet -- so quiet, I thought it wasn't working properly. Second, you don't have to press hard to get it to work -- just keep passing it over any area of your skin requiring extra attention and it will do the job. Third, the lotion/gel samples make the shave live up to its name of Cool Skin -- no razor burn whatsoever.

I have two issues with the shaver. First, Norelco still has one of the most inconvenient methods of cleaning I've ever seen. Every few days you need to disassemble the blades from the discs holding them and using a brush (I use an old toothbrush) to get the old hair out of there. Rinsing it under water doesn't do anything but remove the stray hair stubble in the head itself.

Second, the refills are difficult to find. They are relatively expensive in most sources (including here at Amazon) but are available at the world's largest retailer in a box of 5 for $4.94. I find they last about 10 days if you don't go crazy pressing the button for lotion. I also find the lotion much better than the gel. When I shave at home, I just use regular shave gel with it to preserve the expensive cartridge-based lubricants.

text:
I've been wearing extensions for over 15 years- clip ins, tapes, Great Lengths, you name it. I've tried many different brands. I was very excited to try these- based on the reviews and the price. Let me tell you- save your $$. I purchased on the Canadian site where you can see my verified review but wanted to leave this here also to save other people from my misfortune.

When they arrived, the hair looked beautiful. It was healthy and shiny looking. I ordered 4 bundles- 16inch, 18inch and 2 packs of 20inch. The 20inches were tied too tight on the tape bonds when they arrived- it left a funny wavy dent that made it impossible to seal properly during installation. Fortunately, it wasn't all of them, but quite a few were un-usable. They were also very thin at the ends, like other reviews stated, and had to be trimmed an inch or two off the bottom to make it look decent.

I had an important event coming up and had already booked my appointment to have them professionally installed, so I just cut my losses and ordered another pack of 16inch to make up the difference. So I bought 5 packs in total. All in colour 8/60.

When I first had them installed, they looked great. Up until the first wash... I have now had them in for 2 weeks- I just washed them for the 3rd time last night. I know how to care for extensions- I sleep with a silk scarf over them after putting into a loose braid, use only the highest quality products, deep condition below the bond for minimum 30 min after each wash, use minimal heat, and use a good heat protector when I do. After only TWO WEEKS- the hair is garbage (see photo) I will have to take them out. The photo is AFTER I attempted to smooth them out and cut off another inch. They are full of split ends, and look disgusting. I'm wondering if these are even real hair at this point. They feel and look like cheap doll hair.

I'm not sure if the other reviews were either written directly after install and not after washing or wearing for even a few days- or if I got a bad batch?? Maybe the darker colours are better. I don't know. All I know is I'm super disappointed and out of pocket over $500 after install. The only good thing I can say is that the tape itself is strong and stayed in.

title: Best Makeup Remover I've Tried!
text:
[[VIDEOID:d7f3b7caa709fba8c5eca12e76d19e36]] This micelle water worked really well, and surprised me based on the ingredients. The main one is water. Not just ordinary water though, Hammamellis virginiana water. Whatever that is. I really don't know, but I know that it worked pretty good for me. This does contain alcohol and fragrance, which concerned me initially. But, fragrance could mean a lot of things. It could just be lavender essential oil, which is actually good for your skin. Despite this having alcohol in it, this wasn't really drying to my face. It removed my makeup really well (see the video for the gross cotton pad). There is no need to rinse this afterwards so this is perfect for situations where you may not have access to running water, but need to remove makeup. You could also just have had a rough day and not want to go through your whole routine. This allows you to clean up super quick and CRASH. Which is what I'm about to do haha. You can tell in my video, I had a pretty long day. And maybe I need some pointers on applying makeup......but this definitely helps remove any traces of my crappy makeup application, including my waterproof makeup, which didn't really stay put, and just seemed to end up all over my face. Wonder how that happened.

In full disclosure, I did receive a discount on this makeup remover for testing and review purposes. I thought it worked very well, and the regular price isn't bad at all. Especially considering what I've paid for wipes to just wipe makeup away, you can make this last a lot longer with cotton pads for a heck of a lot cheaper. And I'm all about saving money. There are a lot of products that I try and they are are meh okay, but I did really like this, and would add it to my "hall of fame" products.

title: Like SoftScrub for your teeth (in a good way)...
text:
ADVANCED CLEAN / DEEP CLEAN
This product is currently undergoing a branding/labeling transition that may be confusing for some. "Advanced Clean" used to be this products varietal name, but Colgate is now applying the "Advanced" labeling to most of the Colgate Total lineup. The new labeling reads "Colgate Total Advanced", and features a prominent gold shield. The variety is now called "Deep Clean"

PACKAGING
Love the stand-up cap, which allows it to be stored on its end -- and take up less space in the medicine cabinet.

TASTE & TEXTURE
The taste is unsurprisingly minty, enough to impart a clean sensation and some lasting freshness, but not so intense it burns or lingers beyond it's welcome. The texture is typical of 'paste' type dentfrices, however it is subtly 'grittier'.

INGREDIENTS & HEALTH CLAIMS
Ingredients are mostly standard fare for mass-market toothpastes, including cleaning agents and fluoride for cavity prevention. There are however a few important differences that make the Colgate Total Advanced range, and the Deep Clean variety in particular unique amongst toothpastes here in the states.

All Colgate Total toothpastes contain triclosan, a skin and mucous membrane-safe germ killing ingredient that you likely already use daily in the form of anti-bacterial soaps, lotions, and sanitizers. When added to toothpaste it helps kill undesirable oral bacteria (the kind that cause plaque, tartar, gingivitis and cavities). Studies have shown that it has no long term detrimental effect on desirable oral flora ('good germs'). This is the ingredient that is not found in any other (to my knowledge) toothpaste available in the states, and is what allows them to make claims about 12 hours of efficacy.

Unique to the Deep Clean variety is a modified blend of silica (included in virtually all toothpastes as a cleaning and low-abrasion polishing agent). Colgate Advanced Deep Clean contains more silica, and in a wider range of grit, from very fine and undetectable to larger and more noticeably coarse. In my experience, this makes for more effective cleaning, and leaves my teeth feeling polished and glassy-smooth. It also helps prevent and even dislodge some existing tartar buildup between dental visits.

SOFTSCRUB FOR YOUR TEETH
I use this as my daily toothpaste, and while it is slightly grittier than other toothpastes, it is not coarse to the point of harshness or outright abrasiveness. If you have ever tried Pearl Drops or other home tooth polishes, this product is similar in concept but much much gentler and perfectly suitable for everyday use.

IT'S FOR YOU IF...
- You want healthy mouth, teeth and gums with fewer 'bad' germs
- You want to keep tartar from reforming after a good dental cleaning
- You like the feeling of glassy smooth, deeply cleaned teeth

THINK TWICE IF...
- You are triclosan-phobic (I am not, clearly). Some people believe this additive isn't good for you (in toothpaste, handsoap, or anywhere else for that matter)
- You have especially sensitive teeth and gums -- you may want to explore gentler options. If you consider your sensitivity level to be normal to only somewhat sensitive, I think this product would be fine.

RECOMMENDED: Yes.

text:
Lets be clear about this up front: It only does one thing. It twists a relatively small amount of hair into a braid.

And it does it quickly thanks to two AA batteries which are not included. Lets talk about that for a moment. If you are thinking about giving this as a present, you may want to put the batteries in the unit before you give it. Installing the batteries requires a screwdriver, which is an immediate buzzkill for any kids as Dad has to look not only for batteries but also for a screwdriver. The box is easy to open, and recluse, so you can install the batteries and they'll never know you were in there.

When it says "quick, fun styles" this is mostly up to you to figure out. The instruction booklet does not explain how to accomplish any of the styles that are displayed on the box. The photos on the box are a bit small, but give a decent idea.

Conair encourages young kids to tweet selfies of themselves out to the world with box art and a "@conair" tagline.

The included clips that hold your braid together seem "immature" and "cheap" with their bright multicolor plastic appeal. You may want to grab a bag of nicer braid accessories to go with it.

Its really a useful gadget if you want to have a ton of skinny braids on one head, or if you want to do a multi braid "headdress" on your head, which my daughters have done before. However, I don't think it will have much staying power and will end up in the back of the drawer.

These bath bombs exploded with aroma when I opened the box. Each bath bomb is individually wrapped in tissue paper and has a sticker describing the color and the scent. After the sticker and tissue paper are removed, there is a plastic barrier to protect the bath bomb from getting wet before it is supposed to. They are heavily perfumed. The tissue paper and stickers make for a nice display in a bathroom bowl until they are used.

The ingredients used are all natural and safe. Baking soda, citric acid, Shea butter, coconut oil, sea butter, olive oil, fragrance, and plant extract. These are all items we have in our household. When my wife has made her own bath bombs in the past she used many of the same ingredients. I like that there are no unknowns on the ingredient list. I also like that there are no dyes for the safety of my white tub but also for my children’s skin.

I have found bath bombs to be an awesome motivator to get our children to take baths. While bubbles are fun, bath bombs seem to have a longer lasting effect. The bath bombs have an instant fizzy effect when they meet water. The colors ooze out and the aroma fills the tub. My smaller closed in tub area has a more intense scent than my more open tub. These bombs are fragrant and have long lasting fizzy effects in the tub. The kids are happy and like taking bath bomb baths so I am pleased. Knowing they are made of safe ingredients leaves me feeling comfortable using them with the kids.
