title: Very good razor for the price
text:
Upgraded to this razor after my old Remington died, and I've been very happy with it. It cut a bit close, which irritated my skin at first, but I think that was just me getting used to the "Lift & cut."

This would be an excellent razor if it wasn't for two features (or lack thereof) that make it a pain to use.

1. The internal battery is NiCd. This type of battery has "memory" to it, which means for optimal performance, the battery should be fully drained before you recharge it. Otherwise, the life of the battery will slowly shorten until the battery is useless.

2. There isn't a low battery indicator.

By itself, either of these features wouldn't pose a problem. Combined, you're left wondering when you'll have to charge the shaver, or when you're off on that business trip, if you'll need to bring the charger.

In the long run, this razor is cheap enough and I expect the battery to last for years. Still, it would have been better if the battery was made of NiMH or some technology that's not 15 years old.

PROS:
- Unscented
- Its Natural/Aluminum-free Deodorant (As a former Peace Corps volunteer who completed my 27-month commitment, I really appreciate natural alternatives)

CONS:
- I smelled. Unlike a reviewer who mentioned how they enjoyed letting their armpits breath and bask in the naturalness, I do not, and after about 5 hours my armpits smelled, which means I had to spend the last 3 hours at my office hoping and praying others could not smell me.

- I hated applying/pasting my armpit with deodorant like a savage. Using a small wooden stick to paste deodorant to your armpit feels wrong. After a while i got 'used' to it, but I never liked it.

- I got small red rashes under my armpits. This may be due to the fact that my arms were rubbing together for the 1st time, as I had to trim my hair to get the deodorant to work for more than 2 hours.

- Its expensive AND it only lasted ONE month. Normally, each rolling stick of Gillette/OldSpice will last me at least 3 months....this is just not economical.....$11 for 3 ounces....is a very poor fiscal decision in my book.

Additions:
I really tried. I used the product until every last drop was gone. I wanted to see if my body just needed time to adjust. I noticed that the deodorant last maybe 2 hours with my little armpit hairs, so I shaved, not with a razor, with a trimmer, gave it a nice minimalist look. One month later I still smelled. Daily, I would rush home and use my Dr.Bonners to wash away the armpit funk. God forbid I actually worked up a sweat/perspired from doing something that day, then I would almost immediately smell. It was not enjoyable.

Recommendations:
- Release a version for MEN (in my Ron Swanson voice)
- Eliminate the wooden stick, release a rolling stick version
- Release a larger size, for the same cost (Seriously.)

I live in NYC and walk 1/2 block to the metro, 4 blocks to the office and back, five days a week...

I had box dye in my hair and it took it out to reveal my natural hair plus sun in ends (yeah I’m old school, I use sun in to lighten my hair). Do not go over the 20 minutes leaving it in your hair. After your hair is saturated, wrap it in foil as heat activates the product a bit more. Buy this product! It is worth the price! title: Close shave but can bite.
text: The New Speed XL systems work ok but remember, this is very subjective as faces differ. I've tested several of the Speed Xl series and found them all adequate provided I don't press too firmly. They can quickly irritate the skin or actually cut. Not sensitive skin friendly by any means. This shaver has 3 rows of rotating blades which cut perfectly well but don't do as well as a good foil shaver in my case, even after the 21 day recommended break in period. You might need that much time to adjust but you'll know up front how any shaver will perform new as it is the sharpest. There is a lot of plastic and cheap feel but the heads and motor seem well built. I compared this shaver to my Panasonic pro curve linear and Braun activator. Both shavers did much better overall than the Norelco. The Braun is decent but the head quality is not the best. The Panasonic, on the other hand, did very well and seemed much better in quality. There's nothing really wrong with the Norelco and I can recommend it if you must have a rotary. If you don't, the Panasonic is the best going. Meanwhile the Norelco must be used with care and they're a bit pricey. Make sure to stock up on Remington's shaver saver spray. It sharpens and lubes the heads of any good shaver and lengthens life of the head. As always, follow the directions.

text:
I’m absolutely a bath girl. I love soaking in a nice, hot, bath for as long as I can, as often as I can. Which, unfortunately, isn’t that often. Because, you know…life. Surprisingly though, these Bath Bombs (Set of 6) by Calily are the first time I’ve ever tried bath bombs.

My experience thus far was, kind of eh. They’re ok. If this is how all bath bombs are, then I guess I don’t understand the hype. These really didn’t do much more than fizz a little in the water, and smell for about 3 minutes. To be honest I was kind of disappointed. I thought the smell would last much longer than it did. The vanilla one smelled great, although it did leave a bit of a mess in the tub. A quick rinse with my shower head cleaned it up though.

Overall, not having anything to compare these Bath Bombs (Set of 6) by Calily to, I thought they were ok. They aren’t something I will buy again. The presentation is very nice. They come displayed in a nice box, which would make these ideal for a gift closet item. They did do what they were supposed to. They dissolved nicely in the tub, and did release some scent. Not as long lasting as I would have liked though. +

Though I did purchase this at a promotional price so I could review the product, this review reflects my unbiased opinions and thoughts. They are entirely my own. I actually test out the product and write the review accordingly. It receives the rating it deserves. I hope this helps others in their purchasing decision. I also rely on Amazon reviews.

text:
This product is terrible, I’m kicking myself for purchasing it based on the reviews but am also glad that it was only $10. First off, in the listing title “Pastle,” is not a word, it’s correct spelling is PASTEL; Red flag #1 that I initially missed. Second, the highlights in the “About the Product” are completely contradictory of those in the “Product Description Section.” Example: About the product- Hair chalk washes out with your next shampoo; It won't stain or cause discoloration. Product Description: This chalk is non-toxic and will stay in the hair for 1-2 days washes depending on your hair color & Hair chalk may cause staining on fabrics and materials. Please wear gloves before you apply the chalk. Lastly, for the “NOTICE” that they listed under product description: NOTICE: The chalk maybe crashed during the shipping, but it's still can be used, please consider this before buying, thank you for your understanding.
I had no idea what they were trying to say: It should be that the chalk MAY CRACK DURING SHIPPING, but it can still be used.

All the grammar and contradictory facts aside, this was quite literally chalk you could buy at the store for play on the sidewalk or a chalkboard. My kids have blonde hair and it was a PAIN to apply and extremely messy. The results were sub-par as well. This will be turned into chalkboard chalk because it’s useless in their hair. Look at purchasing the hair chalk that is an actual pen with a soft chalk, they are similar to the pastels used in art class.

title: Fantastic product for oily skin.
text:
This product isn't sold in the US unfortunately, so it may take a little bit longer to ship. That said, it's definitely worth the wait. I have extremely oily skin, and this does a very good job at lessening it. When I don't use this, I have to use multiple oil-blotting sheets throughout the day. My usual routine is to use a cleanser that helps with the oil - something with salicylic acid, or lately Dermologica's Dermal Clay Cleanser, then use some witch hazel as an astringent/toner. After that I use a little bit of oil-free moisturizer, then once that's try, I put this under base on. I noticed immediately that it dries very fast. It doesn't make your skin dry, but I don't have to wait forever for it to soak in before I put on my makeup - it helps the moisturizer soak in faster too. My pores looked much smaller, and my skin felt very smooth. Like other reviewers have said, it made a very nice canvas for the makeup.
You may find yourself surprised at the size when you receive it - the canister is much smaller than you might expect, and it's metal. Depending on how much you use, you might want to go ahead and buy two, just because of how long it will take you to receive your next one. Another word of warning - you'll need a lot less than you think. When you press on the pump, you really only need to tap it; it will put out a bunch of mousse very quickly, and it's easy to get more than you need.

This is basically a rebadged pumice scrub that you can buy at the drugstore - check the ingredients, it's right there - pumice. There are no specific ingredients to help with KP, just some essential oils that you'd find in most scrubs.

Just like the cream, this product is for sale anywhere besides Amazon - you can see that because they've printed the Amazon barcode itself right on the label. There's no real UPC. Don't fall for the new products like this one that pop up periodically - go with something that's been around for a long time.

I highly recommend the cream form of Lume, but will never use the solid again!

title: Pink I chose was a medium pink shade. Pink I got was a light bubblegum pink
text:
This comes in an outer product box that is inside a sealed plastic bag. It is made in the US. The ingredients are listed. The product box says that this is “80% organic. Made with organic ingredients, cruelty free.”

This claims to be a moisturizing lipstick. That sounds great to me, because I hate the feeling of my lips being dry at all. It claims to be highly pigmented, and have lasting color. It also said it has a vanilla fragrance.

I liked that it’s made of 80% organic ingredients, and it also had botanical extracts and essential plant oils. Looking at the ingredients, there’s some great ones like castor seed oil, sunflower seed oil, Shea butter, cocoa seed butter, jojoba seed oil, coconut oil, and vitamin E.

The tube is plain matte black with the brand logo on the cap. It has some weight to it. It kind of feels like it’s metal, but when I pull the cap off, the cap feels like plastic. The bottom part where you twist the lipstick is the part that feels like metal. It’s also the part that has the weight to it. But I’m not sure if it really is metal or not. The cap pulls off. It goes onto the bottom part really snugly, so I don’t see it coming off accidentally.

I got the shade “Crazy For You.” The product photo swatch made it look like a pretty medium pink color that had maybe a little peach color to it. It looked really pretty! I don’t think the color matches the product photo swatch much. I still like the color, but it’s a lot lighter than the product photo made it look, and no peach in it at all. It’s a bubblegum pink color. It’s pretty light with 1 layer. I did 2 swatches - One is 1 layer, the other is 3 layers. Even with 3 layers it didn’t look as dark as the product photo swatch.

There is no vanilla scent at all. I found that really weird since the claims on the product box state it has vanilla fragrance and the last ingredient listed is fragrance. But there’s zero scent, not even a hint of scent. I don’t mind if lipsticks don’t have fragrance. I just find it odd to claim it has a certain fragrance when it has no fragrance at all! The formula is really nice. It’s very moisturizing. It doesn’t feel dry at all. So I agree with the claim that it’s a moisturizing lipstick. It lasts nicely on the lips, so I agree with the claim of lasting color. The color is pretty, but I wish it was the color I saw in the product photo. I wouldn’t say it’s highly pigmented. It has decent pigment. It might be the color I got, but 1 layer is light, and it takes 3 layers to get it to show up more.

Overall, I think it’s a nice lipstick. The packaging is simple but nice. The formula is moisturizing and the color lasts well. I don’t like that the color isn’t what I chose based on the product photo swatch. It’s not even close, aside from the fact that it’s pink. The product photo swatch is a medium pink color, with a hint of peach. The color I got is a light bubblegum pink. So, I’m taking 2 stars off for that. I thought about only taking 1 star off since I do like the color. But, when you choose a color of lipstick, you choose it for a reason (whether it’s a color you like on yourself, a color you want to try out, a color you like that you want in your collection, etc.). Whatever the reason for choosing the color you choose, you should get that color. I understand sometimes colors can be off a tiny bit when ordering things online. But the pink I received is way off from the pink I chose. Other than that, the formula is nice. If you like moisturizing lipsticks and don’t mind risking getting a color way off from what you chose, I’d recommend this!

title: Somewhat underimpressed
text:
I got this razor as a Christmas gift after telling my girlfriend about it and it frustrated me a bit when it just didn't work as well as I expected it to. I thought I was going to have the most amazing shave of my life, and most convenient and comfortable to boot (especially for the price of this shaver). Well I'm sorry to say I eventually got a decent shave by the 3rd try, but as for my expectations well it just didn't happen.

Some background, I used to use a really basic Norelco triple rotary head as my first razor when I got it in my early teenage years to get rid of my meager beard. That was about 20 years ago, and I long ago abandoned using an electric razor. So even though I don't normally use one, instead preferring to use a triple blade and shaving gel every 2-3 days, I knew what to expect. And after reading the literature, the description/outer packaging, and viewing ads on TV I thought this unit would be head and shoulders about anything I'd used before.

I hate dealing with shaving and the possibility of any nicks/cuts/razor burn and ingrown hairs so in addition to avoiding that I wanted this for convenience and to save time, but the first problem I had with this shaver was that it took almost as long to shave using it as it would with my old razor and shaving gel. I used this Philips/Norelco 3 times to make sure I'd given it ample opportunity to perform and there wasn't any fluke, then if I still didn't like it I'd return it and go back to what I was doing or get something else.

Shave #1 - Fresh out of the box. Had about a 2.5 - 3 day beard going (I have a medium growth of mostly straight hairs) Was impressed how it felt and balanced in my hand. Unique flex head didn't flex as much as I thought it needed to, but probably not much of a detriment. Not atypical for me, but a good amount of hair to get rid of for any shaver. Used it to shave with dry skin. Had to get used to the most effective way to use/hold it, but it did well near my cheekbones (the easiest part), OK on my moustache and goatee area, and so-so on my jawbone and neck. Hardest part was my neck but also near my jaw. Had to go over the same areas several several times using medium pressure - much more than expected. And since I knew it takes a few shaves for your skin to get used to it and there is much more likely to be some discomfort the first time I thought OK no big deal. But I could tell there was a lot more "chafe" on my face than I expected and the neck area had quite a bit of razor burn / redness even though I really wasn't pushing hard or using it at what I would call a bad angle. Did not really cut the sideways hairs as well as I expected, since they advertise it will obliterate those and I have quite a few on my neck. Rinsed the thing under water, dried with towel and put it away. Put a bunch of lotion on my face to help, still feeling some light discomfort / itch all over immediately after.

Shave #2 - 2 days later. Opted to go with some water on my face since that is how I'm used to shaving and normally expect to get slightly better results, and a bit less irritation. It worked pretty well, but the shave still took around 8 minutes or so, a bit too long and I still needed a mirror the whole time. My face wasn't quite as irritated as the first time, meaning slightly less chafe and razor burn on my neck, though a few ingrown hairs had made themselves known directly under my chin from shave #1 and I did whatever I could to get rid of those with a tweezer beforehand. Sideways hairs still wouldn't cut quite as well as I expected, though I didn't quite have to go over my neck and rear of my jawbone quite as many times as the first shave. After this shave I still managed to have a few stray hairs that either would not cut easily even after 5 or 10 direct passes or (for a few) if they were facing sideways, then not at all. I went back with the tiny but fairly effective trimmer and knocked these out, but didn't expect to have to do this and added another minute or two to the process. Not much razorburn this time, put a normal amount of lotion on my face and I was good to go. Pretty good shave. Emptied the heads into the sink and rinsed and dried with water.

Shave #3 - 2 days later. Easily the best shave of the three, which was what I was hoping for. Still went with the wet shave, meaning I made sure there was plenty of water on my face to start. Again upper cheek was the easiest and took almost no time, then moustache, goatee, jaw and sideburns, and then neck. Initial shave took roughly 7 minutes. Not as bad but not what I would call super fast. The rotary heads got almost all the hairs this time, except for 1 or 2 stubborn / sideways hairs on my neck near my adam's apple. Some hairs / areas took 5-10 passes with the shave head but went away with the appropriate pressure/motion. Almost no razor burn on my neck and a pretty low amount of chafe. Was impressed how it got the hairs right under my nostrils this time, due to my practice and the shape of the head. After the shave, I had to go back to get about 3 hairs that didn't make the cut (literally). This again added 1-2 minutes of shave time. I applied the usual amount of lotion and rinsed and dried the heads. The weird thing was this time, for some reason due to the water when I opened the heads to clean it, there were almost no hairs inside. Usually with a dry shave and 2-3 days of growth the heads get pretty full quickly. But in this case there was none, and not many showed up in the sink or countertop either. Weird, I guess the water had some strange effect where they either disintegrate into much smaller hairs and/or made them fly out somewhere I couldn't see. Either way I was done. Still, I didn't think this performance was quite up to my initial expectations, or the billing that Philips/Norelco gave it as their "most advanced shaver". But, it was "close" to a wet shave with a blade. Maybe a 8 / 10 this time. However I didn't like having to use a mirror the whole time still. And for the price, especially since it's described as waterproof shouldn't you be able to take it in the shower for the ultimate convenience? I dunno, I figure with a top-of-the-line shaver from this company, you should.

I didn't bother with the cleaning / charging compartment since I didn't know if I would keep the razor or return to the store, and didn't want to learn something I wouldn't need to know, nor use up any of the shaving fluid or dirty it up if I planned to return. Just more hassle. I really think it's a little pointless to do this full cleaning process every time, maybe every few shaves but that's just me. Water works OK and the blades are billed as self-sharpening which means less worry and as long as you pat dry after the clean it should be OK.

The carrying case is the alternative charging mechanism, and you can take it with you on the go. It also comes with a slide-on head cover if you're just going to put the unit away say in a drawer until the next use and don't need to charge it. One problem, the plastic head cover that slides on doesn't work with the travel / charging case. Why they made it so this won't fit, I don't understand. You're prone to lose or break it I think if you can't keep it inside, and why else would they give it to you if you can't take it with you in the travel charging case?

My take is this shaver probably works best if you have a light or medium beard and you shave every 1-to-2 days. Otherwise, stick to a blade and heavy shave gel if possible.

Strengths:
- Good overall shave and closeness, with patience
- Reasonably comfortable shave
- Flexible head, very unique design adds an extra dimension
- Strong trimmer for the size
- Very quick 1 hr. charging in either the cleaning unit or travel case
- Works with wet or dry skin (warning: not designed to work in shower or submerged)
- Good for people with light to medium beards that shave every day
- Self-sharpening heads
- Motor seems strong and good RPM
- Cleaning unit makes maintenance a bit easier and worry-free
- 2 year warranty
- 30 day money back guarantee / trial
- Made in Europe, not China

Weaknesses:
- Price / Value
- Too many passes to get all hairs = longer shaving time
- Had to use a mirror entire time to get accurate shave
- Trimmer is absolutely tiny and I'm not sure how sturdy over time
- Plastic head cover doesn't fit in travel charging case, or have a home when not in use
- Doesn't cut sideways hairs near as well as advertised
- Charging and cleaning processes require more attention than desired
- Not good for people with very heavy beards who only want to shave every 3 or 4 days
- "Clean shaver" icon is not smart - it always appears even after rinsing heads under water
- Can't use in shower
- Overall, just not quite as 'advanced' as advertised

Time for me to bring this back and try another high-end shaver from another european-based company which should remain nameless.

title: Nice smooth glide and large head makes for easy work
text:
The Maybuy Professional Hair Clippers/Beard Trimmers comes with 3 attachments, 1/2 inch, 1 inch and 1.5 inches. These attachments simply clip onto the head of the trimmer. You also get a small brush for cleaning the trimmer and a charging cable which strangely is a USB to Mini-USB even though at the bottom of the trimmer is your standard two prong charging connector.

Being able to charge this via USB however is great for when you need to go on holiday/vacation as you always have some kind of USB charging device with yourself (usually for your phone). On a full charge the clippers will roughly 2 hours and are small enough to just throw in your toiletry bag.

The trimmer itself has a nice shape to it and is comfortable to hold in your hand. It also has a fairly nice heft to it, not too light but not heavy. It feels like you are really holding on to something though.

The head is fairly wide which can be a plus in that it doesn't take long at all to trim an area but can also be a bit of a minus depending on the shape of your face if you are trimming your beard. The action is smooth and has a nice gliding feel to it, even if you don't use any attachments and just use the trimmer head itself.

It would have been nice if the Maybuy came with some sort of carrying case to put it, the attachments and the charging cord in but it doesn't unfortunately. The attachments do come in a small Ziploc bag.

Overall a nice trimmer, nice action and makes quick work whether trimming your beard or hard to reach places like around your ears.

text: The Razorba works alright.  I have a few issues though:  1.  If you are shaving your back with a full crop of hair, it isnt going to work very well, just like trying to shave your face or wherever without trimming things down first. If you are really hairy you will need to either nair anyway or be very very very patient with this thing as it will only shave about a square inch of long hair on its own.  Seems like it will be good to use if your hair is very short though.  2. The plastic slot that you put the razor in could be designed better. It is basically a softer plastic tube that grips the handle of a normal disposable razor inside the harder plastic body of the Razorba.  This could be improved by putting some sort of screw clamp on the side so your disposable couldnt move.  I think this could be done without increasing the cost much since I suspect they make a pretty huge profit margin on these things.  The problem with the razor not being held securely is that it can turn slightly in the plastic sleave and cut you, this doesnt really hurt but if you are a bleeder its hard to get it to stop.  Another thing that could be improved is to make a hole in the end of the head of the thing opposite where you put the razor for water to flow out of.  After you rinse off the razorblade water collects in the head which when you go to do another stroke flies all over your bathroom, but more seriously makes the razor fit less tightly in the soft plastic tube.  All in all this product does work but their are a few minor annoyance type issues that coule be fixed easily to make it better.

I like it, I don't love it.

The good - well, that this thing even exists! I think if you care enough about your hair to do treatments, you probably don't mind taking the extra step to make sure it's as effective as possible. I had a treatment in a salon once, was nothing great. Afterward the stylist found out they hadn't put me under heat - so I got to go back for a freebie - and what a difference that heat made!

The bad - the cord part in the back where it comes out was uncomfortable, I had to fold up a cloth and put it between that and my neck, not a big deal. But the worst part, and not sure if it's just my unit, it doesn't get very hot. I had it on high for 60 minutes and at best it was warm. I was pressing it against my head at times just to ensure my hair was getting heated. Because of the lack of high heat, I also used it with a plastic cap. From what I can tell, the only reason you shouldn't is because the cap might stain, but that doesn't bother me. When I took the cap off, my hair was only slightly warm but went cold within 1 minute. I wonder if my unit is defective?

And lastly, another good, I could hear Netflix just fine! LOL. I was wondering if it would dampen the sound with something over my ears but it really didn't.

The puncture, made by screwing the cap down once the ring has been removed, creates a rough edge with a point as the cap is screwed off.  Watch out for that point.  It scratches the eyeball as you administer the drops.  The other problem with the packaging is that the opening in the vial is too big.  That is, it's almost impossible to aim a drop or two into your eye, given the volume of liquid that emerges when you tilt the vial.  So the stuff just runs down your cheek. title: First time user of poly gel
text:
I watched many videos in preparation of arrival of this kit and was excited to try it. It's a really nice product to work with for a beginner. I haven't been to a nail salon in decades and just have natural nails. Sometimes they grow out long and beautiful but too often they break and are uneven lengths. That's particularly why I wanted a polygel product to allow my natural nails to grow and use this as an
overlay strengthener. I think it will work well for that. If you follow the directions and watch a few videos, prep the nails and wipe off the sticky layer, I feel this is a very good product and was lots of fun to play with on my current shorter nails. With practice, I hope to get better at application. I bought the glow in the dark set and I wasn't crazy about the opacity, so I painted over them. The reason I dropped a start, though, was the nail forms. The deap curve of the forms don't fit my nails very well and I was very glad I'd also ordered nail clips. Without them, there's no way they would have turned out looking decent. It made it difficult to squish out the extra and clean up my cuticles before curing. Cleaning up the under side of the nail to give it a proper shape underneath was a little bit of a challenge because I didn't notice I'd gotten really thin on a couple edges. One pinky nail bubbled between the gel and form because the clip wasn't firm enough on my pinky. These I had to patch. Some of the patches worked, one did not (right hand pointer). I have ordered the paper forms to use in the future and hope they will work better for me. All around I'm very happy with the glow in the dark kit and the one I tried, really does glow in the dark! Very cool and I think my granddaughters will love it! I only applied them yesterday and I'm confident in my nail prep and use of base coat. If I don't get decent wear out of them, because I only applied yesterday, I'll come back and update.

text:
I know this is a baby bath oil, but I'm a fan of using bath oils as shave oils. A little goes a long way, just a few drops per leg (or you can add a drop to your regular shave gel). Helps reduce irritation and you can see where you are shaving! I can't live without it. It's better than any foam, gel or lotion on the market. Truly the best shave experience. I have thick hair and dry flaky skin that is prone to itching and sensitivity. I use this bath oil with a cheapie disposable razor and a few drops of body oil after a shower and my legs are silky for days. Literally days. No razor burn, no irritation, no frustration. I prefer unscented products and this is truly unscented--thank you! Please use caution when using oils in the tub, but I haven't had any problems with the tub getting slippery. Only thing I would change in a better bottle with a pump or dropper top. It's easy to use too much. A little goes a long way so if you're hesitant about the price, don't be, because you'll end up spending more in the long run on something cheaper.

Also, used this as a body wash after getting a little too much sun today, and my skin was super soothed. I think it will help prevent my skin from developing a sunburn--bonus! I may just have to buy a vat of this!

title: Sharp Shears for Healthy Looking Hair
text:
I learned some things when I was looking for hair cutting shears. Mostly that you can pay around $200 for the best ones,used by professionals,and,that you need very sharp scissors or shears to cut or trim hair.

I've been trimming and shaping my own hair for a long time and am usually happy with the results,considering too many times,when I would go to a salon to have it cut or shaped or trimmed,they did a job I was almost always disappointed with. I decided a long time ago,if someone was going to screw up my hair,it might as well be me. At least I have a good idea on when to stop cutting it and I actually care what the final result looks like.

I also have fine,wavy hair. Not the easiest to cut.

I have noticed,and maybe it was from using whatever scissors were around at the time,that sometimes the ends do look a bit frazzled;and in researching shears,I found out that unless the blades are very sharp,the ends can break,or result in split ends. I don't have split ends and never noticed them,except for a long,long time ago when I was a teenager;but,I have used these once to do some light trimming and shaping;with wavy hair you are always shaping,cutting with the wave and not cutting against the wave. And,these shears have produced a nice result. And I don't see the somewhat frazzled or lightningbolt effect at the ends of my hair,that I sometimes get.

I've used these just once,I only trim my hair to maintain healthy looking ends,and I did it a few weeks ago,and I like these and I'm glad I looked for something better than "any old scissors" that I have on hand.

title: Lightweight forumla.  Not crazy about the scent.
text:
Bottom Line Up Front: This is a lightweight formula that is easily absorbed by the skin. I would recommend this serum for the day time prior to the application of any makeup. I use this in place of a moisturizing since it is not as heavy. After application, you can still feel the serum on your skin but after a while, all of it is absorbed. There is a strong scent that almost resembles eucalyptus but not in a good way.

I like to try out different skin care products and I have been having great luck with products that are serums. I saw this product and decided to give it a try. The following is my thoughts regarding this product.

**Pros
1. Lightweight - The consistency of this product is lightweight but thicker than other serums I have tried. The serum is of a milky white appearance. When applied to the skin, it is easily absorbed. It is perfect for day time wear and I want to believe that at least I am applying something to my skin prior to slapping on a whole bunch of makeup.
2. Packaging - I always appreciate when skin care products include a dropper or pump to extract the product. In this case, the serum came with a dropper. Based on the consistency, a dropper is perfect to control how much you need.

**Cons
1. Formula - Although the contents may be good for your skin, if you are looking for something to moisturize extremely dry skin, this is probably not it and you should be looking for a cream. Like I mentioned before, this serum is perfect for day time wear. There is also a slight residue or stickiness that I feel after the product dries which I am not fond of.
2. Scent - I am not crazy about the scent. This is the strongest smelling serum that I have tried to date. If you are sensitive to the smell of a product, this may one of the serum that you avoid.

Disclaimer: I did receive this product at a discount but this in no way influenced my review of this product.

I have been curious about these heartless curling rod headbands for a while now. I mean who wouldn’t love to wake up with curled and bouncy hair that you didn’t even have to use heat on?!?! So when I came across this set I figured it was totally worth a try!

I’m the set you get the shiny metallic/holographic bag, 2 scrunchies, one hair clip, and the long curling thing itself. Both the scrunchies and the curling rod thing have a satin finish, which is great for your hair and is soft to the touch. The curling rod thing seams to be stuffed with basic stuffing like you would find in a cheap pillow. Honestly the overall quality is just ok, nothing fancy.

I have used this multiple times now, and there is for sure a learning curve. It seams simple enough, but the way you wrap it, how tightly you wrap it, how big the sections are that you wrap, and how damp your hair is all play a huge rule in how it turns out. They do include a little card with pictures on the basics of how to wrap your hair, but the rest you will have to figure out as you go.

As far as how well it works, it definitely does work. Even my hair that usually doesn’t hold a curl with heat I was able to get decent wavy styles out of. This does give a nice wave to it, however if I want truly curly hair or even loose curls then this doesn’t do that for me.

One other thing worth the mentioning, I priced these out and this set is 2x-3x more expensive than others sold on here. And being that the quality on this isn’t amazing or anything. Im confused as to why. But overall it’s an ok product.

title: Seems to work okay, but not a lot of care's been put into it
text:
I've been using this brush for about 6 weeks, and haven't had a dental checkup in the meantime, so it's a bit hard to know how well it's really been working.

But here are a few observations:

- It feels cheap. Maybe it's just that I'm used to the solid heft of my trusty Sonicare toothbrush, but this Oral-B toothbrush feels like something you'd get at Safeway for $49.95, not $99.95.

- The polishing brush does seem to do a pretty thorough job. The main brush (whatever it's called) also seems rather decent.

- The tongue cleaner is worse than useless. A cheapie Walgreens manual tongue scraper does a much better job.

- So, too, does the interdental-stimulator / toothpick thingy seem pretty useless. Manual flossing is just as fast and seems much more thorough. And dental floss is about half a penny per 'serving', whereas the replacement Oral-B things are much more expensive.

- The base is so top-heavy, I've accidentally knocked it over twice, hurling the toothbrush to the floor (ouch!). Thankfully, the toothbrush still seems to work fine, but as you can guess, I finally wised up and screwed the base to the wall. I never had such a problem with the Sonicare.

- No carrying case? Not even any friggin' cap for the toothbrush? This basically makes it a total pain to cleanly transport this brush to work or on a trip or anywhere else. ALL the Sonicares (and their replacement brushheads) come with a simple, effective plastic cover. What was Oral-B thinking?!

In fairness, this toothbrush probably merits a 3.5, and if I get a great bill-of-health from my dentist at my next checkup, I'll revise this review to a 4. But in the meantime, I'm certainly disappointed that Oral-B has given a bargain-bin treatment to a premium-priced product.

title: Overwhelmingly Dole
text:
Order delivery was fine. My review of the fragrance on Basenotes:

---

Hi. Newbie here, and I thank this august membership for your expertise!

I have learned a lot.

Anyway, I do not claim to have an advanced olfactory system but, other than the "late powder" I have been reading so much about here, I did not experience a lot of what others have mentioned.

My 1 Million Lucky arrived today. I got a 100 mil. bottle on Amazon for 60 bucks and could not resist the bargain. Have been looking for an Aventus substitute (nothing qualifies as a true clone, I've found) and this fragrance came highly recommended.

First blast was just that - an almost overwhelming gale of The Pineapple Express. Wow! Felt like I was swimming in a piña colada without the colada. Aventus has a decent (and MUCH subtler) pineapple note at first but that calms down very quickly into sublime, complex underthemes. From the pineapple, things got even more sugary and I was reminded of these little candies, Smarties, that I used to eat as a kid. It was a nice sense memory but not terribly masculine. Then, for a moment, the pineapple morphed into what I can only describe rotten pineapple: you know, as if the pineapple rind you threw away yesterday came jumping out of the trash and started pursuing you menacingly around your home?

Not pretty.

3 hours hence, the fragrance has calmed down considerably and, while the pineapple is still there, there's also some remaining candy and, as aforementioned, a LOT of powder.

So, to recap: Robust pineapple-infused nuclear detonation settles into nostalgic children's candy, decays (half-life?) into pineapple corpse, which, blessédly, gives way to a fairly nice pineapplecandypowder.

This strikes me as a unisex scent, though I've not seen that mentioned anywhere. Perhaps I'll spray some on one of my girlfriends and see what happens?!

6.5/10

text:
These patches work as well as other patches I've tried. They are not a miraculous cure-all, but they do help flatten out the acne and draw out the stuff that needs to be drawn out (don't want to get too gross and graphic here). They are small (1 cm diameter) so the coverage is limited, but they adhere well.

There are a couple of cons with these that lower my score:

> They are harder to peel off the backing than others, and it's easy to fold over the edge of the patch when removing it, making it less effective. Other brands I've used have slits in the backing material, making it much easier to dispense a patch without damaging it.

> The packaging is very wasteful. Each sheet of 20 comes in its own box. You could easily fit several sheets into one box. Either the box should be made much smaller or each box should hold multiple sheets. There's no need for all this packaging waste.

Three stars (average). While these work as well as other patches, there are other options that are better choices.

title: I wouldn't start with this--
text:
This is a beginner set, but it's not looking to help you-- No instructions.

Lucky for me--This isn't my first gel kit.

At first when I opened the box I liked how much they had to offer creatively. Some kits try to force a look, but this one was open to play with. Maybe not the best idea for a beginner kit- but I enjoyed that.

First the good:
I like this type of lamp when I'm doing gel- it's easy together both my hands in to hold the nail down when I first start, then I usually pick up the light and rotate it to get a full cure. Yes I have to restart the lamp a few times, but this isn't an expensive lamp so I don't mind.

I liked the little box they came in- sure it's cheep, but it was a nice tough to have (almost) everything in once place.

Then the annoying:

There are a lot of odd little problems, like the Gel itself, two are jelly clear and one is opaque. Opaque gel takes a little longer to cure because the light works a bit harder to travel though the nail. It would have been helpful if they mentioned that, OR only gave you one type of gel-so it doesn't confuse you-- but they didn't.

The nail forms were a bad fir for my hand. Thats just an unlucky break- all hands are diffrent- so im not including that in my rating, just something to mention in case they don't work for you too.

The colors were a little annoying to use, no color indicator on the bottle. this is common with cheeper sets, but I thought I'd mention it anyway- It can make doing your nails just a little bothersome.

The ugly-
they don't include slip solution-I ended up using my own from my nail kit, so I didn't have any problems, but that's a huge mistake on their part-- if you're just starting out you'll think gel nails are a sticky mess. Slip solution makes them manageable.

Overall- I feel like there are better kits that will give you a cleaner start over this one--

I hope this review was helpful!

title: It's an alright little balm stain...
text: I got this balm stain with a few other options to try for my wedding this fall. I wanted something with a rich color, that lasted more than a couple hours, and wouldn't come off on my new husband's face!! While this is a great little balm, it's not the one I think I'm going to go with. The color of this one came out quite a bit brighter pink than I'd expect from the color of the product in the tube, but it's not bad. The opacity of the color does leave a bit to be desired, it's not quite as opaque as I was hoping, it's a little on the translucent side, but I expected that of a balm. However, the color does last quite a while even after several hours of answering the phones at work and talking around the office. It feels a little drying, but as a chapstick addict myself, almost any lipstick/stain feels drying because I'm not reapplying every hour or so! Although, when I rub my lips together even a couple hours after applying, I can still feel there's a moist layer of product on my lips...so I'm sure it won't feel drying to all. As far as transfer is concerned, I haven't noticed any color coming off on the back of my hand when I "test kiss" - possibly a little right after applying, but several hours in and there's no transfer (even with that moist feeling I was mentioning earlier!). Like I said, it's a good little balm stain, and is probably great for day-to-day wear, but not my choice for my wedding!

title: My skin might be too sensitive for this product
text:
I'll start off this review by telling you about my incredibly problematic skin. First off I have been suffering with mild acne for the past eight years. Recently I have developed terrible long lasting cystic acne break outs on my face, neck, chest, and back. If you suffer from this awfully painful form of acne you know that when a break out stops the evidence does not disappear, but instead leaves a huge dark mark or large indented scar ( and when you're really unlucky it will leave a combination of both). I have been using Dead Sea mud masks about twice every week which has been helping, but I was in need for something stronger. This is definitely stronger than your run of the mill Dead Sea mud mask. I have pretty sensitive skin and this honestly aggravates my skin a little and leaves it ruddy and burning, so this product may not be suitable for extremely sensitive skin. Please also notice that the jar only contains 2 ounces of product which will go by very fast, especially if used on more than just the face.

The so-called "wireless" charging consists of a base you plug into a USB adapter (not supplied) which has 4 metal contacts on the top. To charge the device you stand it so that two contacts on the underside of the base make contact with two on the base. It's pretty basic and falls over quite easily.

Once charging is started a pretty (pointless) blue and white light pulses gently for several hours.
After charging is complete you can use this to clean your teeth, by putting the "brush" in your mouth and turning it on. The only problem is that it doesn't do a good job. Various presses of the one button make a blue light come on and the whole device vibrate gently. This is totally insufficient to clean your teeth.

I persevered with this for several days and my teeth felt horrible, like I hadn't brushed then at all.

In summary - worthless.

I have been able to reattach the nut and reassemble the mirror. And then after just a few times the same thing happens. I have now applied "Loctite" to the threads and reassembled again. I cleaned and sanitized it completely and I felt it was 'safe' even though it was clearly a used product that I received. The box had been opened and retaped, there was a bit of nail polish reside left on the little black flexible nail guard that you put your fingers in and the middle light that glows yellow was cracked. I was just so gosh darn excited about getting this amazing item that I didn't want to go through the hassle of returning and waiting for a new one. So it's partly my fault for not returning it. Well after 5 months of use, it just stopped working. No heat, no lights, nothing. I'm crushed that it no longer works but I'm unwilling to purchase another one with the fear it will only last another 5 months. I think the product and idea are fantastic and it worked great, but the quality control is sorely lacking.

title: Quick, easy, blendable & at drugstore prices....gotta love it!!
text: I think we all have days where we're looking for something quick and easy when it comes to makeup.  Anything to get us out the door looking somewhat put together with the least amount of time involved is the goal.  If you're looking for a quick eyeshadow look that takes next to no time these are one answer.  Cream eyeshadow on one end and a brush on the other.  The brush is surprisingly usable, but since I've got older eyes (which means older skin that needs to be babied) I just use one of mine.  They go on pretty smooth and creamy.  Not a ton of pigment on the first pass, but it's very buildable.  The swatches on my arm are 2 passes of each color.  They also blend out really well.  I put a couple passes on my lower lid and blend it up into my crease and I'm good to go.  There is a bit of shimmer in this one, but it's not overwhelming.  Just a bit of sparkle that looks good even on aging eyes.  They make it through the whole day, but I did notice some creasing and breakdown after about 6-8 hours.  Not a lot, just enough to be noticeable.  Overall these were pretty impressive and I think they'd also be great for someone who was just getting into makeup too.

text:
I've been using Norelco shavers for past 18 years, so I've always liked their product. Before I bought this item, I had an old (12 years old) Norelco that I wanted to replace. My brother had bought the 9160XL shaver a while ago and after I checked it out, I thought it looked nice and was much quieter than the older model that I had. I didn't use his to see how well it would shave, so I decided to take a chance and buy it based on his recommendation. However, I was skeptical about how good it would shave because it was too quiet. After I bought and received the shaver, my very first shave was simply great. I can't recall the last shave I had that made my face this smooth. The shave is so close that I don't get a "5 o'clock" shadow until the next day! Another very important thing is that after shaving, I don't get a burning/irritating sensation with this shaver. I don't have sensitive skin but my old Norelco would sometimes irritate my skin.
I also liked the face-contouring elements that they have added to this shaver. I don't have to fight and press the shaver as hard on my face to get the blades to touch my skin.
Cleaning the 9160XL is breeze; just rinse with water and let dry. Battery life is great too. I have used this for 2 months (over 30 shaves) and it still has 1/3 of its charge left!
I would strongly recommend this shaver.

I threw the second one away, and won't be purchasing this product again. title: Really great starter brush that should last a while.
text:
I've had 4 brushes now and have been wet shaving for 8 years. I was concerned that this was going to be too small in my hand or too light as I had a Parker before that was significantly heavy and had a nice sized bulb on it.

This is lighter than that, but not too light. It is smaller than others I've had but not too light. The bristles are a bit stiffer than others that I've had, but I've realised that the stiffer bristles are much better for shaving soap that I use, where the softer bristles are better for the shaving cream that I used when I first started wet shaving.

Overall, great brush. A bit of advice, when shopping for brushes, don't get caught up in all the different levels of badger hair. These are marketing people at work, and while you can tell a slight difference, softer bristles aren't always better. Rather consider - do you use soap (stiffer is better) or cream (softer is better)? Do you have a more sensitive face (softer might be better) or do you enjoy the exfoliation to keep your face soft (stiffer is better). How many passes do you take - if you only take 2 or 3, you don't need a TON of all that water holding capability that people rave about, but if you are taking 5 or more passes, that might be better for you and a bigger bulb and softer bristles might be better for you.

I love this mask. I love it so much that I have been buying it for over 10 years. But this purchase I am unsure about. Part of me wonders if they are "fakes" even though the packaging looks legit. They came with a heavy chemical smell on them when I pulled them out of the plastic and while I do have a very sensitive sense of smell I have never had that issue with this mask before. I have been airing them out in the weeks since I received them as there is no way I can handle that smell on my face and near my nose. Also one of the masks is sewn a bit unevenly but I figured for the price of two I couldn't complain. One of the other things that makes me wonder if these are the real deal is that the pattern is slightly lighter and the fabric is a brighter blue. You can see my old one for comparison in the third picture. Now it is totally possible that maybe the brand has switched things up in the years since I bought and of course my old mask has probably darkened a bit in time but you can see in their ads that the fabric does indeed look darker and closer to my old one.

I am hoping I can use these soon and that they are the real deal and I am not going to end up putting some tainted fabric over my eyes. As you can see I was seriously in need of a new one as my old one I have a hair tie on the strap to keep it from falling off my head as the strap is all stretched out now. A kind of disappointing purchase with these though over all as this has been one of my most loved products for so long... I did not contact the seller before leaving a review as I didn't feel up to getting into it for something of this price and I just feel that would be pretty pointless if all the ones they are selling are the same... title: Best wash cloth for the money
text:
EXPERIENCE: Have been buying these for >5 years and use this every day.

PRICE: Bought for ~$12 for pack of 3. Price has ranged $10-$14 over the years.

PROTIP: Buy one of these at an asian grocery store to know what an authentic one feels like and try it out to see if you like it enough to buy a 3 pack.

PROS:
- provides actual physical exfoliation, not just pouncing a soft, soapy loofah on your skin
- lasts me around 3-4 months before tossing (can last longer but I like changing it out)
- can be cleaned in the washing machine and dryer
- dries out quickly so is good for travel and prevents mold/mildew smells
- large and long enough to scrub your back
- easy and quick to rinse out soap after scrubbing in the shower

CONS:
- nothing about product itself
- watch out for fake products by reading seller reviews, try to only buy if >98% positive + >3000 reviews

text:

title: Not As Good As Previous Norelco Models. Not For Anyone With a Mustache or Beard
text:
I have been using Norelco shavers for 30 years at least. This was my 4th model of Norelco shaver. I have been using this shaver about 6 months. For the first time I am very disappointed in a Norelco product and I will purchase another brand soon.

The trimmer is nearly non-functional. With the old Norelco products, the trimmers worked very well and I would only occassionally have to pull out a special purpose mustache/beard trimmer to perform maintenance on my goatee. With this new 1090, I have to use a separate trimmer all the time. The location of the trimmer makes it very difficult to see where it is placed so I can't use it safely to keep the goatee whisker length in check without risking overcutting it. And the trimemr blades barely protrude from the body of the shaver which makes it nearly impossible to get the trimmer on a lone stray whisker. Now I have to to travel with 2 shavers.

Every other usage requires the shaver to be rinsed out. When travelling I have to keep the shaver in a travel case. This forces me to regularly dry the shaver with the hotel blow-dryer before I use it because it isn't yet dry from the previous day's cleaning. Every day I am either cleaning it or drying it. A real pain.

I will admit that it is light, feels good in the hand, and shaves well if you use it every day. If you skip shaving for a few days it takes many passes before it shaves all the long whiskers. I typically need to use a trimmer to cut some strays down before finishing off.

This product is not effective for anyone with mustaches or beards or someone that skips a day or two on a regular basis. Given how expensive it is, you would be well advised to find a different product to purchase.

title: Wouldn’t Recommend for Dry Skin
text:
I bought this hoping it would be a morning moisturizer. It came well-packaged and with a safety seal, and I have no complaints about the tube itself (easy squeeze tube for no mess and hygienic). The texture of the product is interesting—it’s thick and bouncy, and once it starts warming up on your hand, it applies fairly easily. There is really no scent, and there is a decent amount of product in the tube. The issues I have with the product, however, is the absorption rate and its spreadability on my skin (for reference, I have dry, sensitive skin). This stuff absorbs VERY quickly once it’s spread on the skin, which in this case is not really a good thing. It sticks to your skin where you spread it and doesn’t budge, which makes me tug at my skin inadvertently in an effort to massage the product more thoroughly all over my face. The finishing texture/spreading feeling on the face is very reminiscent of glue. On my skin, it’s also not nearly moisturizing enough—it feels like it’s just sitting on top of my skin.

I wouldn’t recommend this for people with dry skin, it’s just not hydrating enough. The spreadability and odd glue-like feeling of the product is also just not for me. I like thick and emollient moisturizers (for instance, the Bobbi Brown Hydrating Face cream is one of my all-time favorites) and so I thought I’d like this one, but it doesn’t spread or absorb very well. It feels almost more like a gel than a cream.

I do still use this product, but only for my neck as an added skincare step at night. I no longer use it on my face.

title: I want my Remington back
text:
I had a Remington wet/dry that finally got outdated and I thought to replace it. I did a lot of research and decided to try this Panasonic. I was really excited when it got here and the first time I used it I loved it and was all set to write a raving review. But I thought I should wait a couple weeks. I am very unhappy with it, as it turns out. I wish I had my Remington back (or got a new Remington). Yes, the Remington is a little louder. But this one is loud too - you can hear both of them from many rooms away. So really, that's not a big deal. I ended up getting another Remington and it is much better.

What got me is two things with this one:
1) The sides that hold the razor in place are taller than the razor area. So when you go to get a close shave, the sides of the unit scratch/scrape your leg. It is plastic, so no blood drawn or anything, but it doesn't feel good. Has no one else noticed this? I went to do a quick shave on my calves and ended up with stripes from the sides of the unit scraping my legs. And it didn't even get the little stubble. I didn't think the Remington was that fantastic, but it did better than this. Someone suggested to put the side extenders down. I do see the extenders (per the angry reply to this post), but they are down all the way. The won't go any farther down. So your angry post is not applicable. If I did not apply force to my leg with the razor, the length of the stubble it left was ridiculous. Again, maybe very long stubble is just the way it is, but not with my two Remingtons. They got much closer without having to apply force.

2) It vents out the cut hair once in a while all over your leg. You could be shaving along la di da and all of a sudden get a huge area of hair. I thought "I already went over that area?" but it was just the hair that got spit out from the razor. It is a little gross, I'm always wiping the cut hair off my leg. I've had two Remington's that did not do this. The Remington might have left the hair on the ground, or kept it in its head for me to clean later, but I prefer the Remington that didn't spit out puffs of hair on my legs incrementally. Again, the angry reply to this about including a vacuum is a bit silly.

Another disadvantage is that this one's charger plugs straight into the outlet, instead of having a cord. So I have to find an outlet to leave it in to charge that my kids won't get to. I like the cord better, so I can plug the cord in behind my dresser and have it sitting on top of my dresser in the little charger base. This one, you have to put the razor in the charger directly into the outlet. I could deal with this though if it didn't spit hair out all over my leg or leave scrapes down my leg. Yes, you could get an extension cord, so it's not that big of a deal. Just one more thing to add to a poor design IMO.

title: Okay but nothing special.
text:
A plastic jar full of lavender-colored and -scented bath salts. (Apparently some of my Pre De Provence products are showing up in one review - so while this reveiw is for bath salts, I have the lavender lotion as well, which I do love the scent of it but as with the bath salts, wish the bottle were nicer).

There was no seal on the top of the jar, just the lid. That's fine, but I would wonder how long it would sit on a shelf before purchasing and how "fresh" the scent would last. That said, when I opened the lid and took a whiff, it was pretty powerfully scented. I like the lavender aspect but there's another scent there that I don't like and can't figure out what it is. It's off-putting. It doesn't linger in the water, so that's good.

I sprinkled some in my bathroom sink that I'd filled with warm water. The water turned a slight lavender shade as the bath salts turned clear. The salt crystals did melt pretty quickly, though as with any bath salts I've used there are always a few that are stubborn.

The water felt soft enough, I suppose-nothing really special, but that strong scent wasn't as apparent in the diluted water.

I did think it a bit pricey at just under $17 (at time of this review). For that price, I'd like a glass bottle or something prettier in the jar design itself, though the lavender-colored crystals do look pretty. Still, there are plenty of bath salts out there that are half the price and smell about the same, so what would make me want to purchase this one exclusively? Something that made it attractive to me, and that would be a pretty bottle/jar that I could display in my bathroom in my basket of bath goodies. Or, to give someone as a gift.

This plastic jar makes it seem like one of those cheaper jars of bath salts you can buy at Big Lots, which I can do for less than half the price if I want bath salts. Pretty it up some so I feel I'm getting my money's worth. You cold say Pre De Provence has quality ingredients and maybe that's why the price, but I'm not finding it special enough to pay almost $17.

title: Takes a little practice, but pretty in the end
text:
Very excited to get my first magnetic polishes. They came packaged very securely in foam and individually boxed. My first attempt didn’t go well, just couldn’t get it to work. Rather than constantly removing polish from own nails, I switched to pop sticks.

I started with a base coat of black. Once dry I painted one thick coat of the magnetic polish and immediately held the magnet over it, (in my experience it appears coat need to be thick and you need to work quickly) worked great!

So I attempted my own nails again, and it didn’t come out as well. I just couldn’t get as sharp of a line. It could be my nails are just to short with small nail beds, if the coat is to thick it floods my nails. I still love what I did get, when moving my fingers the line I did get appears to move, it’s very pretty and I got several compliments on them.

I did try using different magnets, stuff I had on my refrigerator as well as the Frcolor Double-head Stick Wand for 3 D Magnetic CAT Eye that I purchased on Amazon. It was a strong magnet, I had to really pull to get it off my fridge when I tested it. That magnet work best, As it was the strongest of what I had.

Overall, I like this polish and will enjoy using it.

title: Painful and kind of flawed
text:
Pros
• Sturdy and durable – The tweezers themselves are aluminum, but surprisingly sturdy.
• Great carrying case – Tweezers fit inside tube, just like a lipstick!
• Convenient mirror – Located inside of plastic tube that stores the tweezers.
• Easy to understand – Push a button and use.
• Light – Bright blue, useful in a way.
• Packaging – The packaging is honestly one of the best I’ve received a beauty product in. The bag is sheer with a ribbon in place for the draw string. It’s already filled with my other beauty products. The carrying case is what makes it though! It looks like a tube of lipstick, and when you remove the tweezers there’s a little mirror inside.
• Bellabe-esque spring wand – It works! It hurts like anything but man, it gets the job done. Beware areas with high density hair, it will nearly bring tears. Also, I didn’t find it effective on the outer lying hairs of my eyebrow, I believe the skin is too loose.

Cons
• Light – The button is flimsy and seems like it may break eventually. Also, when I attempted to turn the light off the first time I accidentally held down the button which actually made the light strobe. Also, it may seem silly but I felt like the light was a little too bright and washed out the area of my skin I was attacking. Finally, the light takes 3 of those watch like batteries, and I’m sorry to say that the odds of me taking time out of my day to go get these things once it dies are very slim. It does come with them included though, so for now that’s not an issue.
• Mirror – The mirror is definitely a convenience and the placement is a great idea, however, I feel like it would be more useful if the mirror was a magnifying one so I didn’t need to hold it so close to my face.
• Tweezers – The ends are not as slanted as I would like, and while I may be just tweezer challenged, I found myself chasing the same strand of hair for minutes at a time. It would be great if you could switch the tweezers that the light attaches to, but that doesn’t seem possible.

Overall, while the packaging for this product is awesome, I don’t think it’s for me. But hey, I could just be less tweezer savvy than others.

text:
I have been using Philips/ Norelco shavers for the past 12 years; and for the past 5 years, I have been using the 8894 model. for no good reason, I wanted a change and assumed that the new Philips Norelco 1090 would be more improved than the 8894.

1. Louder.
2. less power; 65 minutes verses 100 minutes
3. the shave is not better; practically the 8894 shaves closer.
4. Plastic casing; 8894 had a leather travel case.
5. Slightly lighter than the 8894.
6. All the 10 series, rate the same
Bottom line if you have been using the 8894 and want a change; my advice is stick to your old shaver and save the money. If you are buying a new shaver, go for the 7810 instead, as the 8894 is no longer in stock.

TLDR: GET THIS mask if you know you dont react to fragrance and simply like the smell of honey. DO NOT get this mask if you are looking for a mask with lots of honey and no added fragrance ingredients.

My skin loves honey. I have therefore tried many honey masks in pursuit of one that my face loves the most. I almost returned this face mask because when I recieved it, one of them seemed to have leaked through the plastic package they were bundled in. However, after deciding that my face needed honey and it wasn't really worth it to return it, I decided to give these guys a go.

This concerned me of course as when something smells amazing it usually has fragrance added to it. When looking at the ingredients, I found that it does have "fragrance" in the ingredients, though it is farther down on the list of ingredients so it is not very much.

Near the bottom too, however, is propolis. Which is the only ingredient related to honey in this mask. Which was rather disappointing as this means this mask has hardly any honey in it.

I probably wont reorder this unless my skin somehow loves it.

title: Thin lotion, but works well for me
text:
I was a little hesitant about getting this set, since it is a little bit pricey and is a rose scented lotion (I can be sensitive to floral smells in particular). I figured I'd like the cuticle oil, and the lotion less so. But it actually turned out to be the other way around - I like the lotion better than the cuticle oil.
The lotion itself is very, very thin, almost the consistency of water, but it does work well for me. Before I used it, my knuckles were cracked to the point of bleeding. I applied a generous amount before bed, and that first night it healed my hands enough that they were no longer bleeding, just cracking a little bit. Even with my handwashing and having my hands frequently wet at work, this lotion brought them back to life. The second use resulted in no more cracks. The third brought my hands back to feeling normal. Since then, I've been using a more moderate amount only a couple of times a week (note the bottle DID come completely full - the pictures are after about three weeks of use, with the first week of that using a lot more than I normally would, due to how bad my hands were cracking). The lotion does have a definite floral scent, but it's actually a lot lighter than I expected it to be. My skin absorbs it pretty fast, within about 5-10 minutes even using a ton, and the scent fades pretty much completely even before this. So it doesn't bother me at all.
The cuticle oil, on the other hand, has a much stronger scent. It's more "planty" and less pleasant to me. Definitely not something I can use when I already have even a hint of a headache. Also, it lingers a lot more than the lotion's scent does. I do like the roller applicator as it makes it much easier to control my application onto my dominant hand, but I don't feel that this cuticle oil is anything better than any other one I've used. Combine that with the smell of it, and I definitely like the lotion in this set better. It is pricey, but to help my hands as much as it has, I think it's worth it.

title: Argan Oil Is Not Snake Oil
text:
I've been used this specific shampoo only a couple of times as it was offered by vendor as a 'for review' item but we've been into Argan Oil shampoos for the past half year or so and we are very happy with the results. In fact our teenage daughter insists that whatever shampoo we purchase it contains the Argan Oil.

This shampoo provided a thorough, gentle cleaning of my hair and scalp and there is not discomfort or itchy feeling whatsoever after use which is a good thing. Our daughter likes it too but she observed that 'it smells funny'. I do agree that there is a strong, not necessarily unpleasant, smell for a brief few seconds while you are applying the shampoo on hair.

Additional facts worth sharing:

- It comes in a tube and a tube this size should probably last 2-3 months if used by a couple of people so, while the price is higher than what you'll typically see at a supermarket, it's not THAT high when spread over several months and it's worth the extra few dollars.
- While it's not stated anywhere, it seems to act as a conditioner. I would not use use a conditioner after this shampoo myself.
- For what is worth, the ingredients include: Aloe leaf extract, Argan oil, Xanthan gum and dozen of ingredients that are difficult to spell or pronounce but the maker promise that there are no petrochemical derivatives or parabens and that no animal testing was conducted.

The odds are I will continue to use this shampoo until I am made aware of a superior product. Until then, I am happy with it.

title: The G380: a questionable price for a non-upgrade to the G370...
text:
This [[ASIN:B000FED5DK Philips Norelco G380 All-in-1 Grooming System]] isn't nearly as good as the cheaper (newer) version, the [[ASIN:B000FED5DU Philips Norelco G370 All-in-1 Grooming System]]. This one you're looking at can never be worth $80+ I've researched this G380 on Philips website and is shows that the G380 is actually older (2006) than the G370 (2010) that is much cheaper and better - I've used both.

I've used the [[ASIN:B000FED5DU Philips Norelco G370 All-in-1 Grooming System]] for almost 4 years now. And when I say I've used it, I mean I've used about 3-4 a year because I cut my own hair with it. At $15-$20 each, it is worth the price. Yes, the G370 has some faults but it just works. With that said, this review is for the [[ASIN:B000FED5DK Philips Norelco G380 All-in-1 Grooming System]] & it is almost identical to the [[ASIN:B000FED5DU Philips Norelco G370 All-in-1 Grooming System]] except for the color and the stand.

Buy the [[ASIN:B000FED5DU Philips Norelco G370 All-in-1 Grooming System]] instead of this overpriced one - the G380.

Lastly, as a product designer, I've tried to comprehend what Philips Norelco could do to upgrade the $15-ish G370 to the $80+ G380? Nothing... The only faults I've had with the G370 is that the 'spring' mechanism that allows you to vary the cutting height no longer provides the proper resistance after many uses - resulting in some varied height. Again, I used the G370 once a week to cut my hair.

One more addition is that I started to search for a 'stubble' trimmer for my face and the [[ASIN:B000FED5DU Philips Norelco G370 All-in-1 Grooming System]] works wonderfully for that! Just awesome, actually.

This face wash by Whitney Jean is a clear gel with no smell so I had high hopes for it being safe for sensitive skin/areas. Unfortunately when washing near my eyes as it’s advertised as “makeup remover” it irritates my eyes a bunch so much to where it burned. I tried to include a image result of what google said but my review keeps getting flagged for it, but in short: “ethylhexylglycerin is not safe due to its performance as a contact allergen. People with sensitive skin and existing skin conditions are more likely to be impacted by products containing this ingredient”.
It did remove my makeup well but at the cost of a burning feeling around my eyes for over half an hour it’s not worth it if I only can clean half my face with it especially for $20…

title: Good, but not magical
text:
Well they say “expectations are the source of all unhappiness”, and maybe that’s the problem. I was expecting this soap to be significantly better than the glycerin-based soaps I’ve been using (which cost a third of what this does), and it just... isn’t. It does a good job, and it lasts a long time, but I didn’t notice any improvement in lubricity or lather richness over my previous soaps.
And the scent was inoffensive, but underwhelming.
As for long-lasting, see the attached picture for what the soap looks like after two months of daily use. It (quite literally) barely made a dent in it. So that’s a plus in the “value” department.
One other issue that may or may not be the soap’s fault: the steel travel tin I was using it in had been used for months with other soaps, and no problems. With this soap, it rusted to uselessness in two months. (The inside, around and under the soap, was completely oxidized and flaking off.) That was curious to me, but I don’t have enough data to say it was definitely caused by the soap.
In summary, it’s a decent soap. Kind of expensive, but I don’t mind paying for quality. But somehow, I was expecting something like mythical powers out of a lanolin soap, and they’re just not there.

title: Hard pressed, don’t pick much up, not very pigmented. Wish they provided more photos to choose color
text:
This claims to be titanium dioxide free, gluten free, made with natural and organic ingredients, vegan, and free of parabens, nano-particles, bismuth oxychloride, talc, silicones, mineral oil, GMOs, artificial fragrance, artificial preservatives, FD&C dyes, carmine, and phthalates. It is made in the USA. The ingredient list is on the product box and it is really short (see photos). It claims to be formulated with natural ingredients, such as Kaolin Clay and Jojoba Oil. They say they are cruelty free. The product page has a photo that says “Leaping Bunny Certified,” but the logo on the box is a PETA logo. I checked both websites and HYNT Beauty is certified by both Leaping Bunny and PETA.

I got the shade “Linen Kiss.” A little searching online showed it was a matte ivory. I really didn’t like they didn’t have much info at all about the shades to choose from. There weren’t any descriptions of the different shades to say whether they were matte, shimmer, etc. There weren’t photos other than the product in the little singles compact. I would have liked to have seen more product photos, like swatches comparing the different shades to help me choose, or at least a description of each shade. I had to search on Google and even when I went to their website there were only 4 shade options there. At least there they had a description for the 4 shades, but they only had the single photo of each in the singles compact. For a single eyeshadow coating $22, I expect more. The focus on the ingredients and what isn’t included is good, but they should also put a little attention on providing customers with more photos so they can easily pick a shade that’s right for them and be happy when the get it. Not have to guess what finish it has or if they shade is going to look like it does in the pan when they get it.

This comes in a little ziplock bag. Inside is a little outer product box.

It comes in a plastic singles compact. The top flips open easily.

It’s a matte ivory.

I show a photo where I swatched it. I did a finger swatch on my clean forearm (no lotion, primer, etc.). I swirled my finger in the pan and it seemed really hard pressed, like I wasn’t picking up much. I looked at my finger to see what I had picked up and should have been surprised after how much I swirled it in the pan that I didn’t have more, but I wasn’t really because of how hard pressed it felt. I took a photo showing it on my finger. As you can see, it isn’t very opaque and doesn’t look like I picked much up. I swirled a lot and that’s all I got. I swiped that onto my forearm. Then I went back into the pan. This time I pressed harder into the pan while I swirled. I picked up the same amount and put a second layer over the first one I had already done. Then, I did the same thing and did a different swipe. I did 3 layers for that one to show how it built up. It showed up enough on my fair skin, but I wasn’t a fan with how hard pressed this was. Maybe if I didn’t get such a light shade I’d like it more? But, I feel like the formula just isn’t too great and wouldn’t have great pigmentation with any color.

It’s nice and smooth.

Overall, its okay. It’s not for me. For me to spend $22 for a single eyeshadow, the eyeshadow needs to be pretty darn good. This just isn’t it. It’s too hard pressed for my liking. You don’t pick up much product and even when you do it doesn’t have that much pigmentation. Like I said, maybe with a different color it would be different, but I don’t think so. There’s way better options out there. I don’t recommend this.
