title: Antioxidant packed, but does burn your eyes!
text:
This cleansing water is JAM PACKED with antioxidant ingredients, 5 types of berries to be exact! This contains Cloudberry, Bilberry, Sea Buckthorn Berry, Raspberry, and Blackberry. It also contains birch tree sap and sunflower seed oil to help lock in that much loved moisture! I've been using this product for a couple of weeks and I'll say, it's a great cleansing water. This does a fantastic job in removing my face makeup or the "dewyness" in the morning (aka morning grease). Give this bottle a quick shake to combine the cleansing water and oil together, pour a little on a cotton pad, and swipe away! Quick, easy, and my skin truly feels refreshed after use. Because this product is packed with brightening ingredients, my skin is beaming after (which justifies its name "Radiance Me"). If you are looking for a product that combines two steps in one, then this is something I definitely recommend trying out.
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀
😢 Drawbacks: This product does burn my eyes when trying to remove my eyeliner and mascara, so I would not recommend using this product around the eye area. Also, for my oily skin peeps out there, I would recommend using this as a night cleansing water rather than a day one IF you are planning to go out for the day. I say this because it is a mix of water and oil and does leave a slight "oily" residue on the skin after, so this product may give you a bit more shine than you'd like if you have oily skin. But nothing a few swipes of toner on a cotton pad can't fix! If you are on the more dry side, then this should be perfect for you!

title: Stay away from this hair color!
text:
I previously had my hair purple but due to inconsistent bleaching some purple washed off much quicker than other parts. Seeing the good reviews on this product, I decided to give Splat! Lusty Lavender a go. The bleach in this kit is REALLY harsh. Be careful not to get it on your skin, or it will burn.

I noticed when I opened both of the bottles (getting two kits) the purple might have had a chance of turning a light purple, but I thought it might redarken (like my initial purple did). I left it on for an hour. When I washed it off, it came out a bright magenta. I did not wash this one off with a shampoo, and either way the dye was lighter than it should have been.

The N-Rage plum color [[ASIN:B003JN2NXW N Rage Purple Plum]] washes out quicker if you did not bleach correctly, but it does last and it is stronger (Just be careful because depending on the bleaching it might come out dark violet or plum; don't commit my error and consistently bleach before!). I thought I made a mistake but this had to be the thinnest, lightest purple dye I've used besides quick washes. I'll try leaving it on for several hours next time, but if you want an immediately more effective (and better smelling) dye try the N Rage dye. If anyone has tried the purple Amore dye, please let me know!

The wipes aren’t too wet. I do a lot of makeup swatches of eyeshadow palettes and things like that. So, I constantly am using makeup wipes to wipe the swatches off of my arms. These work good for that. I wouldn’t use them on my face because, while they’re wet enough to wipe the swatches off my arms, I need to rub more than I do with my usual wipes. Given that, I wouldn’t want to use them on my face where I’d need to rub hard, pulling my skin. It’s not good to use makeup wipes to remove your makeup anyways, since it can tug at your skin and because they usually don’t remove all of your makeup. I still sometimes like to use makeup wipes to wipe the majority of my makeup off, then go in and cleanse my face. But, again, I just wouldn’t use these for that. With the odd smell and needing to rub more to get the makeup off, I wouldn’t want to use these on my face. But, for getting the swatches off my arms they work good.

So, for purposes of wiping swatches off my arm, they work good enough. As I said earlier, with the weird smell and them being not that wet, causing me to need to rub harder, I just wouldn’t use them on my face.

text:
Those new XL shaving heads make a huge difference. The additional blades they added change the whole feel of the shave for the better. The shave is a more friendly shave. It is very quiet and I must agree with another reviewer that it sounds like it's on low power. It's not. I thought that the new heads would shorten the amount of time I needed to shave but that wasn't true. It took just as long. Go figure. I would have given this razor 5 stars except after I got it I realized that it does not have a low battery indicator. That was an unwelcome surprise. The 8150XL or 8151XL does.
ADDITIONAL REVIEW AFTER TWO MONTHS OF USE: Other razors wind down slowly when running out of juice. Not this one, it goes from full speed ahead to dead in three seconds. When it does that, turn it off and then back on. It seems to have another 30 seconds of shaving when you do that. I don't know if this was an accidental or intentional design but that little trick is not in the manual.

title: Not a great choice for a vegan product
text:
Immediately after purchasing this product, I gave it a four-star review. However, after six months of owning it, I have decided that it is not right for me and am changing my rating.

I have watery eyes, oily lids, and long lashes, meaning anything I put on top of the lid is going to end up underneath it in a few hours. After reading hundreds of reviews of vegan, organic liquid liners, I decided to give this one a chance because of all the good reviews. I liked it a lot in some regards, but there were too many drawbacks, which I will detail here. Hopefully this will help you decide if this product is right for you.
Pros:
- No irritation
- Does not smudge or transfer to under eye area, even after exercise (yay!!)
- Removes easily with normal facial cleanser (double yay!!)
- Very black
Cons:
- Difficult to apply, even with an expert hand. (I am all about identical, precise cat eyes.) During application, if you lift up the brush once and then try to continue your line, you will find that it scratches into what you have already applied and leaves gaps that need to be covered up with careful dabbing of more product. After three or four applications, I got used to the consistency of the formula, but this is one of the biggest drawbacks of this product. (Also, even though as a whole it comes off very easily at the end of the day, fixing little mistakes with just some water or spit is quite difficult for some reason, perhaps because the product is still tacky.)
- The liner does not sink into your skin, meaning it sits on top of your eyelid and will flake off over the course of a day. Miraculously, it doesn't give you raccoon eyes, but it does create a ragged edge or little gaps in your liner that are obvious up close.
- Having used various pen, liquid, and gel liners over the years, I find the design of this brush terrible. It is not a bristle brush; it is more of an inflexible point. The design also makes it so you can't grip very closely to the tip, giving you less control. This makes it so you end up with a coat of liner on your lashes (I do have long lashes, for the record). Like I said, the applicator just does not allow a lot of control, especially when you're trying to go back in and fix precise gaps.

I appreciate that this product is vegan and organic, but let's be honest... you can't have your cake and eat it, too. I couldn't deal with the frustrations of the application. I ended up tossing this product and purchasing Black Noir Waterproof liner by NYX that is ah-MA-zing. It is everything this product is not, albeit a little more chemical-y.

Next problem: Norelco suggests that you replace the cartridge for sanitary reasons each time you refill the lotion. OK, but when I ordered the lotion (which is supposed to come with the cartridge), THERE WAS NO CARTRIDGE! So, I decided to stick it out anyway. Each time I replaced the lotion, I would just remove the cartridge and clean it myself. That seemed fine, until this morning when I accidentally broke a piece of this fragile cartridge. Now, I can't get the lotion to come out, so the razor is ineffective. I tried to buy a new lotion with cartridge at Target, and the lotion came without the cartridge, so I have to return it.

I know Phillips-Norelco has excellent customer service, so I called to see if they could help me. It turns out that the lotion does not always come with the cartridge (although it is advertised that way and I was told that it came with the cartridge by a customer service rep before I bought the razor). So, it's kind of like a little guessing game. Where can I find the lotion and cartridge together? Fun! I asked if they could just send me some cartridges, no lotion, just cartridges and I'd be happy. But they could not do that, so I am going to return this razor and get my money back.

I still have a previous Norelco shaver (dry) and I will try that again, although it is not as good. I think in the end I may have to resort back to the painful manual razor shave. I have been a Norelco customer for many years and up to this point I was always very pleased, this is disappointing.

To summarize: This is an excellent razor, but it is not worth the money or the hassle you have to go through to make it work effectively!

I welcome any shaving advice to help my sensitive skin!

title: Works well IF...
text:
The first time I used this, I could barely get the polish to lift up. I used cuticle oil and a cuticle pusher and I wound up tearing up some of my natural nail. After doing some reading, I saw a suggestion to use a traditional basecoat under the gel peel off basecoat. I thought that it sounded silly, but I was willing to try it, as I wanted to have an easy way to take off my gel polish. I have been using Nailtiques Nail Protein Formula 2 as my basecoat because my nails are thin and then tend to peel. Then I put the gel peel off basecoat over the Nailtiques. After that I polish as usual with whatever color/brand of gel polish I have selected. I used an orange stick to assist with lifting and peeling off the polish when I want to remove it, Following this method has worked REALLY well for me and I have done it 4 or 5 times now. No natural nail lifting up! This also lasts a long longer than when I tried to use UNT. UNT lifted on my nails after one 1-2 days usually. This lasts *easily* 1 week+ for me. Capping the free edge properly is key. I rated it 4 stars because, IMO, I shouldn't have to use a traditional basecoat with the peel off basecoat.

UPDATE 12.6.16: I have found that using an orange stick to assist in lifting the gel polish is a KEY FACTOR in making sure that your natural nail does not lift. I figured this out last night. Additional tips for minimal damage: file down your nails prior to taking off the polish. Breaking the seal on the free edge and then washing your hands helps loosen things up, making it easier to lift. Happy peeling!

title: OK enough, but not the game changer for me
text:
This cream was just ok for me. I bought this after my most recent nighttime moisturizer went out (Cetaphil) because I'm trying to shift my skin care regimen to more natural ingredients now that I'm pregnant, but I don't think it was any more moisturizing than anything else I've used in the past, and it definitely didn't seem to make my acne-prone skin any better. The scent was fine for me. (I was still using my Cerave with SPF for my daytime cream because I didn't want to throw it away.)

I ended up switching my moisturizers just three days ago to Bee Naturals Best Oil Free Moisturizer for both my day (with sunblock - Blue Lizard - Australian Sunscreen Face Daily Moisturizer Fragrance Free 30 SPF) and night time moisturizer (by itself), and this has worked out ten times better for me. Instead of waking up each morning discovering new cystic acne bumps and a scattering of blackheads all over my cheeks, or using 2-6 oil blotting sheets during the day, my face has felt clean yet moisturized, and I think my acne-prone skin is finally getting better!

In summary, I think AquaTica Organic Botanical Night Cream is fine and can be good for a lot of people, but it wasn't the game changer for me -- I have eczema, I'm pregnant, I have acne-prone skin already that's gotten worse since pregnant, and my face is generally oily. I don't think it made things worse, it moisturized, the scent didn't bother me, and it did make me feel better that I was using something natural, but it didn't make my skin noticeably better, especially because I still broke out.

We gave this 3 test uses for an initial assessment of this back scrubber/brush. It is designed nicely, with handles that make usage very user friendly. If they made this out of elastic, you could shower and do resistance band exercises. hehe. Seriously, the handles work well, and act as convenient loops to hang the device to dry out in the shower.
There is an issue with using silicone brush heads, they tend to be soft/flexible. So, if you use this brush, do not expect the same experience as a loofah or bristle brush. And, you have to really work up a lather in your hands and then transfer it to the silicone brush head. Attempts to create foam/lather by rubbing body wash or soap on the silicone just wasn't satisfactory.
As mentioned, the brush surface tends to be soft/gentle. The 'scrubbing' side does rub, but nowhere near deep cleaning or exfoliating level. The bumpy side, for massage, does provide a textured rub, but is even less effective for soaping and cleaning your back.
Maybe I'm too old school, liking my cleaning brush to be able to really scrub.
Attached are photos to show real world images, with a ruler for size reference.
Did not use the included hooks, because we used the shower caddy that already had hooks for shower accessories. The bonus bath sponge looks fine, but did not use that yet. Again, maybe I don't pamper myself enough while showering. haha. If the significant other uses it, any pertinent information will be added to this review. However, I think the majority of people will be concerned about the effectiveness and quality of the back scrubber.
So, the product does match the description and depiction in the product details. However, my opinion is the softness of the brush hinders the effectiveness as a shower back scrubbing device. I do like that it is very resistant to mold and is extremely easy to clean and maintain. Maybe I have to learn to adapt to the softer texture of this type of brush. Based on our experience, this silicone brush garners a 3.5 rating. If you already use and like silicone back scrubbers, this is a quality product worth considering. If you are old school, this might disappoint expectations.

title: Top notch. Excellent quality set. Exellent bargain/value.
text:
There are two important aspects regarding this product. Price and quality...and both are positive impressions.
In terms of cost, with the current coupon, the $8 cost of this set is not just an excellent value, it's an amazing bargain. That would be a good value for just the rose quartz gua sha, alone. Even if this was a mediocre, average quality massage duo set, $8 would still represent a very good value. And, as the following review will note, the components of this set are more than worth that price.
I consider the gua sha to be the lesser of the two pieces. Still, it is a good quality rose quartz stone, with beautiful coloration. it has ample polishing, affording a shiny and smooth surface. The contour is adequately and evenly rounded with the same smooth surface as the rest of the gua sha. Close examination of the stone finds no defects or cracks, no scratches or nicks. The only concern is the gua sha is a bit thinner than I prefer. Gua sha stones seem to follow two paths: thicker with more of a rounded aspect and thinner/flattened stones that seem to be a slice of rose quartz, that's then polished to smooth out the surface and edges. This gua sha is in the latter category. It's still a valid, credible gua sha.
The highlight piece is the massage roller. This has two sizable roller heads. One is the typical smooth roller, while the other is a segmented/ribbed roller. The smooth roller is nicely polished, while the ribbed roller has more of a natural texture. On a normal dual sided massage roller, there are two different sized smooth rollers. On this tool, the rollers are distinctly different, but approximately the same size. This gives the tool a good balance.
The massage roller has the plastic grommets where the metal arm/axle enters the roller. This serves to protect the rose quartz and the metal arm from abrasive interaction. It also acts a bearing, affording a quiet and smooth rolling action. Furthermore, the plastic grommet is larger and better designed than other quality massage rollers. Another nice design feature is the metal collar/ring on the metal arm/axle at the intersection point. This design aspect is found on premium level massage rollers.
Attached are photos to show real world images of the product offering, with a ruler for size reference. Various angles and close ups are provided.
I am very impressed with the quality of design, materials and manufacture. It clearly met expectations. If the gua sha was the thicker version, this set would rate a 5+ star rating. So, if you prefer the thinner/flattened gua sha then you'll love this set. Based on my personal preferences, and overall positive impression of this set, due to the gua sha, the product receives "only' a 5- star rating. Yes, a 5 minus, just a very slight negative based on the gua sha preference. A very high level recommendation for this product.

title: Without A Doubt The Absolute Biggest Piece Of Crap I've Ever Bought
text:
And that doesn't only go for razors. This thing is the worst purchase of any kind I've ever made in
my entire life. Nearly $200 worth of junk.

I've used nothing but Norelco razors since I was 15 years old. That is well over 25 years now. I've
bought more than 10 different Norelcos over the years. I had not and would not even consider
buying any other brand of razor. Some were better than others, but none even begins to compare
to this piece of junk. The then 10 year old razor I got as a hand-me-down when I was 15 shaved
100 times better than this piece of crap ever did.

I've always bought the top of line Norelco whenever something new and "better" came out. This
piece of crap was no exception. Oh how great they made it look on the commercials all over the
TV. The wonder shaver of shavers, they claimed. Just read the company description here on this
page. It is all lies.

Now I'm not all haired up like a gorilla or anything. I have just normal thickness of hair and
growth. I usually shave every day and with every other Norelco I've ever owned I could get the
job done in less than 3 minutes. Using this hunk of junk it takes well over 15 minutes of rubbing,
scrubbing, and shoving this thing around trying to get it to work. I've tried stretching my skin so
tight that the skin on my neck was pulled up to my earlobe and it still doesn't cut the hair. I've
tried going back and forth, up and down, around in circles, clockwise, counter clockwise,
everything imaginable and no matter how you do it, this piece of junk just does not shave.

Even with brand new blades this razor misses about 1 in 10 hairs on my neck. And when I say it
misses them, I mean it completely misses them. They are not cut at all. It misses about twice as
many under the jaw line. And all of this is after 15+ minutes of shaving! So much for their line of
"even on the neck".

Oh and don't worry, no one will be able to miss that you look like you had a blindfolded 3 year
old give you 10 second shave. I can assure you that after nearly half an hour of ramming and
scrubbing this thing around on your neck, it will have a nice red glow for about 2 or 3 hours that
just screams "hey look at my 15 minute halfass shave". And I do not even have sensitive skin.

If you plan to use the pop up trimmer it is as big of a joke as the rest of the razor. It is about half
an inch wide and while it does work better than the rest of the razor it sounds like a wood chipper
when it is cutting. Think I'm joking? Just get one and try it. The first time I used it I actually
yanked it away from my neck. It didn't pinch or cut me but the sound of it made me think that it
had.

Oh and do not let me forget, you also get the pleasure of stopping and emptying the hair
chambers at least twice during each shave. If you fail to do this it cuts even worse (if such a thing
is possible) because this razor effectively does not have a place to store what hair it does manage
to cut. There are 3 individual hair "chambers" on the razor. One for each cutting head. They fill
up very quickly and then begin to puke the cut hair all over whatever you are standing over while
you are "shaving".

Now after you clean the bathroom sink (or wherever you were) of all the puked hair, you still get
to clean the razor. Don't worry, it is just as easy as running it under the faucet, right? That is what
they claim. Simply running it under the facet works for a few times but that does not get
everything out of the razor and it builds up over the course of a few days.

Now the geniuses that made this piece of junk cleverly decided to make the cutting head all one
piece. Unlike every other Norelco I've ever owned you can not take the cutters out of the combs
and clean them. They are made as all one piece. You cannot even take the cutter and comb out of
the head, everything is all molded together. All you can do is stick the cleaning brush that they
give you (which is as big a piece of junk as the razor) in behind the cutters and try to scrape out
what you can while spinning the cutter around and around. I quickly wore out the the cleaning
brush they supplied and started using a stiff bristle toothbrush instead. That doesn't work very
well either but it is much better than what they give you.

I've tried many different ways of cleaning the heads of this thing and the best way I came up with
was to use a container with a sealable lid and fill it halfway with very hot water. Spray some
cleaner on the head and put it in the container of water and shake it around as hard as you can for
a couple of minutes. I used foaming bathroom cleaner to clean it. Worked well. Might as well use
what you have and with this razor you are going to use a lot of that anyway to clean up all of the
puked hair.

Lastly, if while shaving you are unfortunate enough to get anywhere near to the hair on your head
with this wonder machine, it will suck it up like a Hoover from 3 inches away. Can't cut the hair
on your face and neck to save its life but it will grab hold of your hair from 3 inches away a suck
it into the cutters. Now with the other Norelcos I've had that was never too much of a problem.
You just take the cutter and comb apart and take the stray hair out, but remember this was
designed as a single piece so you do not get to do that. I've spent 5 minutes many times, fishing a
single head hair out of one of the cutters.

So in conclusion, just how bad is this razor?

After a year of all of the above I have just completely had it with the piece junk. And like I said, I've never
owned any other brand of razor, but I feel completely lied to, cheated, and ripped off by this razor
and Norelco. My solution: I have just ordered a Panasonic and I will never again buy anything
made by Norelco. I hope they choke on my money, they will never get another cent of it. EVER!

Are you going to give them yours?

I wouldn't be so upset about it, but these are not returnable at all and I bought two packs of 50 based on the product description.

Yes, the jar comes in a box, but anything could have gotten in the jar before it was placed into that box. I don’t know anyone that doesn’t feel a little uncomfortable when a cosmetic/skin care product doesn’t have a safety seal. It’s really disappointing because I was really looking forward to trying this.

title: Yes, these really work...but keep a few things in mind
text:
After very minimal and barely noticeable success with whitening toothpastes and gels, I finally decided to give Crest Premium Whitestrips a try. Previously, I had found the cost to be prohibitive, but the fact that $5 or $7 coupons are offered in our Sunday paper with some regularity made the price a bit easier to swallow.

Just like the commercials say, I definitely did begin to see some improvement after about three days. I would describe the effect as more of a lightening than a whitening per se: the darker yellow spots on my teeth began to fade and to become less apparent. Now, after using the product as prescribed for a week, the color of my teeth is clearly improved; I wouldn't say that my teeth are bright white, but they are definitely more of an ivory or a paler yellow color. According to the package insert, you can immediately begin a second course of treatment for even better whitening effects, but I haven't yet decided if I want to lay out another $30 in order to do this. Also, I should mention that the effect is not so dramatic thta anyone has noticed (UNLIKE in the commercials!).

Now for the caveats. First of all, I found these strips to be a bit difficult to use. It can be hard to remove the strips from the protective backing without them becoming mangled, and it is very easy to get the gel on your fingertips (which causes a temporary whitening effect). Also, the strips are not ideally shaped for your mouth, and I found that they covered my front eight teeth only. Finally, while the top strip adhered fairly well, I found that the bottom strip was more tricky and tended to slide around, especially if I moved my mouth at all. The only solution I found to this was to wear the strips while commuting to work, which luckily gave me a 30-minute period when I did not need to talk. Otherwise, it can be difficult to find a good time to wear the strips, as the insert information advises against wearing them immediately after you brush your teeth, while sleeping, and while you are eating/drinking.

Unlike other reviewers, I did not have a problem with the taste of the strips: I could not detect anything while wearing them, and after taking them off, I thought that the gooey paste left behind was virtually tasteless. I did experience some sensitivity in a lower tooth which I had capped over 20 years ago. Although this sensation went away in time, it was uncomforable enough to make me cut the lower strip to fit around this particular tooth.

In summary, I did see clear--although not miraculous--results from this product and I would be willing to try the strips again, especially if the price were to come down a bit. Ultimately, I would rate Crest Whitestrips three and a half stars, as there is definitely room for improvement.

title: Sensitive Girl Approved. Not perfect but overall okay!
text:
Excellent set of brushes with pretty good quality.
#1 rule when buying Bella and bear products: get on their email list for discount codes! I paid a little more than half of the current price for this set. Even at full price it's a good value (price per brush) but due to a few quirks I recommend not paying full price.
I'm a makeup junkie and own many brushes ranging from handmade very expensive Japanese brushes to easily accessible drug-store brand sets. I prefer synthetic brushes due to allergies and skin sensitives and I believe most of these are synthetic or blends.
The set arrived from Amazon in a very nice giftable thick sturdy box. I'm actually using the box and lid as liners in one of my makeup drawers.
I have broken down this review into two sections brushes and the case.
Brushes:
Handles are semi-matte black and the ferules are silver metal and appear to be crimped on which is very nice. The handles/ferules remind me of IT Cosmetics brushes. They are very well made, heavier constructed, and feature the company and brush name stamped on them.
Brush quality is good over all. Except for one of the brushes, they are all very soft and the density is appropriate for the applications.
Foundation, stippling, large shadow, and smudge shadow brushes are not evenly cut. There is noticeable uneven brush hairs with all 4 of these. The application with these particular brushes is okay but it's not as smooth as it would be with perfectly cut brushes.
The flat yellow brush is made of a taklon or nylon type material. It's large, thick, flat, and useless. It doesn't work with any kind of makeup in any kind of application because as soon as it touches skin, it splays, or splits. It's not flexible or functional. I have put it aside for craft applications, as it might work to pat on glue or something like that.
MY favorite brushes are the white shadow blending blushes, they work very well for blending shadow lines.
Runners up are the larger powder brushes for setting powder and bronzer/blush applications.
Even with the damage to the portfolio, some brushes are not cut properly, and one is useless, this is still an excellent value.

text:
This is a tricky review to write. When I received the product, my initial reaction was, "What is this?" The photo on this item's page is very misleading. The product is not a dark creamy brown looking thing. It's basically pale brown colored sugar crystals. That's it. I contacted the seller with a photos (see photos) and said there seems to be something missing. They assured me "As for the packaging, thanks for letting me know, we will have it modified accordingly this week." I'm not sure what that means, but besides the photo being completely different, the description indicates it's 8.8 oz and it's an organic brown sugar. The ingredients don't indicate "organic" at all and the label on the jar states it's 7 oz. So it's not the product I thought I was purchasing. I'm bothered that the photo was SO different than the product I received. I honestly thought the cream or oil must have evaporated or something.

That said, my testing of the product has been odd and I'm torn about an accurate star rating. The first day, I wet my arm and took a scoop of the crystals and rubbed them over my arm. All of the crystals fell off into the sink within seconds and other than being wet, my arm was exactly the same. I was thinking that even one star was too generous for a useless product. Today, I gave it another try. I scooped the crystals up with my fingers instead of the plastic scoop. I did my best to keep them on my arm this time. My arm turned pretty pink during this process and I really didn't know what to expect. I was only able to do this for about 40 seconds before I lost the last of the crystals. I rinsed my arm and was impressed by how soft my arm felt. However, I know you can take salt and product a similar softness by using some oil along with it. So I don't know....it softens the skin but at the rate it's been disappearing on me, the product won't last long and there's really nothing extraordinary about it.

Note: I was able to purchase this item, at a discount, for my honest review.

title: I like it but
text: I've been fighting the war of the beards since about 1952 when I was working at a TV shop where we sold Shick electric shavers so that's what I started with. Except during army basic training I have never used anything but electric. I bought a Norelco rotary at the PX once and promptly gifted it to another soldier as it always lost the battle against my beard. Many years later I was very happy using the shaver that caused Victor Kiam to purchase Remington and I still have several of those that use the now unavailable SP42 head. As it's replacement I have an MS2 that uses the SP69 head. That gives a nice close shave but it's gone from the sales world too. It is great for a close shave but no good if it's been over a day so the SP42 is used first to shorten the long stuff then the SP69 to finish the job. I was hoping this Wahl 7061-900 would be a good replacement for both those old shavers and it makes a good compromise. With a lot of effort it will plow through a 2 day growth and the final result is decent but not as close as the Remington with the SP69 head. I have not mastered the trimmer yet so I go back to either of my old Remingtons for trimming sideburns and to get a straight line on my mustache. If replacement heads ever become available for this shaver I'm hoping they may have solved the close shave problem but I think possibly there is no way to get a close shave and a 2 day beat down out of the same head. I guess the close shave requires a very thin screen while the 2 day requires larger holes that can't be put in a thin screen.

Cons -

title: Works well, if you're careful and use it right.
text:
It works pretty well. It's more painful to use than the Emjoi Seal Wet/Dry Epilator, however it seems to get my skin a lot smoother than the other one does. I've found it works well dry, or in the shower, with soapy skin. (DO NOT USE ON DAMP SKIN!!!)

It gets my skin fairly smooth, but not quite as smooth as shaving.

Really, my only complaint about this item (and the reason I'm knocking 2 stars off), is that it doesn't stop if it catches the skin, like the Emjoi Seal Wet/Dry Epilator does. I can use the other epilator in all the delicate nooks and crannies, and have no fear of rashes, nicks, or bleeding. This one, on the other hand, has left me with some pretty nasty cuts in places that I won't mention. The obvious solution to the problem is to make sure you only use it on short hair, and to hold the skin very taut, before going over it. But, sometimes you're too lazy to trim the hair, or sometimes you don't realize the skin isn't taut enough, and it can leave some pretty nasty cuts on you.

But if you're careful, and use it right, it does work well.

text:
So, first off: knocking off some stars because one shade is absolutely Not Okay. Heck, even something like a ‘light/medium/dark’ 3 shade range would be better than this ONE SHADE. I don’t buy the argument that because it’s a K Beauty brand, this is find. There are so many reasons that this isn’t acceptable, and I urge you to read up on why. Bottom line: it’s 2018, and make up should be inclusive.

The reason I am so bummed about this because this is a really, really good cushion! It’s fairly sheer, which I like (I would say that on one quick layer, it had about 3-4x as much coverage as Glossier’s Skin Tint.. which sounds like a lot, but that stuff is almost invisible tbh), and it’s buildable to almost medium coverage. The finish on this cushion is also better than a lot of others I’ve tried.. some go right past “dewy” and right into “hi, my forehead as a mirror,” but this had a nice, satiny, lightly dewy finish. It also made my skin look smooth and poreless, and lasted all day (though I had to powder a bit at the end of hotter days). It’s also nice to have spf 40 and a list of ingredients that would be impressive if they were in a good skincare item. I mean, it genuinely improved my skin with wear, instead of breaking me out.

Just like.. yeah.. it’s a huge bummer that not everyone can wear it. That’s basically the only reason why I have not and will not repurchased it.

title: Wax On, Wax Off, Hair Still There
text:
I think a lot of us want an easier way to remove hair. Shaving, especially for a bigger girl like me, is not that easy. It’s worse when you have long legs, short arms.

It’s bad when you have certain chin hairs (thankfully not that much it isn’t manageable another way).

I tried some sugar wax kit back about 20+ years ago. That was a NIGHTMARE! It was supposedly edible. I think you microwaved the container, spread it on, let it cool, used a paper strip (supplied) to remove the hair. It didn’t work and stung.

I then moved to a hair removal cream, that partially worked.

After that? Back to the hold stand-by –> shave foam/cream and a razor. For my main body parts, that’s always worked. Tough “chin” hairs –> using a tweezer work. No, the dermaplaning tool didn’t work on them.

I got a wax warmer, so I thought all beads/beans were equal.

These came with ZERO instructions, and the after spray bottle was busted. The warmer kit at least had some. And, my warmer kit had specially made, disposable “cups”.

These beads/beans, in a smaller cup, took over 90 minute to melt. And, the warmer was on 180°(F).

I tried a small amount on my arm. The wax was sticky, not liquidy, and it cooled almost as soon as it hit my skin.

I let it sit there for a few minutes (over 5), and peeled the max off. It didn’t hurt, sting, or cause redness – then again …

THE HAIR WAS STILL THERE

Okay, so my hair on my arm is a little thin. But, if this removes thick hair, shouldn’t it remove thinner hair?

I found another patch, got some warm wax – tried it again. Nope. Tried legs, arms, and under my chin. Nothing. Then again, I see I'm not the only one experiencing issues with these beads/beans.

I may have gotten a bad batch. But, I definitely wouldn’t get these again.
These are 'okay' brushes. I wouldn't recommend unless you're just starting out. They are great for practice.

LES ENFANTS is French for CHILDREN

It doesn’t refer to infants or toddlers. For those who don’t know, a quick note …

Newborn – birth to 4 weeks
Infants – 4 weeks to 1 year
Toddler – 1-3
Preschooler – 3-5
Child – 6-13

That said …

It does state NOT TO SPRAY IT ON A BABY’S SKIN. “Applying gently on clothes” is the preferred method. Though to be honest, I’d say this is more for ages 6+

title: Not sure about daily wear but for ponytails and buns....
text: Nice & soft. Looks identical to my hair texture which is fine, very wavy and curly. I don’t wear daily. Only purchased to put my hair in a ponytail or two buns...I’ve probably used on over 20 occasions and still looks great. I did purchase new and  longer hair for when I have to step it up...so I’m wearing this hair now just to run errands etc...def gets the job done in the way I’m using. Not sure how it would hold up wearing in a weave style daily. My guess we would maybe 30 days...maybe 60 depending on the level of maintenance u do.  All I do is spray a small amount of water and comb throw wide tooth comb 🤷🏽‍♀️ Probably will require more care if you are not removing daily
